Seeing as this question and other things regarding the URM gets asked fairly often on here, I figured I may as well put together a FAQ post that may prove helpful that I can refer others to in the future:

What is URM?

URM, or the Universal Ren’py Mod, is a helpful tool that allows you to view or manipulate variables and scenes in games using the Ren'py engine in real time. Essentially, it works the same as a save editor. It will save you valuable time, should you ever have need of it.

Where can I get URM?

You can get URM from either this link or in Bingoogus's signature. The download is quick and easy to install.

Where do I extract URM to use in Lessons in Love?

You should see an RPA file inside your URM download. You want to drop it inside the 'game' folder of your LiL directory, like so:

View attachment 4139622

Open the game and your URM will be up and running with Lessons in Love.

Why use URM for Lessons in Love?

Reason #1 - Skips Affection Point Grind

Okay, so… you’re aware of the affection and lust point system, correct? And how you have to waste an entire in-game day to get maybe one affection point per girl? Or even worse, how certain girls are locked to certain days and times during the week?

The URM says ‘fuck that’ and lets you skip all that pointless grind! This will save you countless real life hours that would otherwise be spent clicking through menus and holding down your CTRL key.

Exhibit A - You've started a new game, gotten past the first bit of the story, and now you come to your first sandbox section. You think Ami is cute, and you want to tackle her first. Utilizing your trusty Guide Mod, you open up the Hint Menu and see that Ami's events currently look like this:

View attachment 4139065

Note that Ami has 1 affection point, and needs 4 more to reach her first dorm event. True, you can play her other two events first to get 2 affection points organically, but trust me, the game is far less kind with the affection point system later on, especially post Chapter 2.

So okay, what can you do for the two remaining affection points? Talk to Ami and waste a day? Pftt... No. You have the URM.

Press Alt+M to open up the URM menu, and immediately you should see a search bar. Since we're using Ami as an example, type in 'ami_love', then search. It should look like this:

View attachment 4139037

It should be self explanatory what to do from here. Ami has 1 affection point. Simply click on it and edit to your heart's content! Just... maybe don't go overboard. You wouldn't want to break the game. Just use your judgement and you should be fine.

View attachment 4139038 View attachment 4139039

Ami's affection points are now set to 5 with absolutely zero grinding!

View attachment 4139066

And now you can freely access Ami's first dorm event if you so choose. Pretty useful, wouldn't you say?

By the way, you can do this with Lust Points too, when they become relevant. Simply replace 'love' in the variable with 'lust'. To use Ami again, type 'ami_lust', then search.

View attachment 4139040

You can do any of this with any character, so enjoy having a grind free experience.

Reason #2 - Allows You To Unlock Scenes/Events You Missed

Oh no! Looks like you made the wrong decision and now you missed an entire event in the game! Looks like you’re screwed unless you find another save or start the entire game over…

…is what I would say if the URM didn’t exist.

Let’s use a commonly missed event as an example: Rin’s “I Died With You” event from all the way back in Chapter 1:

View attachment 4139338

Well first of all, how did you miss it in the first place? What exactly happened? Here's a helpful bonus tip: there's an amazing wiki for this game that can really come in clutch when you need a quick refresher or tip on what to do. Except for the Reset Puzzles, but I'll get to that...

Anyway, regarding this Rin event, simply go to the Wiki, like so:

View attachment 4139217

Utilizing the nifty little search bar in the top right corner, type in the name of the event that you're missing. Or in this particular example, "I Died With You".

View attachment 4139218

Once on the event of your choosing, it's as simple as scrolling down and seeing why exactly you missed out on the event in the first place.

View attachment 4139219

Welp, looks like you were a Bad Homie to Rin... You kissed Chika before the Beach Vacation despite Rin telling you not to, didn't you? You scoundrel...

But that doesn't matter! Because with the URM, we can undo that mistake, and it will be as if it never happened! After all, who wants to beg for a save or play through the entire game all over again because of one mistake?

So how do you undo this mistake? Well, there's a helpful section on the wiki that can help with this too.

Scroll up until you see the section titled 'Technical Information'.

View attachment 4139220

Click on it and you should see another section titled 'Event Script Name'. That is our ticket to unlocking missed scenes in URM right there, and precisely what we need to type into our search bar.

View attachment 4139221

'cafe35'. Got it. Let's go back to the game and open URM.

View attachment 4139340

Right away, you'll see the variable is set to 'False', meaning that it never happened. To circumvent this, set it to 'True'.

View attachment 4139345

That should be it, right? Mission accomplished! Well, hold on... We still betrayed Rin, and technically shouldn't have this event to begin with because of it. What do we do about that? There's a variable for this too, which the game keeps track of.

Go back to your search bar and type in 'rinbetrayed'.

View attachment 4139343

Unlike the last one, this variable will be set to 'True', since, yes... we did betray Rin in this particular example. Simply set it to False.

View attachment 4139344

Congratulations! The once locked/missed Rin event will now be unlocked and fully accessible via the in-game replayer. Pretty useful, right?

View attachment 4139339

Reason #3 - Ability to replay one-time-only scenes.

You may be asking... 'well, what the hell is a one-time-only scene?', and to that I say... let me explain.

Scenes you see throughout the game like this:

View attachment 4139382

Event Name: "The Cracking of the Egg (Nothing is Beautiful)" (Chapter 3 Main Event)

This:

View attachment 4139383

Event Name: "Flowerchild" (Chapter 3 Main Event)

And also this:

View attachment 4139384

Event Name: "Flora" (Chapter 4 Nao-chan Event)

These are all moments that you will witness once on your first playthrough of the game, and never again. You can't see them in the in-game replayer, because the event cuts off before it ever reaches these moments. No seriously, go to the in-game replayer and try it for yourself. I have the events listed. None of these moments in the above screenshots will show up.

It can be quite annoying, especially if you're hunting for a particular piece of dialogue, a screenshot, or just want to watch the scene again for yourself.

Well, with the URM, you can! It's rather simple, actually.

I think I'll use the event with Himawari as the example this time, so Chapter 3's "Flowerchild" Main Event.

First, press Alt+M to open up your URM menu.

View attachment 4139438

More likely than not, it should say 'variable names' beside your search bar. This is perfect for when we want to mess with affection points and other variables in the game, but not what we want in this particular situation.

Click on 'variable names' and a new menu should pop up:

View attachment 4139439

'Labels/Scenes' is what we're looking for, so go ahead and click that. It should look like this once you do:

View attachment 4139440

Okay good. We're ready to search. So... how do we find the event?

If you read my second reasoning for 'Why use URM for LiL?', then you're already familiar with using the Lessons in Love Wiki to locate script names for situations like this.

View attachment 4139477

'beachwars18' is what we're looking for. Let's search it up.

View attachment 4139441

From here, your instinct may be to click 'Play'. Don't do this.

Instead, click 'Jump'. What this will do is jump you straight to that point in the game's script, as if you were viewing the event for the first time.

With that in mind, do not save when doing this! Simply leave your saves alone, follow the steps I have given you, view the scene, then load back to your own save once you're done. You don't want to accidentally break something, so caution is advised.

View attachment 4139442

Once you're ready, jump to the event and profit! The missing moments will be there once again for you to view whenever you want.

View attachment 4139434

Good question, Himawari. I think we've learned that the URM is well worth it. So try it.

Reason #4 - You can skip Reset Puzzles.

Now look, I don't have a problem with the Reset Puzzles personally speaking. I enjoy them in my own way. But I can see why other people wouldn't. The wiki isn't exactly helpful on giving you hints on what to do in them, and neither is Selebus, so... Yeah, it's understandable.

Luckily for all you haters of the Reset Puzzles, URM allows you to completely skip them! It takes like five seconds.

Let's use the most recent puzzle, "SENSEI-QUEST", as our example:

Step One: once at the Puzzle, wait for the choice menu to pop up and look for a URM prompt in the top left corner of the screen.

View attachment 4139531

Step two: Click the prompt and look for the end label.

View attachment 4139533

Step three: Click Select to jump to the end label. You're done! You made it to the end. Congrats! You used URM to skip the Reset Puzzle.

View attachment 4139534 View attachment 4139535

Commonly Used Variables:

[charactername]_love = A given character's affection point total. EX: yumi_love

[charactername]_lust = A given character's lust point total. EX: chika_lust

rinbetrayed = Is affected depending on if you saw Chika's "Schadenfreude" event in Chapter 1 before the "What's Done is Done" Main Event (start of the first Beach Vacation). If this variable is True, you are considered a Bad Homie and will miss certain events. If this variable is False, you didn't betray Rin and are a Good Homie. No events will be missed.

You will miss countless events over the course of the game if you reject Ami, so this is not recommended. If this variable is True, you accepted Ami's advances and actively pursued her, putting you on the Bad Uncle Route, which ironically seems to be better in every way. No events will be missed on the Bad Uncle route.

URM, or the Universal Ren’py Mod, is a helpful tool that allows you to view or manipulate variables and scenes in games using the Ren'py engine in real time. Essentially, it works the same as a save editor. It will save you valuable time, should you ever have need of it.
Where can I get URM?
You can get URM from either this
link
or in
Bingoogus
's signature. The download is quick and easy to install.
Where do I extract URM to use in Lessons in Love?
You should see an RPA file inside your URM download. You want to drop it inside the 'game' folder of your LiL directory, like so:
Spoiler:
URM Installation Location
View attachment 4139622
Open the game and your URM will be up and running with Lessons in Love.
Why use URM for Lessons in Love?
Reason #1 - Skips Affection Point Grind
Okay, so… you’re aware of the affection and lust point system, correct? And how you have to waste an entire in-game day to get maybe
one
affection point per girl? Or even worse, how certain girls are locked to certain days and times during the week?
The URM says ‘fuck that’ and lets you
skip
all that pointless grind! This will save you
countless
real life hours that would otherwise be spent clicking through menus and holding down your CTRL key.
Spoiler:
Affection Skip Example
Exhibit A - You've started a new game, gotten past the first bit of the story, and now you come to your first sandbox section. You think Ami is cute, and you want to tackle her first. Utilizing your trusty Guide Mod, you open up the Hint Menu and see that Ami's events currently look like this:
View attachment 4139065
Note that Ami has 1 affection point, and needs 4 more to reach her first dorm event. True, you can play her other two events first to get 2 affection points organically, but trust me, the game is far less kind with the affection point system later on, especially post Chapter 2.
So okay, what can you do for the two remaining affection points? Talk to Ami and waste a day? Pftt... No. You have the URM.
Press Alt+M to open up the URM menu, and immediately you should see a search bar. Since we're using Ami as an example, type in 'ami_love', then search. It should look like this:
View attachment 4139037
It should be self explanatory what to do from here. Ami has 1 affection point. Simply click on it and edit to your heart's content! Just... maybe don't go overboard. You wouldn't want to break the game. Just use your judgement and you should be fine.
View attachment 4139038
View attachment 4139039
Ami's affection points are now set to 5 with absolutely zero grinding!
View attachment 4139066
And now you can freely access Ami's first dorm event if you so choose. Pretty useful, wouldn't you say?
By the way, you can do this with Lust Points too, when they become relevant. Simply replace 'love' in the variable with 'lust'. To use Ami again, type 'ami_lust', then search.
View attachment 4139040
You can do any of this with any character, so enjoy having a grind free experience.
Reason #2 - Allows You To Unlock Scenes/Events You Missed
Oh no! Looks like you made the wrong decision and now you missed an entire event in the game! Looks like you’re screwed unless you find another save or start the entire game over…
…is what I
would
say if the URM didn’t exist.
Let’s use a commonly missed event as an example: Rin’s
“I Died With You”
event from all the way back in Chapter 1:
Spoiler:
Rin Event Miss
View attachment 4139338
Well first of all, how did you miss it in the first place? What exactly happened? Here's a helpful bonus tip: there's an
amazing
wiki for this game that can really come in clutch when you need a quick refresher or tip on what to do. Except for the Reset Puzzles, but I'll get to that...
Spoiler:
Unlock Missed Scenes Guide
Anyway, regarding this Rin event, simply go to the
Wiki
, like so:
View attachment 4139217
Utilizing the nifty little search bar in the top right corner, type in the name of the event that you're missing. Or in this particular example,
"I Died With You"
.
View attachment 4139218
Once on the event of your choosing, it's as simple as scrolling down and seeing why exactly you missed out on the event in the first place.
View attachment 4139219
Welp, looks like you were a Bad Homie to Rin... You kissed Chika before the Beach Vacation despite Rin telling you not to, didn't you? You scoundrel...
But that doesn't matter! Because with the URM, we can undo that mistake, and it will be as if it never happened! After all, who wants to beg for a save or play through the entire game all over again because of one mistake?
So how do you undo this mistake? Well, there's a helpful section on the wiki that can help with this too.
Scroll up until you see the section titled 'Technical Information'.
View attachment 4139220
Click on it and you should see another section titled 'Event Script Name'.
That
is our ticket to unlocking missed scenes in URM right there, and precisely what we need to type into our search bar.
View attachment 4139221
'cafe35'. Got it. Let's go back to the game and open URM.
View attachment 4139340
Right away, you'll see the variable is set to 'False', meaning that it never happened. To circumvent this, set it to 'True'.
View attachment 4139345
That should be it, right? Mission accomplished! Well, hold on... We still betrayed Rin, and technically shouldn't have this event to begin with because of it. What do we do about that? There's a variable for this too, which the game keeps track of.
Go back to your search bar and type in 'rinbetrayed'.
View attachment 4139343
Unlike the last one, this variable will be set to 'True', since, yes... we did betray Rin in this particular example. Simply set it to False.
View attachment 4139344
Congratulations! The once locked/missed Rin event will now be unlocked and fully accessible via the in-game replayer. Pretty useful, right?
View attachment 4139339
Reason #3 - Ability to replay one-time-only scenes.
You may be asking... 'well, what the hell is a one-time-only scene?', and to
that
I say... let me explain.
Scenes you see throughout the game like this:
Spoiler
View attachment 4139382
Event Name:
"The Cracking of the Egg (Nothing is Beautiful)"
(Chapter 3 Main Event)
This:
Spoiler
View attachment 4139383
Event Name:
"Flowerchild"
(Chapter 3 Main Event)
And also this:
Spoiler
View attachment 4139384
Event Name:
"Flora"
(Chapter 4 Nao-chan Event)
These are
all
moments that you will witness once on your first playthrough of the game, and never again. You can't see them in the in-game replayer, because the event cuts off before it ever reaches these moments. No seriously, go to the in-game replayer and try it for yourself. I have the events listed. None of these moments in the above screenshots will show up.
It can be quite annoying, especially if you're hunting for a particular piece of dialogue, a screenshot, or just want to watch the scene again for yourself.
Well, with the URM, you
can
! It's rather simple, actually.
I think I'll use the event with Himawari as the example this time, so Chapter 3's
"Flowerchild"
Main Event.
Spoiler:
View One Time Scenes Again!
First, press Alt+M to open up your URM menu.
View attachment 4139438
More likely than not, it should say
'variable names'
beside your search bar. This is perfect for when we want to mess with affection points and other variables in the game, but not what we want in this particular situation.
Click on
'variable names'
and a new menu should pop up:
View attachment 4139439
'Labels/Scenes'
is what we're looking for, so go ahead and click that. It should look like this once you do:
View attachment 4139440
Okay good. We're ready to search. So... how do we find the event?
If you read my second reasoning for 'Why use URM for LiL?', then you're already familiar with using the
Lessons in Love Wiki
to locate script names for situations like this.
View attachment 4139477
'beachwars18'
is what we're looking for. Let's search it up.
View attachment 4139441
From here, your instinct may be to click 'Play'. Don't do this.
Instead, click 'Jump'. What this will do is jump you straight to that point in the game's script, as if you were viewing the event for the first time.
With that in mind,
do not save when doing this!
Simply leave your saves alone, follow the steps I have given you, view the scene, then load back to your own save once you're done. You don't want to accidentally break something, so caution is advised.
View attachment 4139442
Once you're ready, jump to the event and profit! The missing moments will be there once again for you to view whenever you want.
View attachment 4139434
Good question, Himawari. I think we've learned that the URM is well worth it. So try it.
Reason #4 - You can skip Reset Puzzles.
Now look,
I
don't have a problem with the Reset Puzzles personally speaking. I enjoy them in my own way. But I can see why other people wouldn't. The wiki isn't exactly helpful on giving you hints on what to do in them, and neither is Selebus, so... Yeah, it's understandable.
Luckily for all you haters of the Reset Puzzles, URM allows you to completely skip them! It takes like five seconds.
Let's use the most recent puzzle,
"SENSEI-QUEST"
, as our example:
Spoiler:
Reset Puzzle Skip Guide
Step One:
once at the Puzzle, wait for the choice menu to pop up and look for a URM prompt in the top left corner of the screen.
View attachment 4139531
Step two:
Click the prompt and look for the end label.
View attachment 4139533
Step three:
Click Select to jump to the end label. You're done! You made it to the end. Congrats! You used URM to skip the Reset Puzzle.
View attachment 4139534
View attachment 4139535
You may miss out on fun dialogue and Happy Events by doing this, but I mean... hey. You can activate Happy Events with URM as well, so do as you will.
Commonly Used Variables:
[charactername]_love
= A given character's affection point total. EX: yumi_love
[charactername]_lust
= A given character's lust point total. EX: chika_lust
rinbetrayed
= Is affected depending on if you saw Chika's
"Schadenfreude"
event in Chapter 1 before the
"What's Done is Done"
Main Event (start of the first Beach Vacation). If this variable is
True
, you are considered a
Bad Homie
and will
miss
certain events. If this variable is
False
, you didn't betray Rin and are a
Good Homie
. No events will be missed.
amifingered
= Is affected depending on if you accepted or rejected Ami's advances towards you in her
"No One Can See Us"
Chapter 1 Event. If this variable is
False
, you rejected Ami's advances and are on what's considered the
Good Uncle Route
. You will
miss
countless events over the course of the game if you reject Ami, so this is not recommended. If this variable is
True
, you accepted Ami's advances and actively pursued her, putting you on the
Bad Uncle Route
, which ironically seems to be better in every way. No events will be missed on the Bad Uncle route.
*May edit this section a bit more later*

That should be it, right? Mission accomplished! Well, hold on... We still betrayed Rin, and technically shouldn't have this event to begin with because of it. What do we do about that? There's a variable for this too, which the game keeps track of.

Go back to your search bar and type in 'rinbetrayed'.

View attachment 4139343

Unlike the last one, this variable will be set to 'True', since, yes... we did betray Rin in this particular example. Simply set it to False.

View attachment 4139344

Congratulations! The once locked/missed Rin event will now be unlocked and fully accessible via the in-game replayer. Pretty useful, right?

View attachment 4139339

Reason #3 - Ability to replay one-time-only scenes.

Scenes you see throughout the game like this:

View attachment 4139382

Event Name: "The Cracking of the Egg (Nothing is Beautiful)" (Chapter 3 Main Event)

This:

View attachment 4139383

Event Name: "Flowerchild" (Chapter 3 Main Event)

And also this:

View attachment 4139384

Event Name: "Flora" (Chapter 4 Nao-chan Event)

These are all moments that you will witness once on your first playthrough of the game, and never again. I have the events listed. None of these moments in the above screenshots will show up.

I think I'll use the event with Himawari as the example this time, so Chapter 3's "Flowerchild" Main Event.

First, press Alt+M to open up your URM menu.

View attachment 4139438

More likely than not, it should say 'variable names' beside your search bar. This is perfect for when we want to mess with affection points and other variables in the game, but not what we want in this particular situation.

Click on 'variable names' and a new menu should pop up:

View attachment 4139439

'Labels/Scenes' is what we're looking for, so go ahead and click that. It should look like this once you do:

View attachment 4139440

View attachment 4139477

'beachwars18' is what we're looking for. Let's search it up.

View attachment 4139441

So okay, what can you do for the two remaining affection points? Talk to Ami and waste a day? Pftt... No. You have the URM.
Press Alt+M to open up the URM menu, and immediately you should see a search bar. Since we're using Ami as an example, type in 'ami_love', then search. It should look like this:
View attachment 4139037
It should be self explanatory what to do from here. Ami has 1 affection point. Simply click on it and edit to your heart's content! Just... maybe don't go overboard. You wouldn't want to break the game. Just use your judgement and you should be fine.
View attachment 4139038
View attachment 4139039
Ami's affection points are now set to 5 with absolutely zero grinding!
View attachment 4139066
And now you can freely access Ami's first dorm event if you so choose. Pretty useful, wouldn't you say?
By the way, you can do this with Lust Points too, when they become relevant. Simply replace 'love' in the variable with 'lust'. To use Ami again, type 'ami_lust', then search.
View attachment 4139040
You can do any of this with any character, so enjoy having a grind free experience.
Reason #2 - Allows You To Unlock Scenes/Events You Missed
Oh no! Looks like you made the wrong decision and now you missed an entire event in the game! Looks like you’re screwed unless you find another save or start the entire game over…
…is what I
would
say if the URM didn’t exist.
Let’s use a commonly missed event as an example: Rin’s
“I Died With You”
event from all the way back in Chapter 1:
Spoiler:
Rin Event Miss
View attachment 4139338
Well first of all, how did you miss it in the first place? What exactly happened? Here's a helpful bonus tip: there's an
amazing
wiki for this game that can really come in clutch when you need a quick refresher or tip on what to do. Except for the Reset Puzzles, but I'll get to that...
Spoiler:
Unlock Missed Scenes Guide
Anyway, regarding this Rin event, simply go to the
Wiki
, like so:
View attachment 4139217
Utilizing the nifty little search bar in the top right corner, type in the name of the event that you're missing. Or in this particular example,
"I Died With You"
.
View attachment 4139218
Once on the event of your choosing, it's as simple as scrolling down and seeing why exactly you missed out on the event in the first place.
View attachment 4139219
Welp, looks like you were a Bad Homie to Rin... You kissed Chika before the Beach Vacation despite Rin telling you not to, didn't you? You scoundrel...
But that doesn't matter! Because with the URM, we can undo that mistake, and it will be as if it never happened! After all, who wants to beg for a save or play through the entire game all over again because of one mistake?
So how do you undo this mistake? Well, there's a helpful section on the wiki that can help with this too.
Scroll up until you see the section titled 'Technical Information'.
View attachment 4139220
Click on it and you should see another section titled 'Event Script Name'.
That
is our ticket to unlocking missed scenes in URM right there, and precisely what we need to type into our search bar.
View attachment 4139221
'cafe35'. Got it. Let's go back to the game and open URM.
View attachment 4139340
Right away, you'll see the variable is set to 'False', meaning that it never happened. To circumvent this, set it to 'True'.
View attachment 4139345
That should be it, right? Mission accomplished! Well, hold on... We still betrayed Rin, and technically shouldn't have this event to begin with because of it. What do we do about that? There's a variable for this too, which the game keeps track of.
Go back to your search bar and type in 'rinbetrayed'.
View attachment 4139343
Unlike the last one, this variable will be set to 'True', since, yes... we did betray Rin in this particular example. Simply set it to False.
View attachment 4139344
Congratulations! The once locked/missed Rin event will now be unlocked and fully accessible via the in-game replayer. Pretty useful, right?
View attachment 4139339
Reason #3 - Ability to replay one-time-only scenes.
You may be asking... 'well, what the hell is a one-time-only scene?', and to
that
I say... let me explain.
Scenes you see throughout the game like this:
Spoiler
View attachment 4139382
Event Name:
"The Cracking of the Egg (Nothing is Beautiful)"
(Chapter 3 Main Event)
This:
Spoiler
View attachment 4139383
Event Name:
"Flowerchild"
(Chapter 3 Main Event)
And also this:
Spoiler
View attachment 4139384
Event Name:
"Flora"
(Chapter 4 Nao-chan Event)
These are
all
moments that you will witness once on your first playthrough of the game, and never again. You can't see them in the in-game replayer, because the event cuts off before it ever reaches these moments. No seriously, go to the in-game replayer and try it for yourself. I have the events listed. None of these moments in the above screenshots will show up.
It can be quite annoying, especially if you're hunting for a particular piece of dialogue, a screenshot, or just want to watch the scene again for yourself.
Well, with the URM, you
can
! It's rather simple, actually.
I think I'll use the event with Himawari as the example this time, so Chapter 3's
"Flowerchild"
Main Event.
Spoiler:
View One Time Scenes Again!
First, press Alt+M to open up your URM menu.
View attachment 4139438
More likely than not, it should say
'variable names'
beside your search bar. This is perfect for when we want to mess with affection points and other variables in the game, but not what we want in this particular situation.
Click on
'variable names'
and a new menu should pop up:
View attachment 4139439
'Labels/Scenes'
is what we're looking for, so go ahead and click that. It should look like this once you do:
View attachment 4139440
Okay good. We're ready to search. So... how do we find the event?
If you read my second reasoning for 'Why use URM for LiL?', then you're already familiar with using the
Lessons in Love Wiki
to locate script names for situations like this.
View attachment 4139477
'beachwars18'
is what we're looking for. Let's search it up.
View attachment 4139441
From here, your instinct may be to click 'Play'. Don't do this.
Instead, click 'Jump'. What this will do is jump you straight to that point in the game's script, as if you were viewing the event for the first time.
With that in mind,
do not save when doing this!
Simply leave your saves alone, follow the steps I have given you, view the scene, then load back to your own save once you're done. You don't want to accidentally break something, so caution is advised.
View attachment 4139442
Once you're ready, jump to the event and profit! The missing moments will be there once again for you to view whenever you want.
View attachment 4139434
Good question, Himawari. I think we've learned that the URM is well worth it. So try it.
Reason #4 - You can skip Reset Puzzles.
Now look,
I
don't have a problem with the Reset Puzzles personally speaking. I enjoy them in my own way. But I can see why other people wouldn't. The wiki isn't exactly helpful on giving you hints on what to do in them, and neither is Selebus, so... Yeah, it's understandable.
Luckily for all you haters of the Reset Puzzles, URM allows you to completely skip them! It takes like five seconds.
Let's use the most recent puzzle,
"SENSEI-QUEST"
, as our example:
Spoiler:
Reset Puzzle Skip Guide
Step One:
once at the Puzzle, wait for the choice menu to pop up and look for a URM prompt in the top left corner of the screen.
View attachment 4139531
Step two:
Click the prompt and look for the end label.
View attachment 4139533
Step three:
Click Select to jump to the end label. You're done! You made it to the end. Congrats! You used URM to skip the Reset Puzzle.
View attachment 4139534
View attachment 4139535
You may miss out on fun dialogue and Happy Events by doing this, but I mean... hey. You can activate Happy Events with URM as well, so do as you will.
Commonly Used Variables:
[charactername]_love
= A given character's affection point total. EX: yumi_love
[charactername]_lust
= A given character's lust point total. EX: chika_lust
rinbetrayed
= Is affected depending on if you saw Chika's
"Schadenfreude"
event in Chapter 1 before the
"What's Done is Done"
Main Event (start of the first Beach Vacation). If this variable is
True
, you are considered a
Bad Homie
and will
miss
certain events. If this variable is
False
, you didn't betray Rin and are a
Good Homie
. No events will be missed.
amifingered
= Is affected depending on if you accepted or rejected Ami's advances towards you in her
"No One Can See Us"
Chapter 1 Event. If this variable is
False
, you rejected Ami's advances and are on what's considered the
Good Uncle Route
. You will
miss
countless events over the course of the game if you reject Ami, so this is not recommended. If this variable is
True
, you accepted Ami's advances and actively pursued her, putting you on the
Bad Uncle Route
, which ironically seems to be better in every way. No events will be missed on the Bad Uncle route.

GSwole said:
Funny to think the man who writes out a schizophrenic character can't play with you the same way you play my game.
Click to expand...
I think I may have given off the wrong impression (or not, I will admit your implication here is hard to parse. I will assume you mean that as LiL is a representation of your mindscape we get to play with your mind whereas here I am refusing to be in your perception so as to not be "played with" by you which is unfair and one-sided). As it stands, the problem for me is that upon being observed I end up wanting to influence you. All of my posts when I'm aware of you observing me are an attempt to influence you to do something in the game - wearing different masks to inspire different responses. And as a reader I should not be trying to influence the author like that. We're here to read your work, not write our own works. My last post on the discord was trying a very overt move to influence you to potentially shift the direction of the meta plot I perceived as occurring within the work. Which is to say chastise you for revealing the extremely dumb-sounding intention for Ayane's beach scene to be a commentary on lust values in game and that the player has agency for simply not turning the game off - I felt like the western obsession for postmodern meta commentary was unduly corrupting your otherwise noble values of secondary belief. But that's downright embarrassing of me so I immediately had to leave. It's not my position to do so and it's embarrassing to imagine any post on discord would impact anything so significance. My nature is to be a corrupting influence for the worse and I don't want the media I'm engaging with to be worse or just copies of what I think is best (unlike some individuals). Of course, you are very mentally resilient and aware, so I don't think any real corruption occurred. But I don't like the fact I'm trying, and I don't get the impression you welcome this kind of thing, either. LiL is better off uninfluenced by me. Although it's intriguing to imagine a world in which you actually WANT people like me playing stupid mind games with you so you can talk circles around them. Or a world where you actually want users to corrupt your goals as part of the meta plot (which there is more than ample room for and actually kind of what I was afraid of back then). I have to say that your intentions are so multitudinous that even what may feel obvious to you end up feeling surprisingly opaque from the outside. In terms of you just generically psycho-analyzing and playing with me as form of torment similar to the torment you may feel with people playing your game, I don't mind. I have been through the wringer there. The horror for me only is how I'm writing even now with a small hope inside to inspire a meta comment from a character or a kitchen appliance to reference your f95 sockpuppeting now or something. But maybe that, too, is the horror you want to engender. If so I'd almost offer to rejoin the discord but I would probably be banned there for piracy now (lol) and I STRONGLY doubt you feel any significance towards me whatsoever beyond this brief exchange so instead I prefer to stop posting and keep LiL pure.

そしていつかは
寂しさから手を伸ばし

(there, I wrote something embarrassing in public and now feel tormented, be happy!)

Tbf, Koikatsu character models (such as in LiL) are at least as repetitive as Daz3D models.
In my personal opinion, I don't see a correlation between different game engines and the quality of a game. Whether a dev uses Daz3D models, Koikatsu, Honey Select, AICG, photo-tracing or hand-drawn graphics will just impact the personal visual taste of the player. There's enough good titles using either of those styles. Some of my favorite games are text only even.

The fact that so many popular games are using Daz3D models is probably because it is easier to use/edit existing models than having to create images from scratch (e.g. hand-drawn). I wouldn't even say that there is a lot less Koikatsku or HS games out there though, which are comparable in terms of effort used in character creation. AICG is also not too difficult to use, at least if doesn't have to be perfect, the high quality ones need a lot of work too though (a lot of touching up).

I also find it funny that you bring up the RPGM engine and highlight it positively. This is by far the most archaic engine still in use, probably because the sex game dev slaves in Japan keep pumping out low effort slop in that engine to this day, somehow keeping it relevant.

Tl;dr: You can't derive the quality of a game by the engine or the character creation software used (unless it's very sloppy AICG, I guess) and need to look at them individually.

I am of the opinion that this is a misunderstanding of what Maya Prime explained. Every Akira was Akira, what she meant was that none of the previous Akiras could withstand learning about the past - thus none of them were "her" Akira. The very notion that they broke down upon learning the past is evidence that they were in fact Akira, otherwise they wouldn't meltdown upon revisiting memories of another person.

In that same token, every Maya, actually every character, is the real, and has been the real, person everytime. It's just that they're dragged from the person that was in the very beginning of the first cycle.
To look at it from another angle, consider this picture:


Timeline "A" is what happens before the first cycle, and eveytime the timeline is reset, the person that came from there is used as a template to generate a current character. This process doesn't seem to be perfect, and it will also get some added distorted memories or compulsions from previous timelines, but more or less, that's the base for every single one of them.

Then, we have the timelines from inside the cycles. As you can see, the original template manages to grow and become their own thing up to an extent, that being when they're reset. Usually for Akira that happened by the end of summer, or at most the middle of winter. That person would have been cut short, and a new Akira would have been pulled from timeline A.

What makes our Akira different is that the current timeline, which I'm calling "7" for the sake of explanation, hasn't been cut short yet. Which makes him the Akira (inside of the cycles) that had most time to develop his uniqueness. This doesn't mean that the Akiras from previous timelines were fakes, just that ours has been able to exist for longer - and that could possibly be because he was able to recover more memories than the previous ones.

To me, this seems to be the more plausible explanation at the moment, but there is, of course, the possibility that the others were fakes and just that the evidence at the moment doesn't support that theory as much as it supports this one imo.

I am of the opinion that this is a misunderstanding of what Maya Prime explained. Every Akira was Akira, what she meant was that none of the previous Akiras could withstand learning about the past - thus none of them were "her" Akira. The very notion that they broke down upon learning the past is evidence that they were in fact Akira, otherwise they wouldn't meltdown upon revisiting memories of another person.

In that same token, every Maya, actually every character, is the real, and has been the real, person everytime. It's just that they're dragged from the person that was in the very beginning of the first cycle.
To look at it from another angle, consider this picture:
View attachment 4148875

Timeline "A" is what happens before the first cycle, and eveytime the timeline is reset, the person that came from there is used as a template to generate a current character. This process doesn't seem to be perfect, and it will also get some added distorted memories or compulsions from previous timelines, but more or less, that's the base for every single one of them.

Then, we have the timelines from inside the cycles. As you can see, the original template manages to grow and become their own thing up to an extent, that being when they're reset. Usually for Akira that happened by the end of summer, or at most the middle of winter. That person would have been cut short, and a new Akira would have been pulled from timeline A.

What makes our Akira different is that the current timeline, which I'm calling "7" for the sake of explanation, hasn't been cut short yet. Which makes him the Akira (inside of the cycles) that had most time to develop his uniqueness. This doesn't mean that the Akiras from previous timelines were fakes, just that ours has been able to exist for longer - and that could possibly be because he was able to recover more memories than the previous ones.

To me, this seems to be the more plausible explanation at the moment, but there is, of course, the possibility that the others were fakes and just that the evidence at the moment doesn't support that theory as much as it supports this one imo.

I would like to again make the point that there is no rape in "stomachache", other than the rape that would exist in every student's scene. Furthermore, imo, "stomachache" is one of the best if not the best/worst event in LiL. If ever there was a reason for LiL to delve into the topics it does, it was to have scenes like that. It's painfully realistic, complicated and it makes people feel horrible.
If what happened there was rape, ironically enough, it would probably be easier to go through. As I have written essays about at this point, and some have already reminded us of relevant points, both Io and Akira realise a lot about themselves in that scene. First of all, Io apologises for the way she put things as they ended up leading where they went, and highlights that she was going to do it:

It was her decision. Was she in the middle of an episode? yes. No one in their right mind would say that Akira should have had sex with her then, but if anyone thinks that just one of them was having an episode they didn't pay attention. It was two shells trying desperately to connect to one another in their own ways. Stomachache is so hard to watch because they're both harming the other by emulating what their abuser taught them love is, when what they actually want is to show proper love, they just have no idea how.
I'm not going to go through every detail from both of the variations, but since Akira's intent was obvious insofar as he went through the trauma of emulating Sekai, here's Io's counterpart:


What this tells you is that Io, in the end, does want to have sex. posts.content_html_raw:
Seeing as people are talking about Yumi I guess ill bring this up. The other day while looking through my screenshots I saw something that completely contextualised to me why Yumi seems to care so much about Chinami, or at least why she seems to be so earnest in her interactions with and while playing with Chinami. In hindsight It's quite obvious, so I'm not sure why it didn't click in my mind when I initially played the event its from. I would try to explain it but I figured I would post the progression of screen shots that made it click because it will probably be more effective than whatever I would manage to type up. So if anyone else overlooked it like I did here you go, hopefully it make is click into place for you.






Maybe I was in a particular mood at the time but it legitimately made me start crying after swiping through these and having it click together.
She just wants to give Chinami something that she maybe never had in her own childhood. And in those fleeting moments it shows that underneath the façade she constructed to hide herself from what she fears, that even she might have started to see as her real self is a different person. The person she used to be before pushing everyone away, before becoming the bitch/bully etc. The person that legitimately and whole heartedly loves Chika and Chinami. The person that she can become again if she could only find the strength and support she needs to do so. Her true self.

Am i okay calls Akira Sekai on one happy event, the one at the classroom.
On "how i feel" she does indeed translate his name to Sekai:
Akira has Sekai's shadow on the flashback, but also on some other events. Yasu makes a reference to it on Frankincense, but that also presents a problem because the one that is shown following him there is Shadow Maya:
Or maybe that's Pareidolia, and it's just that all gods take Maya's form. We don't know since shadow Maya never showed up again.

But back to the point, there are many explanations, none of them confirmed. The easiest one is that Akira "became" Sekai, in the sense that she fully groomed him, the most glaring example is during "stomachache". The second is the many variations of the idea that Sekai is inside him, kind of like Pareidolia was. Pareidolia lived in his head, Sekai is his shadow, both being "gods" whose believer is Akira, and they in turn provide him with a service.
To more tinfoil ideas, following the revelation of possibly true sekai in Kyoto, and NAO (xeonon)'s statements, it could be that this story was never about Akira, but rather that TERMINAL23 is Sekai's world = why her name is Sekai (world) in the first place. That would make TERMINAL22 Miu and Yuu's world, TERMINAL23 Sekai and Nozomu's world, and TERMINAL24 Akira's world. This would also be in line with the theory that says that Akira is Yuu's grandson, then making 23 Yuu's sons and daughters world, and Akira's would be the terminal one generation past that.

For a less complicated tinfoil, you could say that TERMINAL23 is Sekai's world and Akira never existed, instead he himself is a forgotten god that was summoned by Sekai. He provided a function as "the boy", and as she died he was left without function. Which then might have led to him summoning Maya, another forgotten god, and he managed to survive by becoming Sekai himself, thus serving another function - now as the predator, or the collector, or most likely as the "SENSEI". Those would be his "legends".
On the Yumi situation, Nodoka explains that when he acts out of his control it's because of the compulsion of having acted that way so many times before. Therefore what we see during "this town has two halves" could just be him replaying what he already did to Yumi so many times prior in previous cycles, rather than a god taking control. Why did he do it the first time I have no idea.

Taking away the why the compulsion happens, then it becomes simpler to explain, as it happens during Stomachache. He simply doesn't know another way to behave and ends up replicating what Sekai did to him onto others.

May or may not be related to these future Maya events, but to me "Wake Up" packs a lot more punches than the already very foreboding "My Story" because of a memorable moment during a reset that happens to have Maya in it.
View attachment 4156878
It was only at this later stage in the game that I realized that a good portion of the in-game gibberish is actually decipherable instead of something resulted from ramming your forehead against the keyboard. Suddenly being able to understand what zdnh xs meant solely by context must've given me an everlasting impression.
Click to expand...
In that specific event Sensei is telling her to wake up in order to escape the nightmare version of the past that she's trapped in during the reset. It's possible the same thing is happening to all of the RAS this time, with each of them having to wake up to return to the "true" timeline.

It's also possible there's a bigger meaning, since "waking up" has been tied to being aware of and/or escaping from the simulation, most obviously by the crying AmIOkay (who might be Maya Prime) in "The Room With Clocks":
Waking up is how Sensei ended up in the clock room in the first place, which is also how Nodoka's book ends.

...
Given Nodoka's end goal is breaking out of the cycles, she could be suggesting that's how it will eventually happen. Or it could just be how every meta-cycle ends when Sensei gets reset.

In the last update, Sekai told Tsuneyo that her event was a dream inside of a dream inside of a dream.
I presume that makes Kumon-mi/Terminal 22 the second level of the dream, and since Sensei ends up in the room with clocks when he wakes from that, possibly the room with clocks is the original dream.

This isn't a literal dream in the sense that everything is happening in Akira's head, as Selebus has made clear through his spokes-Himawari.
I would guess that the act of dreaming is referring to the creation of the simulated world, which is then somehow inhabited by real people.

One more interesting conversation about sleeping/waking comes from Maya herself in "Past/Present/Future":
It's pretty clear she's not talking about literal sleep, but rather something having to do with the cycles. Maybe she's suggesting that it doesn't matter if she's awake, i.e. aware of the nature of the "dream", because it only matters whether Akira himself is able to wake up - he's the dreamer who has the made the world real, and only by waking up and perceiving it's true nature can he end the illusion.

Side note: Maya uses the phrases "perfect harmony" here, and the voice in "Perfect Harmony" that talks about redacting the beach events and tells Akira to "embrace this perfect harmony" is the one that's been used in the past for Maya and AmIOkay. I wonder if this is indicating a connection between Maya and the narrator from the beach trip. I have a suspicion that "My Story" is going to be about that narrator, not the Maya in Kumon-mi. It's probably a coincidence, but that could also fit with the next Maya event "Right as Rain" since the narrator said that it's always raining where they're from.

posts.content_html_raw:
The current state of affairs really leaves some interesting conundrums for our "heroes" doesn't it

In the case of Frog Boy and Nerd Girl, they are all the way back to the very first Halloween This is interesting because this before things got really messy for Akira, which makes one wonder if he wouldn't be tempted to try to "fix" the things he feels he "broke" in the original timeline and just stay where he is. Maybe now he can set Chika straight before she goes off the deep end, maybe he can not break Miku's vagina this time, maybe he can start being a father to Ami a little earlier and spare her from the psychotic break and subsequent ostracization as a result. Maybe he could not completely destroy his relationship with Karin? Maybe he can convince Rin not to dye her hair blonde? He wouldn't have to be "good", he knows he can't be that. But maybe he can be a little better now that he knows what will happen with some of the decisions he made previously.

In the case of Makoto there are also a few advantages here, as now she is in a position where all her major competition has effectively been removed. She has Sensei completely to herself. Also, her father isn't dead in this timeline yet, assumedly. And even if that were to change it will assuredly be less of a shock the second time. Even if Sensei gathered the nerve to even attempt to find a way back to the prime timeline and to his other lovers, Makoto might not be so inclined to just sit back and let that happen.

Ayane may be all alone in Halloween 2 but what's interesting about that, is that I believe the Sensei she is there with isn't the one we know. It's the one who was only having sex with one girl instead of 15 of them. Ayane, being best girl, has really been putting on a brave face despite the knowledge that she doesn't have Sensei to herself, but that doesn't mean it doesn't bother her. Ayane has been in love with Sensei since forever and it makes you wonder now that she's in this alternate timeline with the same man she loves, albeit less heavily and unrepetently flawed, would she feel the temptation to just take chances where she is instead of going back to the original timeline, if she even can. That said, because she is best girl, we know she will do that right thing, even if it hurts her.

And then there's Maya, not a time lord this time, truly a normal teenage girl. Basically being freed from the nightmare she had just found herself in prior with Niki swooping in and stealing her "boyfriend", while he kicks her to the curb, quite harshly. If Halloween 3 Sensei is also pre-timeloop, memory problems, Sensei, then her relationship with him has effectively been reset and returned to what it was before. However, by Halloween 3 Niki and Noriko have re-entered the picture and should be encroaching on his heart as we speak. Knowing this, what is this normal teenage girl going to do with the vision of the future she has been granted? Now that she knows about Ami and her true feelings about her Uncle/Dad, and the fact that she has CHR 10 and 100 Speech + Cherchez Le Femme when she cuts her hair short, what will happen with their interactions going forward in this resetted timeline?

Though do we really have time to explore all these possibilities when we have so many unanswered questions with the main timeline? Are Futaba's parents dead? Will Chika ever NOT be insane? What evil machinations do the dastardly duo of Ami(Forma de pelo corto) and Maya have in store for Sensei and his idol gf? Is Nodoka gone for good? Who or what is Nao? Will Sensei FINALLY bone Rin? Will Rin finally bone Sensei AND Chika? Will Haruka ever be back in business again? Tsuneyo! What's her deal? So many questions!

inb4 no answers

As you said it doesn't make sense from a storytelling perspective to devide the story between 3 different timelines, while leaving a lot of current plotlines unresolved. But it also wouldn't work logically. Time Travel fiction is of course open to a lot of interpretations, but a concept like the Butterfly Effect is so ingrained in them that I don't see LiL defying it and getting away with it.

If we believe the last scene of 0.44 as it is, then Akira and Makoto were thrown back to Halloween 1, Maya to Halloween 2, and Ayane to Hallowen 3. And all of those time travels happened simultaneously. Makoto and Akira being sent back to the furthest point in time would make enough changes in the timeline just by existing and acting normally, that the situations that will lead to the scenes where Maya and Ayane were thrown back, either will not happen or change significantly.
They could choose to re-enact the next few months exaclty, but not only that's humanly impossible, they have no reason to do that because there's no reason to believe that Ayane will also be sent back in time at some point later. They will just assume she was lost in the reset.

The only way to make this work is to make it so that the Apocalypse Squad were sent to different timelines, where their counterparts were not sent back in time. But there's literally no reason to do that from a storytelling perspective...

So it's better to assume that whatever is happening at the end of last patch is temporary due to the reset, and they will be sent back at some point.

In the case of Frog Boy and Nerd Girl, they are all the way back to the very first Halloween This is interesting because this before things got really messy for Akira, which makes one wonder if he wouldn't be tempted to try to "fix" the things he feels he "broke" in the original timeline and just stay where he is. Maybe now he can set Chika straight before she goes off the deep end, maybe he can not break Miku's vagina this time, maybe he can start being a father to Ami a little earlier and spare her from the psychotic break and subsequent ostracization as a result. Maybe he could not completely destroy his relationship with Karin? Maybe he can convince Rin not to dye her hair blonde? He wouldn't have to be "good", he knows he can't be that. But maybe he can be a little better now that he knows what will happen with some of the decisions he made previously.

In the case of Makoto there are also a few advantages here, as now she is in a position where all her major competition has effectively been removed. She has Sensei completely to herself. Also, her father isn't dead in this timeline yet, assumedly. And even if that were to change it will assuredly be less of a shock the second time. Even if Sensei gathered the nerve to even attempt to find a way back to the prime timeline and to his other lovers, Makoto might not be so inclined to just sit back and let that happen.

Ayane may be all alone in Halloween 2 but what's interesting about that, is that I believe the Sensei she is there with isn't the one we know. It's the one who was only having sex with one girl instead of 15 of them. Ayane, being best girl, has really been putting on a brave face despite the knowledge that she doesn't have Sensei to herself, but that doesn't mean it doesn't bother her. Ayane has been in love with Sensei since forever and it makes you wonder now that she's in this alternate timeline with the same man she loves, albeit less heavily and unrepetently flawed, would she feel the temptation to just take chances where she is instead of going back to the original timeline, if she even can. That said, because she is best girl, we know she will do that right thing, even if it hurts her.

And then there's Maya, not a time lord this time, truly a normal teenage girl. Basically being freed from the nightmare she had just found herself in prior with Niki swooping in and stealing her "boyfriend", while he kicks her to the curb, quite harshly. If Halloween 3 Sensei is also pre-timeloop, memory problems, Sensei, then her relationship with him has effectively been reset and returned to what it was before. However, by Halloween 3 Niki and Noriko have re-entered the picture and should be encroaching on his heart as we speak. Knowing this, what is this normal teenage girl going to do with the vision of the future she has been granted? Now that she knows about Ami and her true feelings about her Uncle/Dad, and the fact that she has CHR 10 and 100 Speech + Cherchez Le Femme when she cuts her hair short, what will happen with their interactions going forward in this resetted timeline?

Though do we really have time to explore all these possibilities when we have so many unanswered questions with the main timeline? Are Futaba's parents dead? Will Chika ever NOT be insane? What evil machinations do the dastardly duo of Ami(Forma de pelo corto) and Maya have in store for Sensei and his idol gf? Is Nodoka gone for good? Who or what is Nao? Will Sensei FINALLY bone Rin? Will Rin finally bone Sensei AND Chika? Will Haruka ever be back in business again? Tsuneyo! What's her deal? So many questions!

spoilers.title: Butterfly Effect
spoilers.html:
If we believe the last scene of 0.44 as it is, then Akira and Makoto were thrown back to Halloween 1, Maya to Halloween 2, and Ayane to Hallowen 3. And all of those time travels happened simultaneously. Makoto and Akira being sent back to the furthest point in time would make enough changes in the timeline just by existing and acting normally, that the situations that will lead to the scenes where Maya and Ayane were thrown back, either will not happen or change significantly.
They could choose to re-enact the next few months exaclty, but not only that's humanly impossible, they have no reason to do that because there's no reason to believe that Ayane will also be sent back in time at some point later. They will just assume she was lost in the reset.

The only way to make this work is to make it so that the Apocalypse Squad were sent to different timelines, where their counterparts were not sent back in time. But there's literally no reason to do that from a storytelling perspective...

Technically, there may be 2 Maya Primes, in these Alt Timelines. Sensei and Makoto may have one, and considering the Maya in Ayane's timeline seemed to notice something was off with her, she might be a Maya Prime as well. We don't actually know who is or isn't "aware" in these timelines, or why they in particular were chosen.

It's likely that being in these timelines won't last, though, and they'll return to the main timeline, after experiencing whatever they are intended to. The supernatural stuff love their little trials and tribulations, it seems. Still, chances are, the characters won't be quite the same after this. Probably a bit more traumatized.

As for most of those questions: We'll have to wait and see.

However, I do think Nao may be behind this Reset or at least involved. The Xoanon (Nao) was at least waiting for this Reset, and Ami taking care of Sensei seemed to have inspired it:
Narrator/Auto-Pilot - "These good deeds of hers, hidden behind closed doors, would only be witnessed through the eyes of her uncle and the gods that watch over the Wishing Well."
- "Throughout the course of this story, you have decided who some of those gods are. But you have made those decisions based on what you believe you know rather than what is actually true."
- "In a place far from here, the Xoanon plucks a body from the water, drying it off with a towel made of sheepskin, before scribbling something down in a notebook."
- "It writes the following-"
- "'Blessed be those who live to protect. Who live selflessly, helplessly, and full of regret.'"
- "'What is it they long for? Why can't they forget?'"
- "Then it puts its pen down and awaits the next reset."
(Chapter 4 Ami 'The Caretaker' Event)
Nao being the Xoanon and in the Wishing Well was revealed back in Chapter 3's 'Mother's Milk' Happy Event:
Sensei - "Who are you?"
Nao/Ima/The Xoanon - "The xoanon --- the one who holds the strings yet neglects to tighten them."
- "Here as in a vast collection of universes known only as the Wishing Well --- where all information created by man is chronicled and protected by those who created him."
- "You may call me a guardian angel if you like, but I prefer the name 'Nao.'"

What exactly is going to happen, is anyone's guess, but it may be Ami centered, and Nao may be behind it.

Nao and The World/Sekai(?) are also probably still looking forward to Sensei realizing how powerless he is:
Nao - "I hope you realized how powerless you are."
- "And how excited we are to watch the further realization of that come to light."

This is a puzzle that plays like an adventure game. You have to grind currency until you have enough money to get all the items on both shops, to then go on to defeat a number of bosses and clear the puzzle.

First thing is the currency, don't bother fighting the enemies on Fields of Despair. Instead do this, open URM and search for:

now change it to a ridiculous amount:

View attachment 4090590
Now that you have everything, let's go to field of regrets for the one actual relevant thing here:
View attachment 4090591
go to the suit guy (you don't really have to do this to clear the puzzle) but it's the one interesting bit here. After going through that once we can move on.

Now let's go in the order they appear:

Noriko
Noriko is the epitome of reliability. Her unwavering dedication and work ethic make her a pillar of strength. She is the rock that others lean on in times of turmoil, showcasing an unyielding resolve to see things through to the end. This steadfastness is both her greatest strength and her most significant limitation. While her dependability is admirable, it also means she rarely steps out of her comfort zone, leading to predictable behavior that can sometimes be perceived as dull or uninspired. Noriko's character arcs often center around her ability to persevere, but this can come at the expense of personal growth and spontaneity.

Her interactions with other characters are usually marked by a sense of duty and responsibility. She is the one to pick up the pieces when things go wrong, always ready with a solution or a helping hand. However, this can make her seem more like a narrative device than a fully realized character. Her role is to support and stabilize, but this often leaves little room for her own emotional development. Noriko’s predictability can make her feel static, especially in a story teeming with dynamic characters who evolve and surprise the audience.Her steadiness is a double-edged sword; while it ensures she is always there when needed, it also means she seldom experiences the transformative arcs that make other characters more memorable. Noriko's strength lies in her ability to remain a constant, but this very trait can also make her fade into the background of more adventurous and unpredictable characters.

Kaori
Kaori captivates with her enigmatic charm. Her talent for humor is undeniable, and she often serves as an inspiration to those around her. Kaori's comedy is not just a skill but a defining aspect of her identity, making her stand out as a character of intelligence and wit. However, her focus on cock can sometimes create a barrier, distancing her from deeper emotional connections and making her seem somewhat aloof. Her struggles and triumphs in her journey are compelling, yet they can overshadow her personal growth, leaving her character feeling one-dimensional.

Kaori’s interactions with other characters are often marked by admiration and a sense of bafflement. She is the muse, the unattainable ideal that others aspire to emulate. This pedestal, while flattering, can also isolate her, making it difficult for her to connect on a more personal level. Her character is frequently defined by her naivety and the mystique surrounding it, which can overshadow other facets of her personality. The focus on her naivety, while engaging, often leaves little room for exploring her vulnerabilities and personal struggles outside it.

Despite these challenges, Kaori’s presence enriches the narrative. However, to truly resonate as best girl, Kaori would need to transcend her role as an enigmatic clown and reveal more of her inner self. Her wit is remarkable, but it is the exploration of her vulnerabilities and personal growth that could elevate her character to new heights.

Ayane
Ayane brings an electrifying energy to the narrative with her vibrant personality and boundless enthusiasm. She is the life of the party, injecting a sense of fun and excitement wherever she goes. Ayane’s impulsive nature and zest for life make her a captivating presence, but they can also lead to reckless behavior and unpredictable outcomes. Her character is marked by a dynamic spontaneity that keeps the audience on their toes, but this same trait can sometimes overshadow deeper emotional arcs and character development.

Her interactions are filled with charisma and a contagious energy that draws others in. Ayane's ability to light up a room is unmatched, making her a beloved character among her peers. However, her impulsiveness can also lead to complications and conflicts, highlighting a need for greater balance in her character. While her energetic nature is endearing, it can sometimes come across as overbearing, overshadowing moments of introspection and growth. Ayane’s charm is undeniable, but her journey often focuses more on her external actions than her internal evolution.

Despite these challenges, Ayane’s presence is essential for infusing the narrative with a sense of vitality and excitement. She brings a refreshing contrast to more serious characters, adding a layer of unpredictability that keeps the story engaging. To truly shine as best girl, Ayane would benefit from a deeper exploration of her inner world, revealing the complexities behind her vibrant exterior. Her chaotic charisma is a double-edged sword, providing both entertainment and an opportunity for profound character growth.

Ami: The Quintessential Best Girl
Ami stands out as the quintessential best girl, embodying a perfect blend of wit, charm, and emotional depth. Her intelligence and sense of humor make her a relatable and engaging character, while her vulnerability adds layers of complexity to her personality. Ami’s journey is one of self-discovery, resilience, and growth, offering a rich tapestry of experiences that captivate and inspire. Unlike Noriko, Kaori, and Ayane, Ami's character is defined not just by her strengths but by her ability to navigate her shortcomings and transform them into sources of strength in the race to win Sensei's heart.

Her interactions with Akira are marked by genuine warmth and insight, making her a standout character in every scene. Ami challenges Akira and the audience, encouraging them to grow and evolve alongside her. Her ability to balance insanity and incest, humor and seriousness, makes her a well-rounded character whose impact lingers long after the story concludes. Ami's multifaceted personality ensures that she is not just a source of support or inspiration but a dynamic force that drives the narrative forward.

In conclusion, while Noriko, Kaori, and Ayane each bring unique elements to the table, Ami encapsulates the essence of a truly great character. Her ability to connect on multiple levels, coupled with her dynamic growth and emotional depth, makes her the definitive best girl. Ami’s journey is a testament to the power of nuanced character writing, proving that the best girl is more than just a title—it’s a testament to the profound impact a well-crafted character can have on a story.

First, congrats on finally being able to post screenshots

My take on these is very meta and again unassuming: while A House Near a Lake shows a clear effort in referencing or intentionally replicating a past event (from both Sensei's and viewers' perspectives), Everything is Connected on the other hand gives me the feeling of only for showing the viewers that Saki exists in the same universe: an excuse for lore dumping if you would. As in, the rest of the elements in Everything is Connected are pretty close to non-factors and cannot withstand interrogation.

For example, Nao demonstrates a clear understanding of both her action and her intention (i.e., what will happen if Sensei goes into the doll house, what is inside the doll house, why does she want Sensei to go in, etc). Sensei gets to challenge what Nao knows afterwards, and this consequently fortifies "how real/accountable" this encounter is. However, the same thing cannot be said for Maya or any other character's potential partaking in Everything is Connected. There is no rhyme or reason or aftermath of what's transpired. Sensei never asked and Maya never confided. The sole takeaway is "Now viewers know Saki exists in the same universe" (like from the looks of it I am not even sure if Sensei remembered the first time he went to terminal 22 at all)

I am also reluctant to think about the possibility Himawari's participation if the sole reason to go off is that sunflower next to Maya. There are so many sunflower placements in so many events that lack both any worthwhile meaning or any separate piece of evidence that can prove the connection of "this particular sunflower" to Himawari. It creates so much false positive if we were to scream "Ah! My shapeshifting daughter!" every time we see a sunflower.

tldr is that any resemblance you see in A House Near a Lake is not about functionality, but a deliberate setup to ring Sensei's bell. Meanwhile, how Everything is Connected is crafted has no sense in it at all.

Finally, my slight grilling at Selly is that how could A House Near a Lake doesn't have path deviation if Everything is Connected is skippable? Sloppy!

For example, Nao demonstrates a clear understanding of both her action and her intention (i.e., what will happen if Sensei goes into the doll house, what is inside the doll house, why does she want Sensei to go in, etc). Sensei gets to challenge what Nao knows afterwards, and this consequently fortifies "how real" this encounter is. However, the same thing cannot be said for Maya or any other character's potential partaking in Everything is Connected. There is no rhyme or reason or aftermath of what's transpired. Sensei never asked and Maya never confided. The sole takeaway is "Now viewers know Saki exists in the same universe" (like from the looks of it I am not even sure if Sensei remembered the first time he went to terminal 22 at all)

I am also reluctant to think about the possibility Himawari's participation if the sole reason to go off is that sunflower next to Maya. There are so many sunflower placements in so many events that lack both any worthwhile meaning or any separate piece of evidence that can prove the connection of "this particular sunflower" to Himawari. It creates so much false positive if we were to scream "Ah! My shapeshifting daughter!" every time we see a sunflower.

tldr is that any resemblance you see in A House Near a Lake is not about functionality, but a deliberate setup to ring Sensei's bell. Meanwhile, how Everything is Connected is crafted has no sense in it at all.

Finally, my slight grilling at Selly is that how could A House Near a Lake doesn't have path deviation if Everything is Connected is skippable? Sloppy!
