My current understanding of how the time loop works, using the point of view of Maya Prime because most of what we know comes from her info :


Soft Resets: Resets as depicted in the game so far. You go back to the beginning of the school year, with most people's memories of the school year still intact. Seasons change every second SR.

Hard Resets: You go back to the beginning of the school year, but this time no memories of previous SRs are carried over (except for some slight deja-vus, varies by characters). The existence of hard resets is confirmed by Maya Prime depicting Senseis as conquering the girls multiple times, which is why they seem so accepting of Akira during the current iteration according to her. This was further confirmed by the narration in the scene between Ami and Maya last patch.

It's currently unknown what triggers a hard reset. Maya Prime implied she did a little something extra during the first SR to make it happen, but it seems it was just something she said to impress Sensei. We already had a SR without her too. Is it always after a certain number of SRs ? Unlikely. It's stated that Akira never "survived past the 3rd reset", so if that was the case, there would have been lots of Akira-less school years, and we would have heard about that from Maya Prime. The answer that makes the most common sense is that it's linked to Sensei's consciousness in some way (Which would imply that the whole phenomenon is related to him). It's unclear, but likely that HRs always start back with summer, considering the normal japanese school year calendar.

It kinda bugged me that the start of the game does not correspond to how resets work later. Everyone thinks of Akira as an upstanding teacher, and Maya tells us instantly that we've been isekai'd. She knows that something is different about the last reset. I know the common theory is that Akira offed himself last time, but why does everyone's memory get reset instead of only his ? So I tried to come up with a good explanation.

Anyway, this brings me to the now very common theory that Ami is a secret loop traveler. There's a lot of hints that were given already so I won't go long on that, but one I particularly noticed and I hope was part of the setup, is that Ami supposedly does not immediately remember her Madoka cosplay (from the previous year). It's stated that Ami's favorite thing not named Akira is magical girl anime, so you'd think that would be hard to forget, right ? Unless you had hundred of other halloweens since, that is. (PS: Homura cosplay would fit Maya to a T)

So I tried to come up with a couple theories on why and how that would be the case, I'll name them after another japanese fiction that would resemble them in how they play out :


Ami keeps her memories intact during the resets by going to the 'Box room'.

Cross Channel is a VN among others that inspired Selebus to make LiL, and we could potentially see some plot points borrowed from it in the next patches.

In that game, high schoolers are stuck in a 1-week-long time loop. The interesting parts for us here are :
  1. There's a particular place (a shrine) that prevents both people and physical objects from the effects of the reset.
  2. There's one girl that was pretending to be reset each time, but was secretly a loop traveler by using the shrine.
  3. Less important than the rest, but during one iteration, that girl went psycho and murdered everyone but the MC.
So what if there's a place like the shrine in CC ? Last patch had a scene with Miku and Noriko (edit: initially wrote Nodoka) having a danganronpa moment and finding pictures of themselves that they do not remember taking. There's 3 possibilities here :
  1. Those pictures were taken in the future, and then sent back to the current time.
  2. Those pictures are from the current iteration (between soft resets) but was forgotten by everyone for reasons unknown.
  3. Those pictures are from a previous iteration, where Noriko was also transferred to Akira's class.
Of all these I think the third option is the most likely. It would also go well with Maya Prime's boxes. It would mean the boxes contain evidence of each iteration, and that 'box room' can protect them from the effect of hard resets, which seem to even bring back Akira from the dead and delete all physical proofs of any events that may have happened between soft resets. We already know the roof does not offer those protections, as we saw Ayane being soft reseted before our own eyes.

If such a room exists, it would be natural to think that Ami could use it. I doubt she was sneaking on us on the roof everytime. It's also not hard to pretend to be either hard or soft reset if you know about the symptoms.

Another reason I'd think this could be the case is what Maya told us about Ami in previous iterations. Maya Prime got kinda exposed as fraud lately because of how much she either got wrong or lied about because of her own biases, but what if seeing Ami murder everyone was truthful ? She was, for no clearly stated reason, adamant in not involving Ami in any Apocalypse Squad related matters. What if both knew about each other's knowledge of the loops ? That would be a nice twist isn't it, although I think it would be a big reach. But at least it would explain Ami probing Maya for information in their dorm last patch.

Admittedly there's a lot of problems with this thoery, most notably literally seeing Ami dead in a couple resets, and the whole Maya Prime-Ami dynamic in the first three chapters (if Maya did know about Ami loop traveling).
Ami herself is the cause of the time loop, and thus, can observe each iteration.

If Ami herself is the gamemaster, she doesn't need to do mundane things like go to the roof.

The Empty Box and Zeroth Maria is a great series of LNs which I recommend. The very first volume starts with a similar twist to LiL:
This series is about the MCs solving paranormal incidents. In the first volume, the MCs got stuck as oberserves in a 2-day-long time loop, that occured for thousands of times. You literally start in the 13,118th iteration.

It is stated that except for the observers, only the 'culprit' can perceive the different loops. It turned out it was someone who was repeating time in order to avoid an unfortunate future.

That book resembles LiL more in the fact that the observers can perceive the loops are like that just because. What interests us here is that Ami supposedly knows about the loops without following the rules (going to the roof). What if it's because she's the cause of it ? It's possible that her depicted deaths are her unfortunate future that she is trying to avoid by repeating time. She would also have the most to benefit from it, living endlessly in a closed space with her uncle, although the circumstances of the loop are more favorable to Akira than to her.

I don't know how much foundation there is for this theory to be true. People here who pay more attention to happy scenes, in which she often appears as a monstrosity probably have more to say about this. I think it's less likely to be correct for the simple reason that this sounds like endgame content, and it's stated that the game isn't ending anytime soon.

Or this could be just a gigantic red herring all along, and that would be very cruel.

spoilers.title: Time Loop
spoilers.html:
Soft Resets: Resets as depicted in the game so far. You go back to the beginning of the school year, with most people's memories of the school year still intact. Seasons change every second SR.

Hard Resets: You go back to the beginning of the school year, but this time no memories of previous SRs are carried over (except for some slight deja-vus, varies by characters). The existence of hard resets is confirmed by Maya Prime depicting Senseis as conquering the girls multiple times, which is why they seem so accepting of Akira during the current iteration according to her. This was further confirmed by the narration in the scene between Ami and Maya last patch.

It's currently unknown what triggers a hard reset. Maya Prime implied she did a little something extra during the first SR to make it happen, but it seems it was just something she said to impress Sensei. We already had a SR without her too. Is it always after a certain number of SRs ? Unlikely. It's stated that Akira never "survived past the 3rd reset", so if that was the case, there would have been lots of Akira-less school years, and we would have heard about that from Maya Prime. The answer that makes the most common sense is that it's linked to Sensei's consciousness in some way (Which would imply that the whole phenomenon is related to him). It's unclear, but likely that HRs always start back with summer, considering the normal japanese school year calendar.

spoilers.title: Time Loop
spoilers.html:
View attachment 4168910
Soft Resets: Resets as depicted in the game so far. You go back to the beginning of the school year, with most people's memories of the school year still intact. Seasons change every second SR.

Hard Resets: You go back to the beginning of the school year, but this time no memories of previous SRs are carried over (except for some slight deja-vus, varies by characters). The existence of hard resets is confirmed by Maya Prime depicting Senseis as conquering the girls multiple times, which is why they seem so accepting of Akira during the current iteration according to her. This was further confirmed by the narration in the scene between Ami and Maya last patch.

It's currently unknown what triggers a hard reset. Maya Prime implied she did a little something extra during the first SR to make it happen, but it seems it was just something she said to impress Sensei. We already had a SR without her too. Is it always after a certain number of SRs ? Unlikely. It's stated that Akira never "survived past the 3rd reset", so if that was the case, there would have been lots of Akira-less school years, and we would have heard about that from Maya Prime. The answer that makes the most common sense is that it's linked to Sensei's consciousness in some way (Which would imply that the whole phenomenon is related to him). It's unclear, but likely that HRs always start back with summer, considering the normal japanese school year calendar.

spoilers.title: Cross Channel Theory
spoilers.html:
Ami keeps her memories intact during the resets by going to the 'Box room'.

Cross Channel is a VN among others that inspired Selebus to make LiL, and we could potentially see some plot points borrowed from it in the next patches.

In that game, high schoolers are stuck in a 1-week-long time loop. The interesting parts for us here are :
  1. There's a particular place (a shrine) that prevents both people and physical objects from the effects of the reset.
  2. There's one girl that was pretending to be reset each time, but was secretly a loop traveler by using the shrine.
  3. Less important than the rest, but during one iteration, that girl went psycho and murdered everyone but the MC.
So what if there's a place like the shrine in CC ? Last patch had a scene with Miku and Nodoka having a danganronpa moment and finding pictures of themselves that they do not remember taking. There's 2 possibilities here :
  1. Those pictures were taken in the future, and then sent back to the current time.
  2. Those pictures are from the current iteration (between soft resets) but was forgotten by everyone for reasons unknown.
  3. Those pictures are from a previous iteration, where Nodoka was also transferred to Akira's class.
Of all these I think the third option is the most likely. It would also go well with Maya Prime's boxes. It would mean the boxes contain evidence of each iteration, and that 'box room' can protect them from the effect of hard resets, which seem to even bring back Akira from the dead and delete all physical proofs of any events that may have happened between soft resets. We already know the roof does not offer those protections, as we saw Ayane being soft reseted before our own eyes.

If such a room exists, it would be natural to think that Ami could use it. I doubt she was sneaking on us on the roof everytime. It's also not hard to pretend to be either hard or soft reset if you know about the symptoms.

Another reason I'd think this could be the case is what Maya told us about Ami in previous iterations. Maya Prime got kinda exposed as fraud lately because of how much she either got wrong or lied about because of her own biases, but what if seeing Ami murder everyone was truthful ? She was, for no clearly stated reason, adamant in not involving Ami in any Apocalypse Squad related matters. What if both knew about each other's knowledge of the loops ? That would be a nice twist isn't it, although I think it would be a big reach. But at least it would explain Ami probing Maya for information in their dorm last patch.

Admittedly there's a lot of problems with this thoery, most notably literally seeing Ami dead in a couple resets, and the whole Maya Prime-Ami dynamic in the first three chapters (if Maya did know about Ami loop traveling).

The thing that caused his catatonic state back then?

In anticipation of learning more about Maya's past, here's a theory that I've believed for a while but never got around to writing up:
  • Akira and Maya met before the accident.
  • Sekai knew about Maya, was pushing Akira to groom her, and might have been part of it herself.
I'm fairly confident in the first part. The second part is admittedly very speculative, with one piece of symbolic evidence that I might be massively misreading.
I think the strongest piece of direct evidence is from the audio clip in sleepsong.mp3, which plays for the first time in "Torrential Downpour. Child of Man." Maya's voice describes falling in love with Akira:

"Do you remember the first time we touched hands? It happened on accident on the floor of your bedroom. At first I thought that there was no way you would ever see me in that light. But when all of the other lights burned up and I was still there, I finally understood you were just as broken as me. And I knew then and there that I would fall into you."

So this is the order of events described:
1. Maya and Akira have a non-sexual relationship and touch hands on the floor of his bedroom.
2. Something happens that causes the "other lights" in Akira's life to "burn up", and Maya finds out that he's broken.
3. Sometime later their sexual relationship starts.
For me, #2 has to be describing the accident: Akira's lovers Sekai and Niki (the "other lights") are removed from his life, one by death and one my choice, and he completely breaks for the first time. So that means that #1 happened before the accident.

The fact that #1 happens in his bedroom also suggests that it's pre-accident. After the accident, Akira is living with Ami and never tutors at his house, so there's no reason for Maya to have been there. The tutoring apartment looks like a one room studio apartment, and there's no evidence that Akira ever lived there (certainly not after the accident), so Maya wouldn't refer to that as his bedroom. The only thing that makes sense to me is that Maya visited him at his house (or even lived there) before the accident when Akira was living alone.

There's a few other hints:
  • Ami remembers having a play date with a mystery girl at Akira's house. Since this happened before they lived together, it's pre-accident. We know it wasn't Noriko since she has natural pink hair, so it's natural to think the girl was Maya, the only other wizard we know that Akira had a relationship with - especially since the play date happened at Sensei's house and not wherever this other girl lived.
  • When asked about Ami's parents, Maya says that she wasn't close to them rather than saying she never met them. She also specifies that her friendship with Ami started later, but doesn't say anything about when she initially met the Arakawas.
  • Maya and Niki never met (Maya Prime also says this), but Niki has a vague feeling of recognizing Maya from somewhere. Maybe she saw Maya around the area where she and Akira lived pre-accident?
As for Noriko saying that Maya didn't show up until sometime after Akira started tutoring again, that just means he wasn't tutoring Maya with the other girls - even if she was living at the apartment at the time, it would be easy for her to be elsewhere during tutoring hours. Maybe he originally intended to keep her separate but realized that it would be best for both Noriko and Maya for them to be tutored with someone of similar intelligence.
Whether Akira and Maya met before or after the accident doesn't by itself make much of a difference for our understanding of their relationship, especially since it didn't become sexual until later. So that begs the question, why has this all been shrouded in mystery, with Selebus only dropping hints at a pre-accident relationship? For me, the most obvious difference it makes is that Maya was around while Sekai was still alive, and the two could have interacted. Maya saying she was "not close" to Ami's parents indicates they might have met, and it's most likely that Ami's play date was arranged by Sekai - in which case she knew that Akira had a little girl at his house.

From what we know of Sekai's personality, I think it's likely that she would encourage a relationship between Akira and a wizard, rather than be jealous of it. She's a sexual predator who rejects conventional morality as a point of principle. This comes from a world-view so twisted that Wakana thinks her poems are actually dangerous to read. How likely is it that a person like that would only have one victim? Wouldn't see want to indoctrinate the boy she loves into sharing that twisted world-view? What better way to do that than by pushing him to take his own victim(s)?

If we take Ghost Sekai at face value as a reflection of the real Sekai, the evidence definitely points in this direction.
Ghost Sekai is constantly pushing Sensei to fuck more girls, and she seems especially interested in wizards. She's the one who tries to get him to molest Tsukasa.
She's the one who makes Uta appear as a wizard and goads him about his preferences. She even reminds him how much he liked being with wizard Maya.
As for Sekai getting involved herself, Sensei said that he wasn't the only one she treated as a piece in a game and she tells him he was always her favorite, implying that there were others.

...
In just this last update, Ghost Sekai tells Tsuneyo that she likes to play with Sensei's "toys". And that happens while a blurred out Maya is on the screen.
Even with the real Sekai, we've seen that she likes to tease Akira about his relationship with Niki, but there's no sign that she actually opposes the relationship's existence.
There is one piece of evidence that might directly describe Maya and Sekai interacting before the accident: Futaba's ghost story.
I think the most important part of this is actually Yasu's reaction. The "camera" focuses on her during the story's climax which suggests it has special meaning for her. And after the story finishes, she implies the story really happened and that it's sad that the girl never got to "pet the cat".
Of course, the phrase "pet the cat" is specifically used to describe molesting Maya in "The Room With Clocks".
As for why Yasu is affected by the story and thinks that it's sad that the girl never got to pet the cat, keep in mind this is in Chapter 3 when Sekai/Pareidolia are in her head

If Maya is the cat in the story, then who is the girl? The girl has been dead for years and cannot speak. Sekai has been dead for years and cannot breathe (even before her death in Terminal 23 she might have been dead for years if you count Terminal 22). Unless someone wants to propose an alternate interpretation involving Nao-chan, I think that Sekai is the most likely person for the girl to represent.

So my interpretation is that the girl (Sekai) wanted to pet the cat (molest Maya), but died before she was able to do so. If Akira had successfully groomed Maya before Sekai died, she could have gotten involved later and "played with his toy", but that didn't happen.

There's a lot in the story that seems meaningful but I don't know how to interpret, like the importance of the 2nd and 63rd floors, why the girl feels hands on her shoulders (like how Akira frequently feels Sekai's hands), and even whether the cat actually caused her death. So it's definitely possible that I have this all completely wrong.
To finish off, even if this theory turns out to be true, I think it still leaves open Akira's intentions and the extent of his culpability with regards to Maya. Here's a couple of different possible scenarios with radically different implications on Akira's character:
  • The relationship originally started off as a wholesome one, with Akira seeing Maya as a reflection of himself and wanting to protect her. Because he's completely whipped and can't keep any secrets from Sekai, she finds out about Maya and pushes him into making the relationship sexual, but he initially resists even though Maya clearly loves him. Only after the accident breaks him does he give in and accept her feelings.
  • The relationship was planned out by Sekai from the start. She identified the vulnerable homeless girl as a target and gave Akira the task of grooming her. He always intended to turn the relationship sexual, it just hadn't reached that point yet at the time of the accident.
Of course those are two extremes, and the truth might be somewhere in the middle or include elements of both.

spoilers.title: The girl and the cat
spoilers.html:
I think the most important part of this is actually Yasu's reaction. The "camera" focuses on her during the story's climax which suggests it has special meaning for her. And after the story finishes, she implies the story really happened and that it's sad that the girl never got to "pet the cat".
Of course, the phrase "pet the cat" is specifically used to describe molesting Maya in "The Room With Clocks".
As for why Yasu is affected by the story and thinks that it's sad that the girl never got to pet the cat, keep in mind this is in Chapter 3 when Sekai/Pareidolia are in her head

If Maya is the cat in the story, then who is the girl? The girl has been dead for years and cannot speak. Sekai has been dead for years and cannot breathe (even before her death in Terminal 23 she might have been dead for years if you count Terminal 22). Unless someone wants to propose an alternate interpretation involving Nao-chan, I think that Sekai is the most likely person for the girl to represent.

So my interpretation is that the girl (Sekai) wanted to pet the cat (molest Maya), but died before she was able to do so. If Akira had successfully groomed Maya before Sekai died, she could have gotten involved later and "played with his toy", but that didn't happen.

There's a lot in the story that seems meaningful but I don't know how to interpret, like the importance of the 2nd and 63rd floors, why the girl feels hands on her shoulders (like how Akira frequently feels Sekai's hands), and even whether the cat actually caused her death. So it's definitely possible that I have this all completely wrong.

I put off this update because I didn't want to be stuck on a cliff hanger for too long. Meant to pace myself and make it last a few days until the next update but then blitzed though it. whoops.

  • I respect Niki a lot. She's probably the most responsible adult in the game. Unfortunately, she's sitting nicely as the king of the hill, unaware of all the sights being scoped on her. It's a bit foreboding.
  • Somebody please tell Makoto that there's still a lot of continuity between resets. Shes going to do something stupid and then be surprised when everyone still remembers it.
  • Oh god Chika. She's broken but not in the way you would expect. Her wholesome idea of romance is dead and now she sounds like she's reciting the beliefs of a cult.
    • Yumi is turning into a reliable voice of reason in both of her conversations with Chika and Makoto. She could probably do a lot more if she had any confidence in her own intelligence. Maybe Deathball Professor Yamaguchi is a real future for her.
  • Ami individually tells both her best friends that they're her real and only best friend. It's concrete evidence of how manipulative she is but our perspective as viewers is the only way to catch her red handed.
    • Ami is kind of scary because you can't trust what she says. I can't tell you if she's genuinely okay with being in a throuple or if this is just part of her giga brain plan to become the one and only.
  • I really need to go back and see the non stomach ache version of this event. Io is sorta pulling a Chika here and bulldozing her own preferences to try to keep Sensei around. It's pretty sad.
  • Tsuneyo being raped by Sekai was not on the bingo card. Tsuneyo is the most morally just girl in the class and now she's being deliberately targeted for corruption. Sekai also knows her most private thoughts? How and why? Does she know what other people are thinking?
    • We now have in game confirmation beyond the checkmarks that Sensei did rape Molly. Tsuneyo probably thinks it was just in her head though so she doesn't actually know.
    • The narrator also implied that Tsuneyo's father died? It lends credence to the idea that the resets have to do with her father's death. But during the first slumber party Mr.Tojo called Tsuneyo back home and nothing like that occurred this time. Is his protection slipping?
  • So Yuu is Sekai's father too? Bad news for Ami. Supposedly being a product of incest isn't a problem until it's happened multiple generations which would be the case if Ami gets the kids she wants.
  • Nao's motives raise enough questions that it's hardly worth even asking. But casually hanging out as Kaori bangs Sensei is hella weird. Also Kaori suggested involving Nao?? Hello CPS?
  • So pareidolia is both a real thing that exists and an excuse Sensei created for his actions. Its an interesting detail that after pareidolia left Sensei has to tell himself not to be a bitch and fuck kaori. I'm not sure if Sensei is being ironic intentionally or if hes just doing it because now his scapegoat wont do it for him. Also is HOPE dead without Yasu? Surely not, right?
  • Sensei quest. My god.
    • I did this on a vanilla copy of the game because I guess I hate myself. I was an idiot and grinded for the sword, thinking that would let me farm the other enemies. Nope. Sword is a key item for later. You need abilities.
    • The commentary of how much Sensei Quest sucks is pretty funny to me but I'm still the one who has to play it so ultimately I'm the butt of the joke.
    • I know a lot of people hate them, but I actually like the puzzles. This however is not a puzzle. It's just brute forcing a hidden combination over and over.
    • Thematically as a reset event I like it though. Kenji is also the first non-sensei non-silhouette male model in the game. Taken from us too soon... Whoever could have done this.
  • The cliffhanger is everyone in RAS has been transported to different realities.
    • Makoto at least went with Sensei for some reason.
    • Ayane's reality is curious. Molly and Sensei aren't currently traumatized by Tsuneyo's revelatory standup act. It's too brief to tell but... is that Maya Prime? She acts the same. Sensei helping Ayane prepare for her act is also out of character. Our Sensei is a much shittier person.
    • New Maya is confirmed to still be part of RAS but I'm not sure if she'll have anyone to help guide her through it. That will be interesting to see how it will play out
In fact this whole scenario is really exciting. I'm really looking forward to the next update. Woe is me, I have to wait now. At least I have like 60 pages of this thread to skim through.
Also Yumi MIA. Nodoka too?

In anticipation of learning more about Maya's past, here's a theory that I've believed for a while but never got around to writing up:
  • Akira and Maya met before the accident.
  • Sekai knew about Maya, was pushing Akira to groom her, and might have been part of it herself.
I'm fairly confident in the first part. The second part is admittedly very speculative, with one piece of symbolic evidence that I might be massively misreading.
I think the strongest piece of direct evidence is from the audio clip in sleepsong.mp3, which plays for the first time in "Torrential Downpour. Child of Man." Maya's voice describes falling in love with Akira:

"Do you remember the first time we touched hands? It happened on accident on the floor of your bedroom. At first I thought that there was no way you would ever see me in that light. But when all of the other lights burned up and I was still there, I finally understood you were just as broken as me. And I knew then and there that I would fall into you."

So this is the order of events described:
1. Maya and Akira have a non-sexual relationship and touch hands on the floor of his bedroom.
2. Something happens that causes the "other lights" in Akira's life to "burn up", and Maya finds out that he's broken.
3. Sometime later their sexual relationship starts.
For me, #2 has to be describing the accident: Akira's lovers Sekai and Niki (the "other lights") are removed from his life, one by death and one my choice, and he completely breaks for the first time. So that means that #1 happened before the accident.

The fact that #1 happens in his bedroom also suggests that it's pre-accident. After the accident, Akira is living with Ami and never tutors at his house, so there's no reason for Maya to have been there. The tutoring apartment looks like a one room studio apartment, and there's no evidence that Akira ever lived there (certainly not after the accident), so Maya wouldn't refer to that as his bedroom. The only thing that makes sense to me is that Maya visited him at his house (or even lived there) before the accident when Akira was living alone.

There's a few other hints:
  • Ami remembers having a play date with a mystery girl at Akira's house. Since this happened before they lived together, it's pre-accident. We know it wasn't Noriko since she has natural pink hair, so it's natural to think the girl was Maya, the only other wizard we know that Akira had a relationship with - especially since the play date happened at Sensei's house and not wherever this other girl lived.
    View attachment 4171426 View attachment 4171428 View attachment 4171430
  • When asked about Ami's parents, Maya says that she wasn't close to them rather than saying she never met them. She also specifies that her friendship with Ami started later, but doesn't say anything about when she initially met the Arakawas.
    View attachment 4171432 View attachment 4171433 View attachment 4171434
  • Maya and Niki never met (Maya Prime also says this), but Niki has a vague feeling of recognizing Maya from somewhere. Maybe she saw Maya around the area where she and Akira lived pre-accident?
    View attachment 4171437 View attachment 4171443 View attachment 4171446 View attachment 4171447
As for Noriko saying that Maya didn't show up until sometime after Akira started tutoring again, that just means he wasn't tutoring Maya with the other girls - even if she was living at the apartment at the time, it would be easy for her to be elsewhere during tutoring hours. Maybe he originally intended to keep her separate but realized that it would be best for both Noriko and Maya for them to be tutored with someone of similar intelligence.
Whether Akira and Maya met before or after the accident doesn't by itself make much of a difference for our understanding of their relationship, especially since it didn't become sexual until later. So that begs the question, why has this all been shrouded in mystery, with Selebus only dropping hints at a pre-accident relationship? For me, the most obvious difference it makes is that Maya was around while Sekai was still alive, and the two could have interacted. Maya saying she was "not close" to Ami's parents indicates they might have met, and it's most likely that Ami's play date was arranged by Sekai - in which case she knew that Akira had a little girl at his house.

From what we know of Sekai's personality, I think it's likely that she would encourage a relationship between Akira and a wizard, rather than be jealous of it. She's a sexual predator who rejects conventional morality as a point of principle. This comes from a world-view so twisted that Wakana thinks her poems are actually dangerous to read. How likely is it that a person like that would only have one victim? Wouldn't see want to indoctrinate the boy she loves into sharing that twisted world-view? What better way to do that than by pushing him to take his own victim(s)?

If we take Ghost Sekai at face value as a reflection of the real Sekai, the evidence definitely points in this direction.

spoilers.title: The girl and the cat
spoilers.html:
I think the most important part of this is actually Yasu's reaction. The "camera" focuses on her during the story's climax which suggests it has special meaning for her. And after the story finishes, she implies the story really happened and that it's sad that the girl never got to "pet the cat".
View attachment 4171492 View attachment 4171493 View attachment 4171494 View attachment 4171495
Of course, the phrase "pet the cat" is specifically used to describe molesting Maya in "The Room With Clocks".
View attachment 4171496 View attachment 4171497 View attachment 4171498
As for why Yasu is affected by the story and thinks that it's sad that the girl never got to pet the cat, keep in mind this is in Chapter 3 when Sekai/Pareidolia are in her head

If Maya is the cat in the story, then who is the girl? The girl has been dead for years and cannot speak. Sekai has been dead for years and cannot breathe (even before her death in Terminal 23 she might have been dead for years if you count Terminal 22). Unless someone wants to propose an alternate interpretation involving Nao-chan, I think that Sekai is the most likely person for the girl to represent.

So my interpretation is that the girl (Sekai) wanted to pet the cat (molest Maya), but died before she was able to do so. If Akira had successfully groomed Maya before Sekai died, she could have gotten involved later and "played with his toy", but that didn't happen.

There's a lot in the story that seems meaningful but I don't know how to interpret, like the importance of the 2nd and 63rd floors, why the girl feels hands on her shoulders (like how Akira frequently feels Sekai's hands), and even whether the cat actually caused her death. So it's definitely possible that I have this all completely wrong.

Gentlemen, if I may, I would like to step in quickly to to address a post and some reactions to it made earlier. I strongly advise reading GSwole's posts with greater care and a more literary glint, lest you fall prey to an abstract psychological trap without even realizing a hook has attached itself to your lip. Let us analyze this ARG gift which has been granted upon us like pearls cast before swine.

GSwole: "Well yeah of course. He got the best teaching from an early age."

Taken at face value with a naturally superficial reading we find ourselves giving a small, knowing smile at this clever turn of phrase; "Well yeah of course" is brisk, casual language implying something is obvious, and one would generally not imagine such a blase attitude directed to the idea of fucking a man due to the implied homoeroticism which is a rather touchy subject in boys locker rooms such as this, resulting in contrast - the source of all humor. This is followed by "he got the best teaching from an early age," which turns our smirk into a open-mouth grin as we chortle with joy at the cleverness of relating someone's sexual prowess to the abuse they received at a young age. By deftly softening the impact of this abuse with "teaching" we are allowed to think back to our favorite "teaching" moments in Lessons in Love without ceasing to smile. All-in-all a deftly crafted and humorous joke.

But hark! Therein lies the trep. Let us not be misled by the humorous tone to forget that "teaching" in Lessons in Love (TM) indeed serves itself as an allegory for "grooming" or at times "corrupting" (but not in the sexual sense: the kind where a bird vomits in the mouth of another). Consider the title itself in this context and perhaps the grin on your face will freeze and turn into an O-shape look of stunned horror. Indeed: What we have been so jovially laughing at is indeed no laughing matter at all! Who among us would look at sexual abuse and laugh in its face? I hope none! Yet the glittery silver coating of humor in this case has, so to speak, "baited" a number of individuals into laughing and chortling and chuckling and giggling and cackling with infinite jest at a mask covering equally unending sorrow. This is to say that the "Haha" reaction was the wrong one to press. The correction reaction to press is "Sad", or, in some circumstances implying the death of innocence upon a grim realization so heavy as to make someone's innocence shatter into six million pieces, "Wow". In other cases, it may be better to sit back and have no reaction at all.

I hope this public service announcement has provided some enlightenment. When approaching an "ARG" (alternate reality game) (the game is in real life!!! it's not a game!!! oh god!!!), it is best to measure one's reactions and carefully consider what one says or does. It may be the case that someone out there is embittered by sexual abuse being treated with such light-hearted mockery - to say nothing of eroticism! But what do I know? In fact, perhaps my own interpretation is completely off base here... perhaps the "Haha" reaction was correct at all? Perhaps we must face our fears and laugh? Perhaps there is no better fuel for surpassing the darkness of our souls than masturbating with glee and cumming all over the abyss? A cum-drawn smiley face in the void is kind of like a ticking clock that marks the end to all this supposed misery! It's boner time! Discuss!

posts.content_html_raw:
Resonating what others have said; Dorm Wars are great, but any future implementation needs to either step it up a notch or at least maintain the same standard the 1st Wars has established. Otherwise, why do we keep observing something that isn't even unavoidable like national holidays?

There are two things all Dorm Wars except for the 1st are guilty of that I can nag about:

- The lack of conclusion/aftermath
Till this day, only the 1st Wars honors the winning dorm with something worthwhile. 2nd Wars is somewhat excusable; 3rd Wars is not; 4th Wars is such an incoherent mess that isn't worth thinking about.
This is not about "why don't my choices matter"; I am fine with every contest result being scripted. What I am not fine with is going through a supposed contest with no real impact. If making two versions of the same event becomes too much, don't. Make one event for the scripted winning team and be done with it.

- The decreasing amount of interesting contests and contestant pairings
In the 1st Wars, many of the contests are either effective segues to showcasing characters traits, deliberate pairings, or at least exciting takes on common competitive plays. In my eyes, there are well-tailored. The problem is that these good elements will eventually run out; even reusing them reduces their appeals. When it does, we have contests that either feel repetitive without new blood, or feel rambunctiously thrown together for the sake of novelty.

From what I am seeing, the major source of these unsatisfaction is the fact that Selly frames what is essentially Class A group outing into a form of competition. A competition means a little less than a dozen minigames (that are hopefully all exciting) and a prize that everyone (the girls and the viewers included) gives a fuck about. Perhaps Dorms Wars is the only activity Selly can think of that is motivating enough for all 20 girls to participate. Perhaps Dorm Wars becoming a routine is a part of the circular timeline design. Or, perhaps this framework allows easier workstreams for Selly to come up with events. Either way, it has become more and more difficult to deliver everything with comparable excitement as each Dorm Wars goes by.

Meanwhile, beach trips are also self-invented and repetitive, but every single beach update has been a banger. Without needing to frame activities into dumb competitions, beach trips often are more liberal to really utilize the rare opportunity to have uncommon pairs of characters interact that results quality events (for example, some good heart-to-heart conversations or the recent reset talks). Imho, Selly should just let go of Dorm Wars as an excuse to let all 20 girls hang out if he can't consistently come up with exciting things under that premise. They can just...hang out under a lesser cause as long as the gathering itself is interesting enough. I know he can do it if he can pull off all the beach trips, but I am not sure if his ego allows him to give up this cute but outdated idea he came up by himself that is called the Dorm Wars.

This is not about "why don't my choices matter"; I am fine with every contest result being scripted. What I am not fine with is going through a supposed contest with no real impact. If making two versions of the same event becomes too much, don't. Make one event for the scripted winning team and be done with it.
- The decreasing amount of interesting contests and contestant pairings
In the 1st Wars, many of the contests are either effective segues to showcasing characters traits, deliberate pairings, or at least exciting takes on common competitive plays. In my eyes, there are well-tailored. The problem is that these good elements will eventually run out; even reusing them reduces their appeals. When it does, we have contests that either feel repetitive without new blood, or feel rambunctiously thrown together for the sake of novelty.
From what I am seeing, the major source of these unsatisfaction is the fact that Selly frames what is essentially Class A group outing into a form of competition. A competition means a little less than a dozen minigames (that are hopefully all exciting) and a prize that everyone (the girls and the viewers included) gives a fuck about. Perhaps Dorms Wars is the only activity Selly can think of that is motivating enough for all 20 girls to participate. Perhaps Dorm Wars becoming a routine is a part of the circular timeline design. Or, perhaps this framework allows easier workstreams for Selly to come up with events. Either way, it has become more and more difficult to deliver everything with comparable excitement as each Dorm Wars goes by.
Meanwhile, beach trips are also self-invented and repetitive, but every single beach update has been a banger. Without needing to frame activities into dumb competitions, beach trips often are more liberal to really utilize the rare opportunity to have uncommon pairs of characters interact that results quality events (for example, some good heart-to-heart conversations or the recent reset talks). Imho, Selly should just let go of Dorm Wars as an excuse to let all 20 girls hang out if he can't consistently come up with exciting things under that premise. They can just...hang out under a lesser cause as long as the gathering itself is interesting enough. I know he can do it if he can pull off all the beach trips, but I am not sure if his ego allows him to give up this cute but outdated idea he came up by himself that is called the Dorm Wars.

posts.content_html_raw: Usually I don't go into media with specific expectations since it creates a binary pass/fail which I feel is often unfair to the developer. I get shivers of intellectual horror when I observe some reviewer say something like: "I'm going to try X, and if X fails, then the game is bad." It's like setting oneself up for negative feelings which need not exist and putting developers up to trials which they do not even know are happening ahead of time - in another sense, it's kind of like threatening a developer using one's negative feelings as a crowbar to pry what we want out of them. Even removing the developer from the equation, though, it's kind of like gambling, going double-or-nothing, and I'm not a gambling man. We benefit more from keeping our interpretations wider than the sky such that we can enjoy as many possibilities as possible. In this sense, what I want to happen this update is a natural progression of the story and characters as per the developer's long-term and not wholly disclosed intentions!

posts.content_html_raw: I read the whole thread before posting, albeit skimming the non-Selebus posts. It was an interesting experience and well worth doing. The most interesting thing is how Selebus would help an enormous number of people and guide them through events - how to unlock them, what they're missing, etc. We're talking quadruple digit posts just helping people. This was rather intriguing to me, for was the purpose of the unlock conditions of these events not to be obscured to some degree? I had to wonder if developers universally feel some kind of stress response when people get stuck, or maybe in the past there was greater criticism-aversion such that helping people was felt as a way to avoid the game being blamed for the situation in some way... The most tragic post of all was Selebus's declaration that he would no longer be posting. I have felt that way a number of times at various points. It is like the last gasp of idealistic, purposeful choice against the ravenous hungering of the instincts. To know the right choice but be unable to make it without essentially putting your pride on the line by announcing it to others, thereby adding consequences to failing. It's for this reason I could not begrudge any stealthy posting on an alt that came after; how are we to quell the beast inside us that demands us to read everything, to see everything, to know everything, and most of all, to vent our truth upon them like steam from an overheated eye of sauron? In summary... damnit I didnt make it before the update who cares now. goodbye

Oasis951 said:
I'm new to this thread. Why does the date say "5 Years" if it's still being uploaded on this site now?
Click to expand...
When a developer breaks the site's rules and doesn't agree to start abiding by them again, their game(s) stop getting promoted. That basically just means that new updates don't push the game back to the top of the "latest updates" feature and the game becomes much harder to find for new players.

Rule violations that can result in this include harassing moderators and attempting to sic lawyers on them, using sock puppet accounts to post negative reviews of similar games (or fake reviews of your own game), etc. There's a handful of de-promoted games on this site, the other one that I'm aware of off the top of my head is Champion of Realms. I think they were guilty of review manipulation, but don't count me on that.

Some rules just get a game outright deleted, and that's what Sel had actually been hoping for when he started harassing mods.

The game tends to leak here within moments of going live, and that pisses off the dev. So he created the idea of "care packages" that function similar to DVD bonus content, and were going to have de-aged versions of the girls in bonus animations, with this hopes that those would constitute rule 7 violations and prevent the care packages from being uploaded here.

It didn't work, and they started getting uploaded here almost instantly, and he threw a fit. Mass-ban of any potential leakers from the Discord, his cronies creating sock puppet accounts to mass-report the game, threats to sue, the works. The mods de-promoted the game and told him to take a hike.

He wants the game deleted. He had no problem with this site when he was getting started, but now that he's making $10k/month, he wants it gone, and I suspect it's only a matter of time before he adds content to the game that will get that done.

posts.content_html_raw:
Have you guys finished the update feeling good? (not my thoughts on the update yet, just this one question)
I'll be completely honest, I think I wish these two updates had been just one. It was the original plan, and after seeing the final result, we could really had done without the second puzzle (that killed my mood in a major way). And if you account for the 40 supposed events actually being 36 - you could also account for most of the events from the last update not being reset related, and there you go, no reason for having reset part one and two - could have been just one.

That aside, I think this update was really confusing (and bloated) in multiple ways that weren't that fun tbh. Don't get me wrong, a lot was revealed and stuff that explained critical points in the plot, such as what the pictures that were shown to Maya were during "Scary Room"(Ami raping her repeatedly throughout multiple timelines), and the boxes being Maya's notes (most likely) - I'll unpack it all on a later post.

I just feel like the overall tone, especially cause we'll now be without updates until 2025 wasn't the best choice. To have just one event addressing this:

which is extremely cute, imo, could have used one or two more events after they're back to set a lighter tone for such a long wait to come. But oh well. I guess this will have to make due:

Hell if that isn't the perfect way to wake up.

Fuck it, let's start the discussions.
So, DeSkel must be having a field day as Ami killed his favorite character. That being said, let's highlight a few points of interest:

1. Ami is probably the original Maya. By that I do not mean that she's Maya, but that Maya's "place" in the reset was likely Ami's. If we take a look at the world Sekai is alive, Ami is behaving in a way that assumes the world is hers and Akira's. It's her happy ending, she was someone put in Maya's place (of having her memories preserved through the resets), but was MUCH smarter than Maya, and was able to figure out the mechanics of it all and manipulate them.

From that we can assume that Ami has always been lying, and has always known what was going on. She was the one that put Maya in her place during "Scary Room", and a lot of other stuff. It's possible that the voice she talks to is simply herself, either "mega-ami", or likely to be narrator Ami.

2. Maya Prime lied a lot and forgot a lot. She's had threesomes with everyone and has been raped countless times by Ami in the "Scary Room", from which photos survived somehow. VERY IMPORTANT to take note is that Maya is a somewhat recent development in the cycles, and that the actual companion to Akira was Ami. What this means is that countless cycles have been experienced (like a cycle in which Sekai is alive) that Maya doesn't know about simply because she wasn't there.

What this entails is that Maya simply doesn't exist. There was no Maya prior to the resets, she's an "accident" that happened at some point during them. That all of the girls were replicas we more or less understood, but Maya doesn't seem to be even that. Of course this is based on Ami's idea of things, she could simply be wrong about her own memories as well.

3. Nodoka wasn't erased, she was slipped in time. Very cute scene between her and Akira, and most importantly: "Don't go to the roof, stop her from researching, and you're going to need a new shirt". So Nodoka knew Ami would kill her, which also means that she sacrificed herself in order for Akira to learn this, or that this was the key for him getting back. This could also mean that Nodoka being there was one of Pareidolia's gifts.

4. Kaori doesn't erase Yumi, but helps her to go back. Think back to when Nodoka was erased. Actually it was Pareidolia that erased her, but he didn't erase her at all, he slipped her. This time she didn't erase Yumi either, and Yumi ends up also being slipped back. Maybe it was Pareidolia with Kaori at this point in time?

Think about it, Pareidolia said that he left gifts through time. Akira remembers Ami being a psychopath, and what Nodoka said. Ayane made it back with the scarf. New Maya died and Maya Prime did something instead of going to the roof, that was obviously not by accident. Maybe she attempted to slip back instead of New Maya? (Himawari says by the end that some things are different and that they won't be detected at first glance).

5. All Akiras are Akiras. This becomes very clear on the scene that New Maya is kissing him while he carries boxes. That's no random person in his body, that's just him. What changes is the amount of memories he's able to recall.

6. Akira doesn't really love Niki. And even with Sekai alive he'd rather have Maya. I mean, he loves Niki to some extent, what I mean is that he chooses to go to episcopalis and keep seeing Maya. When it changes to Niki, he forces it back to Maya. And Sekai is alive in front of him at the time. I guess that's a win for Maya.

7. Karin getting fucked in other timelines. Nothing to add, go Karin.

8. USER4 is here. And USER2 is booted? First off, USER2 was inside Akira's head and being corrupted by either Sekai or Ami, that was the issue. We also saw how an infinite amount of gods were trying to access the terminal.

9. Man, Makoto's childhood was really fucked. I already sort of had a problem with Maki's sex life, but now I really do. No child should be exposed to that.

10. Himawari is likely the first narrator of the game. And possibly USER4. Okay, this is a big one so let's get a separate topic:
So, Himawari is likely the first narrator and possibly USER4. Let's take a look at what this narrator says:


"while I squash a few bugs" implies she's able to do stuff, and just a few events before we see this:
"mom keeps joking" is likely about Ayane, could be about Sekai, but I mean - this is all very Himawari
Himawari herself was there for "senseiquest", which she mentions, and she's also there for this reset puzzle, which she compares it to:

waiting room also resembles the place she was at for ad meliora


By the end you'll see that the narrator says that herself is a flower that follows a light. In the new happy event, we see an alternate Ayane talking a lot about her child, which is about her age already, and just basically describes Himawari, including the not allowing her to reveal her name.

Well, we could go on, but I think it's enough to conclude that Himawari is the first narrator, and her overall plan is to fix this world. She lives with her mom somewhere, and Akira isn't there for it. If she's USER4 I don't know, but a bit more evidence has been added to that possibility. There's even a laptop with Lessons in Love installed with that one dude in the waiting room.
More or less these are just first impressions on some of the stuff I think could generate discussions.

Edit: forgot to add that Ami is likely the insane narrator that GOES LIKE THIS. Don't know if it's always her when it goes like that though. The entire story is changed by what was revealed this update, I'm sure a lot of us will be replaying the whole thing in the next months anyway. We can compare Ami notes then.

From that we can assume that Ami has always been lying, and has always known what was going on. She was the one that put Maya in her place during "Scary Room", and a lot of other stuff. It's possible that the voice she talks to is simply herself, either "mega-ami", or likely to be narrator Ami.
2.
Maya Prime lied a lot and forgot a lot
. She's had threesomes with everyone and has been raped countless times by Ami in the "Scary Room", from which photos survived somehow. VERY IMPORTANT to take note is that Maya is a somewhat recent development in the cycles, and that the actual companion to Akira was Ami. What this means is that countless cycles have been experienced (like a cycle in which Sekai is alive) that Maya doesn't know about simply because she wasn't there.
What this entails is that Maya simply doesn't exist. There was no Maya prior to the resets, she's an "accident" that happened at some point during them. That all of the girls were replicas we more or less understood, but Maya doesn't seem to be even that. Of course this is based on Ami's idea of things, she could simply be wrong about her own memories as well.
3.
Nodoka wasn't erased, she was slipped in time
. Very cute scene between her and Akira, and most importantly: "Don't go to the roof, stop her from researching, and you're going to need a new shirt". So Nodoka knew Ami would kill her, which also means that she sacrificed herself in order for Akira to learn this, or that this was the key for him getting back.
4.
Kaori doesn't erase Yumi, but helps her to go back
. Think back to when Nodoka was erased. Actually it was Pareidolia that erased her, but he didn't erase her at all, but slipped her. This time she didn't erase Yumi either, and Yumi ends up also being slipped back. Maybe it was Pareidolia with Kaori at this point in time?
Think about it, Pareidolia said that he left gifts through time. Akira remembers Ami being a psychopath, and what Nodoka said. Ayane made it back with the scarf. New Maya died and Maya Prime did something instead of going to the roof, that was obviously not by accident. Maybe she attempted to slip back instead of New Maya?
5.
All Akiras are Akiras
. This becomes very clear on the scene that New Maya is kissing him while he carries boxes. That's no random person in his body, that's just him. What changes is the amount of memories he's able to recall.
6.
Akira doesn't really love Niki. And even with Sekai alive he'd rather have Maya.
I mean, he loves Niki to some extent, what I mean is that he chooses to go to episcopalis and keep seeing Maya. When it changes to Niki, he forces it back to Maya. And Sekai is alive in front of him at the time. I guess that's a win for Maya.
7.
Karin getting fucked in other timelines.
Nothing to add, go Karin.
8.
USER4 is here. And USER2 is booted?
First off, USER2 was inside Akira's head and being corrupted by either Sekai or Ami, that was the issue. We also saw how an infinite amount of gods were trying to access the terminal.
9.
Man, Makoto's childhood was really fucked.
I already sort of had a problem with Maki's sex life, but now I really do. No child should be exposed to that.
10.
Himawari is likely the first narrator of the game. And possibly USER4
. Okay, this is a big one so let's get a separate topic:

posts.content_html_raw:
Some very quick first thoughts regarding the new update:

Ayane from a timeline where her feelings are not being reciprocated by Akira is very cute. Not that I don't like "our" Ayane, but it was refreshing and heartwarming.
This whole timeline (apart from Ayane) was just really creepy. I hated Sekai and it immediately destroyed all benefit of doubt I gave her during last update's Kyoto scene. She really was just a horrible abuser, it seems. Unless there has been some godfuckery involved to make her this way. Also, apparently we have a confirmation that Akira is Ami's Dad. Although I find it suspicious how Nozumu has been conveniently left out during this whole sharade.
Holy Maya Macaroni, I really hate this Akira. I will have to assume this is the creepy ass version of Akira from most of the other timelines that has been hinted at by Maya and Yumi, because the way he talks to Maya and the way he looks at her is really just giving me "I'm a piece of shit abuser and I like it" vibe, in contrast to the "I'm a piece of shit abuser but I hate myself for it and am a depressed mess as a result" vibe he has going on in "our" timeline.
Oh yes, as a Karin stan I was not only pumped to see her in that hot Wii Fit outfit, we even learn she is basically the closest to a LI after Ami in this reality, LETSGO. Ironically mostly because somehow Akira is really into football which I inexplicably found really funny. barglenarglezous Given Sel is American, I am 99% sure he was referring to American football, he would use soccer specifically if he were to refer to that sport. He has been using that term during the many soccer practice events with Miku, Karin and Kirin.
I'm really curious how new Nodoka will change going forward. I suppose it is implied that she will not retain most of the crucial memories that brought her into the position she found herself in, so I wonder how much she will really know and try to find out and how Akira plans to stop her (assuming he will remember to do so, which is also implied at the end of the update).
During this scene it is implied that Ayane knows for certain that Yumi and Akira did not have sex, which obviously refers to the list she made Akira do with all the girls he screwed. Was that not supposed to be a retained memory of Ayane's? Why would that particular information be deleted?
I was also very happy to see that one of my biggest gripes about Maya's lore has been addressed (see one of my previous posts ) where I protested that Maya would be unable to retain anywhere near the amount of memory that she claimed she had lived through. Now either Sel is reading along here (in which case, Hi!) or he has just naturally come to the conclusion that it needs to be explained, which would also give Maya's boxes a potential purpose, so he might have had that in mind the whole time.

Also, needless to say, the reset puzzle was dog shit. I don't know what I expected. I guess, after Sensei Quest, for him to become a bit more creative. This just felt like a drag and I would have taken way too long for me to come up with all of the answers on my own accord. I've lost all hope of him producing any good and interesting reset puzzles.

Cycle Variation Speculation:
1. On the world that Sekai is still alive, Nodoka says that the color is back. Maya is supposed to be the color that was stolen by Akira and corrupted. The world where Sekai is alive is also the world where Maya doesn't exist.

2. Ami says that Maya is an accident, and Ami is able to retain her memories through the resets (presumably) - Maybe she means that the act of retaining memories is done by her intentionally and Maya does it by accident?

I don't know how to put those two together yet. Maya is something that shouldn't exist, that didn't exist when Ami was main girl in the resets, and then she started showing up/retaining memories by "accident". At the same time, her arrival was actually an act of robbery of a color done by Akira, from which through corruption Maya spawned. It is also heavily implied in this update that Maya's parents don't exist, as even she can't remember them.

Maybe at some point an Akira of the resets went back in time, caused Sekai to die, and then went on to rob a color and conjure Maya? Which led to a variation of the cycles?

- Maybe we have Variation A of the cycles, in which Akira always ran away with Sekai during Kyoto, which led to her becoming his wife, Ami being his daughter from the start and that's the original cycles more or less. Which also means that the nature of the cycles wasn't because of Akira's death or a Maya pact, but rather from Sekai x Akira x Ami trio. We see variations of these cycles in the current update, on "arms bent back" (the rabbit family), and in "Amy" - in all of these, the three of them are a family.

Then, something happens, and the past is changed, leading to Variation B - Sekai dies, Maya shows up, and rather than Ami being main girl, Maya becomes main girl. Sekai starts to hate Maya (whereas before she didn't even exist), and Ami regards Maya as an accident that dares to consider herself main girl when she doesn't even know what she's doing (also robbing Ami of her place - and possibly of her mom).
That's as far as I got right now.

2. Ami says that Maya is an accident, and Ami is able to retain her memories through the resets (presumably) - Maybe she means that the act of retaining memories is done by her intentionally and Maya does it by accident?

I don't know how to put those two together yet. Maya is something that shouldn't exist, that didn't exist when Ami was main girl in the resets, and then she started showing up/retaining memories by "accident". At the same time, her arrival was actually an act of robbery of a color done by Akira, from which through corruption Maya spawned.

Maybe at some point an Akira of the resets went back in time, caused Sekai to die, and then went on to rob a collor and conjure Maya? Which led to a variation of the cycles?

- Maybe we have Variation A of the cycles, in which Akira always ran away with Sekai during Kyoto, which led to her becoming his wife, Ami being his daughter from the start and that's the original cycles more or less. Which also means that the nature of the cycles wasn't because of Akira's death or a Maya pact, but rather from Sekai x Akira x Ami trio. We see variations of these cycles in the current update, on "arms bent back" (the rabbit family), and in "Amy" - in all of these, the three of them are a family.

Then, something happens, and the past is changed, leading to Variation B - Sekai dies, Maya shows up, and rather than Ami being main girl, Maya becomes main girl. Sekai starts to hate Maya (whereas before she didn't even exist), and Ami regards Maya as an accident that dares to consider herself main girl when she doesn't even know what she's doing (also robbing Ami of her place - and possibly of her mom).

posts.content_html_raw:
….Well that was something.

Let’s address the elephant in the room first and foremost: holy fucking shit, Maya Prime was right and Ami is definitely a psychopathic killer! I made a whole post about how I doubted this was the case not long ago too… Me and my big mouth.

I keep searching for reasons to like and defend Ami, and as a character she’s definitely one of the most well written in the entire game, but man… it’s hard to like her when she takes things to the extreme.

I’ve had my fair share of problems with Nodoka as well in the past, and yet her gruesome murder at Ami’s hands caught me really off guard and made me feel really bad that she had to sacrifice herself in that way.

Nodoka hugging Akira was cute, though. Also the callback to White Fronted Parrot to confirm it was actually him. I liked that.

All of this, of course, only opens up more questions. How will things go with Nodoka now that the reset is over? Can Akira really recall Nodoka’s instructions and put them to good use? How will Akira and Ami’s dynamic change after… all of that?

Unfortunately, we have two months to think about it before we get any insight.

Oof, okay… I honestly feel… really bad for New Maya in this update. From her perspective, all this crazy ‘time stuff’ is finally revealed as true, revealing how wrong she was about the situation, and she can’t even talk to Akira about it or try to make it up to him. She has to live with that regret…

Or… had to live with regret?

Is New Maya even still alive? The Narrator at the end of her last event seemed to imply that she wasn’t. Not to mention you have Maya Prime (from the timeline Ayane and Yumi got stuck in) who wandered off to do… something?

I’ll just chalk this up to yet another thing that will just have to remain a mystery until next update.

Makoto’s events were really bizarre. I suppose that comes with the territory with these TSS events at this point, though.

It’s one thing to imagine what Makoto’s childhood situation was like, but it was another to actually witness it. And… yeah… I can understand why she was so distant with Maki. That looks like a tough environment for a kid to be in.

I’m glad Makoto made it through the reset once again. Good to have her as a RAS mainstay.

DUUUUDE, Yumi actually retained her memories this time! Let’s goooo!!

I would say this was long overdue or something dramatic like that, but… nah. I think Yumi’s inclusion in the RAS came at the perfect time for her. The fact her and Tsuneyo didn’t make it before lets us know that we can’t expect success every time. Strict stipulations need to occur before their memories can carry over.

What this is? Still unclear… but maybe one day we’ll know for sure.

Soooo… Reset Notes? Is that all that was in the boxes Maya made Akira carry?

Seems kinda anticlimactic if that’s all it was, but… I suppose it makes some amount of sense at least.

Wait… there’s two Reset Puzzles this Halloween??

…Can’t say I expected that.

So how was it overall? …Eh.

I wrote the numbers down myself in the past events they showed up in, more out of curiosity to see if they would become relevant, and what do ya know… they wind up as answers in this Waiting Room puzzle.

The side characters (if they can be called that) were as weird as you would expect. The questions asked are mostly non-sensical unless you know how to use Google and/or URM.

All in all, it was mostly just an obstacle event to reach the ending of the update. I would have personally preferred this screentime to focus more on the aftermath of the reset stuff, but that’s just what I think.

By the by, the bearded dude on the pirate ship mentioned seeing an Asian girl with pink hair with a chipper demeanor. Could this be Noriko? If it was, then wtf was she even doing here?

Another question to add to the pile.

…Wait. Is there a Happy Event? I completely missed it if there was.

Judging from others’ posts, you have to trigger it from… the Amy Happy Event?

Like… can you just trigger it from the replay or does it have to be on the first time you play it?

If nothing else, I can just use URM to trigger the event, watch it, then mark it as complete afterwards.

May make a separate small post on this Happy Event if I find it interesting enough. I already closed out of the game, though, so I’ll look into it later.

Ah fuck… HOPE’s back again. This can only end so well.

USER2 is no longer part of Akira? And I guess neither is any god? So like… What does this mean?

It certainly sounds promising, but USER2 has been way too quiet for my liking. There’s no way that’s the last we ever see of him.

USER2 may not seem so bad on the surface level, but I still remain unconvinced he doesn’t have any ulterior motives.

I suppose time will tell on that one.

Oh daaamn! Karin and Sensei are fucking in the alternate Halloween Dorm Wars timeline??

…Nice.

Now if only we could make that happen in our timeline.

The update overall was serviceable. I’ve never been too big on time travel bullshit, so focusing on multiple timelines at once kinda got grating after awhile.

As expected, we were left with more questions than answers this time, but we did still learn a lot:

One: Nodoka knows her shit.

Two: Ami is fucking nuts, and has been able to control these resets to her advantage for quite some time.

Three: Karin still looks really cute dressed as the Wii Fit Trainer.

All in all, this will be an update that keeps us talking for a little while. We’ll need it too, because the next couple of months are gonna be quite a wait.

I keep searching for reasons to like and defend Ami, and as a character she’s definitely one of the most well written in the entire game, but man… it’s hard to like her when she takes things to the extreme.
I’ve had my fair share of problems with Nodoka as well in the past, and yet her gruesome murder at Ami’s hands caught me really off guard and made me feel really bad that she had to sacrifice herself in that way.
Nodoka hugging Akira was cute, though. Also the callback to White Fronted Parrot to confirm it was actually him. I liked that.
All of this, of course, only opens up more questions. How will things go with Nodoka now that the reset is over? Can Akira really recall Nodoka’s instructions and put them to good use? How will Akira and Ami’s dynamic change after… all of that?
Unfortunately, we have two months to think about it before we get any insight.
Spoiler:
Maya
Oof, okay… I honestly feel… really bad for New Maya in this update. From her perspective, all this crazy ‘time stuff’ is finally revealed as true, revealing how wrong she was about the situation, and she can’t even talk to Akira about it or try to make it up to him. She has to live with that regret…
Or…
had
to live with regret?
Is New Maya even still alive? The Narrator at the end of her last event seemed to imply that she wasn’t. Not to mention you have Maya Prime (from the timeline Ayane and Yumi got stuck in) who wandered off to do…
something
?
I’ll just chalk this up to yet another thing that will just have to remain a mystery until next update.
Spoiler:
Makoto
Makoto’s events were really bizarre. I suppose that comes with the territory with these TSS events at this point, though.
It’s one thing to imagine what Makoto’s childhood situation was like, but it was another to actually witness it. And… yeah… I can understand why she was so distant with Maki. That looks like a tough environment for a kid to be in.
I’m glad Makoto made it through the reset once again. Good to have her as a RAS mainstay.
Spoiler:
Yumi
DUUUUDE, Yumi actually retained her memories this time! Let’s goooo!!
I
would
say this was long overdue or something dramatic like that, but… nah. I think Yumi’s inclusion in the RAS came at the perfect time for her. The fact her and Tsuneyo didn’t make it before lets us know that we can’t expect success every time. Strict stipulations need to occur before their memories can carry over.
What this is? Still unclear… but maybe one day we’ll know for sure.
Spoiler:
Maya Boxes
Soooo… Reset Notes? Is that all that was in the boxes Maya made Akira carry?
Seems kinda anticlimactic if that’s all it was, but… I suppose it makes some amount of sense at least.
Spoiler:
Reset Puzzle
Wait… there’s
two
Reset Puzzles this Halloween??
…Can’t say I expected that.
So how was it overall? …Eh.
I wrote the numbers down myself in the past events they showed up in, more out of curiosity to see if they would become relevant, and what do ya know… they wind up as answers in this Waiting Room puzzle.
The side characters (if they can be called that) were as weird as you would expect. The questions asked are mostly non-sensical unless you know how to use Google and/or URM.
All in all, it was mostly just an obstacle event to reach the ending of the update. I would have personally preferred this screentime to focus more on the aftermath of the reset stuff, but that’s just what I think.
By the by, the bearded dude on the pirate ship mentioned seeing an Asian girl with pink hair with a chipper demeanor. Could this be Noriko? If it was, then wtf was she even doing here?
Another question to add to the pile.
Spoiler:
Happy Event
…Wait. Is there a Happy Event? I completely missed it if there was.
Judging from others’ posts, you have to trigger it from… the Amy Happy Event?
Like… can you just trigger it from the replay or does it
have
to be on the first time you play it?
If nothing else, I can just use URM to trigger the event, watch it, then mark it as complete afterwards.
May make a separate small post on this Happy Event if I find it interesting enough. I already closed out of the game, though, so I’ll look into it later.
Spoiler:
HOPE
Ah fuck… HOPE’s back again. This can only end so well.
Spoiler:
USER2/Wires
USER2 is no longer part of Akira? And I guess neither is any god? So like… What does this mean?
It certainly
sounds
promising, but USER2 has been way too quiet for my liking. There’s no way that’s the last we ever see of him.
USER2 may not seem so bad on the surface level, but I still remain unconvinced he doesn’t have any ulterior motives.
I suppose time will tell on that one.
Spoiler:
Karin
Oh daaamn! Karin and Sensei are fucking in the alternate Halloween Dorm Wars timeline??
…Nice.
Now if only we could make that happen in
our
timeline.
Spoiler:
Final Verdict
The update overall was serviceable. I’ve never been too big on time travel bullshit, so focusing on multiple timelines at once kinda got grating after awhile.
As expected, we were left with more questions than answers this time, but we
did
still learn a lot:
One: Nodoka knows her shit.
Two: Ami is fucking nuts, and has been able to control these resets to her advantage for quite some time.
Three: Karin still looks really cute dressed as the Wii Fit Trainer.
All in all, this will be an update that keeps us talking for a little while. We’ll need it too, because the next couple of months are gonna be quite a wait.

Pool reset event skip:

Open chap4.rpy

search for

Code: 
    menu poolmenu:
        "Refreshments" if fourthsquid == False:
            jump poolrefreshments
Replace it with:

Code: 
    menu poolmenu:
        "Refreshments" if fourthsquid == False:
            jump endofwaitingroom
WARNING:
This is a very crude way to do this, should the dev call for any of this segments variables to be necessary to proceed future code changes will be needed.
