posts.content_html_raw:
Fire Lord Zuko said:
….Well that was something.

Let’s address the elephant in the room first and foremost: holy fucking shit, Maya Prime was right and Ami is definitely a psychopathic killer! I made a whole post about how I doubted this was the case not long ago too… Me and my big mouth.

I keep searching for reasons to like and defend Ami, and as a character she’s definitely one of the most well written in the entire game, but man… it’s hard to like her when she takes things to the extreme.

I’ve had my fair share of problems with Nodoka as well in the past, and yet her gruesome murder at Ami’s hands caught me really off guard and made me feel really bad that she had to sacrifice herself in that way.

Nodoka hugging Akira was cute, though. Also the callback to White Fronted Parrot to confirm it was actually him. I liked that.

All of this, of course, only opens up more questions. How will things go with Nodoka now that the reset is over? Can Akira really recall Nodoka’s instructions and put them to good use? How will Akira and Ami’s dynamic change after… all of that?

Unfortunately, we have two months to think about it before we get any insight.

Oof, okay… I honestly feel… really bad for New Maya in this update. From her perspective, all this crazy ‘time stuff’ is finally revealed as true, revealing how wrong she was about the situation, and she can’t even talk to Akira about it or try to make it up to him. She has to live with that regret…

Or… had to live with regret?

Is New Maya even still alive? The Narrator at the end of her last event seemed to imply that she wasn’t. Not to mention you have Maya Prime (from the timeline Ayane and Yumi got stuck in) who wandered off to do… something?

I’ll just chalk this up to yet another thing that will just have to remain a mystery until next update.

Makoto’s events were really bizarre. I suppose that comes with the territory with these TSS events at this point, though.

It’s one thing to imagine what Makoto’s childhood situation was like, but it was another to actually witness it. And… yeah… I can understand why she was so distant with Maki. That looks like a tough environment for a kid to be in.

I’m glad Makoto made it through the reset once again. Good to have her as a RAS mainstay.

DUUUUDE, Yumi actually retained her memories this time! Let’s goooo!!

I would say this was long overdue or something dramatic like that, but… nah. I think Yumi’s inclusion in the RAS came at the perfect time for her. The fact her and Tsuneyo didn’t make it before lets us know that we can’t expect success every time. Strict stipulations need to occur before their memories can carry over.

What this is? Still unclear… but maybe one day we’ll know for sure.

Soooo… Reset Notes? Is that all that was in the boxes Maya made Akira carry?

Seems kinda anticlimactic if that’s all it was, but… I suppose it makes some amount of sense at least.

Wait… there’s two Reset Puzzles this Halloween??

…Can’t say I expected that.

So how was it overall? …Eh.

I wrote the numbers down myself in the past events they showed up in, more out of curiosity to see if they would become relevant, and what do ya know… they wind up as answers in this Waiting Room puzzle.

The side characters (if they can be called that) were as weird as you would expect. The questions asked are mostly non-sensical unless you know how to use Google and/or URM.

All in all, it was mostly just an obstacle event to reach the ending of the update. I would have personally preferred this screentime to focus more on the aftermath of the reset stuff, but that’s just what I think.

By the by, the bearded dude on the pirate ship mentioned seeing an Asian girl with pink hair with a chipper demeanor. Could this be Noriko? If it was, then wtf was she even doing here?

Another question to add to the pile.

…Wait. Is there a Happy Event? I completely missed it if there was.

Judging from others’ posts, you have to trigger it from… the Amy Happy Event?

Like… can you just trigger it from the replay or does it have to be on the first time you play it?

If nothing else, I can just use URM to trigger the event, watch it, then mark it as complete afterwards.

May make a separate small post on this Happy Event if I find it interesting enough. I already closed out of the game, though, so I’ll look into it later.

Ah fuck… HOPE’s back again. This can only end so well.

USER2 is no longer part of Akira? And I guess neither is any god? So like… What does this mean?

It certainly sounds promising, but USER2 has been way too quiet for my liking. There’s no way that’s the last we ever see of him.

USER2 may not seem so bad on the surface level, but I still remain unconvinced he doesn’t have any ulterior motives.

I suppose time will tell on that one.

Oh daaamn! Karin and Sensei are fucking in the alternate Halloween Dorm Wars timeline??

…Nice.

Now if only we could make that happen in our timeline.

The update overall was serviceable. I’ve never been too big on time travel bullshit, so focusing on multiple timelines at once kinda got grating after awhile.

As expected, we were left with more questions than answers this time, but we did still learn a lot:

One: Nodoka knows her shit.

Two: Ami is fucking nuts, and has been able to control these resets to her advantage for quite some time.

Three: Karin still looks really cute dressed as the Wii Fit Trainer.

All in all, this will be an update that keeps us talking for a little while. We’ll need it too, because the next couple of months are gonna be quite a wait.

spoilers.title: Final Verdict
spoilers.html:
The update overall was serviceable. I’ve never been too big on time travel bullshit, so focusing on multiple timelines at once kinda got grating after awhile.

As expected, we were left with more questions than answers this time, but we did still learn a lot:

One: Nodoka knows her shit.

Two: Ami is fucking nuts, and has been able to control these resets to her advantage for quite some time.

Three: Karin still looks really cute dressed as the Wii Fit Trainer.

All in all, this will be an update that keeps us talking for a little while. We’ll need it too, because the next couple of months are gonna be quite a wait.

How to trigger the "Alexisthymia" Happy Event:
1.) Complete the entire 0.44 and 0.45 Halloween event chain.

2.) Download the URM or borrow someone else's save file that starts at the beginning of the "Amy" Happy Event. You cannot use the replay feature to trigger the new Happy Event. It will not work. If you're borrowing a save and not using URM, skip to step 4B.

3.) (URM only) Open up your URM menu with alt+M. By default, it will say Search in Variable Names. You don't want this. Click where it says 'Variable Names' and change it to where it says 'Labels/Scenes'.

4A.) (URM only) With that set, type 'alexisevent' in the search bar. Click 'Jump' to jump straight to the new Happy Event.

4B.) If you borrowed someone else's save, upon starting the "Amy" happy event and making it to the first choice menu, move left and then forward to reach the Taco Bell in the mall. This will trigger the Happy Event for you.

5.) When you have reached the end, you'll know it when Amy wants to get back to your date. When she finishes talking, ignore this and reload back to your latest save at the end of 0.45. The "Alexisthymia" Happy Event will be marked as complete and you will have a new Ayane profile outfit for your troubles.

The persistent variable 'alexisisreal' will once again be marked as False, and a new variable 'alexisevent' will be marked as True.

Overview:
Take over as the teacher of twenty high school students as they attempt to find their way through life. Manage and develop relationships with each of them in the fictional city of Kumon-mi. Choose how to spend your time after school and on weekends to best suit the path you want to take. Whether it be visiting the girls at their part time jobs, trying to convince them to let you into their dorm rooms, or just hanging out in the room with clocks at the local bar, there is always something to do in Lessons in Love.
Please note, some things in this game may be meant to confuse or disturb you.
But don't worry! Everything will be okay~​

Yarazin said:
Thoughts on .45

Just a reminder I type this out as I think of it then edit it later. It may make no sense and also all is subject to change 5 mins later.

You may want to skip this all since I kinda went off the rails this time.

If you are still interested, then here we go:
Didn't replay the last update again, just still burnt out I guess. Plus I don't even want to take the time to URM through the reset. I did start this one right after the orb fight though. Also, I kept getting interrupted while reading due to other stuff going on so I wrote down a lot more useless comments and I tried to be funny

Sensei/Makoto:
Right away Ayane/Makoto are awesome and Ami is a annoying psycho. I just cant like her the way some of you others do. She has her moments like the first time calling Akira dad but fuck she is annoying.

You tell her Makoto! Shit! Shit Shit!

Ayane story:
Maya's smile! I love it!

This talk between Ayane and Maya is so freaking fantastic! This is the stuff I most enjoy in the story.

Yumi! Please be part of the reset and please remember.

On to New Maya:
Uggh, I still have zero interest in Maya kissing or doing anything with Ami or any other girl.

Maya's smile in the hallway is very deranged looking. Understandable.

Yeah went from a great scene to this. Not interested! But hey, maybe this is what they were talking about way back during the real event.

Back to Sensei and Makoto:
Cant lie, Sekai is definitely beautiful in that dress. Nice legs.

However, I don't like her. She feels way creepier than even Akira. I don't like this scene with her and Makoto. Grow some fucking balls dude and push the bitch away.

Yeah the Maya and Niki stuff was funny.

God of Save Slots is a very funny name and that was definitely a happy memory.

I just really cant stand Sekai. Akira is so annoying as well.

Back to Ayane story:
Another great scene with Ayane and Maya.

Back to Yumi,
Please realize you need to find Ayane. Man this update is hella all over the place with the multiple timelines.

Damn touching scene with Makoto and Yumi.

Hilarious stuff with Miku. Karin main girl here lol.

Shit, is Yumi dead again?

With New Maya now:
Yeah lets just forget about the kiss. But got to admit the scene is making me laugh. "Someone help! Maya's on a kissing rampage and blaming it on all time!" Funniest line so far.

And it ends on psycho Ami, great.

Sensei/Makoto:
Good for Makoto to try and yeah at least she learned something (which she probably forgot later).

Fuck this shit is as confusing as ever.

Now confused more, is New Maya traveling or what the heck is going on here. I might need to start drinking, for today I mean.

So are we only getting one season between resets? Was Hope summer? Fuck I cant remember shit!

Ok, after getting a Jack Daniels...
Even though I don't like them, its a good conversation with Ami and Sekai

Very confusing with Nodoka, she verified it was Akira and then said don't go to the roof. Is it because she got time traveled there, he does still need to go right?

Fucking here she is, the killer Ami. I don't like Nodoka but geez. I cant wait for this shit to get back to happier times, which it wont for maybe 6 years

Is Ami really responsible or just more red herrings and lies?

On to New Maya:
Oh please I don't want to see Ami use that on Maya. The Sekai molesting Tsuneyo was bad enough. Come on please, to me this shit is NTR! (don't lecture me on any definitions please)

Fuck I am really starting to hate Ami.

I cant believe I just fast clicked past this. We seriously get a Ami raping Maya scene as a memory (that I will NEVER watch on purpose) before we see a actual Akira and Maya sex scene. You are a fucking asshole Sel.

Even though I hated that, it was funny for Sel to mention NTR. Plus fuck you again for not giving us PROPER Maya memories.

Starting a second Jack and Coke now. Fuck you Sel.

Back to Ayane:
Yay Yumi! Your not dead... or who knows Ill keep reading now.

I love Ayane.

Back to Akira:
Geez, happy music on a gruesome background.

Kinda have zero interest in this scene. Let see what happens in this confusion fest.

New Maya:
Don't understand anything here, other that I still hate this Ami and fuck Sel. I do have a buzz now so is that good?

Ayane/Yumi:
Insightful words from Yumi

Are those two the lame angels? Yeah I guess so. How did Hope come back? This shit is so confusing. I do remember Yasu saying summer would come back. But is this still spring or winter, it was snowing at the end!

So here I had to take a break but not due to the game.

Back a hour or so later and still have a slight buzz - I listened to Good Morning over and over while working on something else. Its my favorite song in the game since it reminds me of Maya. Ok she is now #1, with Niki #2 and then Ayane #3.

If only I was able to purge UNVALUABLE MEMORIES so fast.

Box of unpleasant memories. Sel is such a troll

And now I have to go look at the forums cause I don't want to go through all the options. (which I had to do anyway)

Uggh, another BS reset event. New friends is not fun so far. Why do I play this?

WTF would I want the tiny Maya as a outfit. LAME! I want a pretty dress on her!

I almost have no interest in this and just want to FF. By the time I got to meditate I started doing that. Not like I will remember anything except how lame this was.

Thanks Hernestojavier621!

I had to read the video game shit about LIL. Its like he is reading my mind! FUCK YOU SEL!

More FFing

More FFing, fuck what is the point of this shit. I never though I would FF through new content. I also wanted to stick with this until the end but I am starting to have doubts.

More FFing

Yay! Good Morning is playing!

Narrator asks if I am having a good time? On the whole, NO!!!! Also, they called him Sensei. Mean anything? I have no fricken clue! But I could (and have) listened to Good Morning for hours! I am clearly crazy!

Yumi with her arm over Makoto, SO CUTE! But New Maya is dead I guess?

So happy about what Akira thought about Ayane, she is great isn't she!

If they cant remember the reset, then what is the damn point? Just to fuck with the player? Glad Yumi made it through though. Hope things progress with her. Sad about New Maya but who knows what will happen with New New Maya? Maybe she is the same New Maya with spring memories but not the rape stuff. Fuck you Ami.

I just love it when the girls smile. Beautiful.

So it is still spring? With the snow. I am always so confugled.

Another uggh. Fast replay through AMY. Ohh that didn't work, need to load a earlier save. Jesus, Sel hates his players. or he just doesn't think about them at all.

Final thoughts:
Well I feel I have been complaining a lot. I liked some of the stuff here but if you add in the bullshit rape, the dumb reset stuff, and the weird way to get the Happy Event, all in all this update was very frustrating.

I mostly fast forwarded through the happy event since by then I was extremely frustrated. I did see some stuff about the daughter so I imagine a smart person will explain it. But does any of it really matter?

I will try and read others thoughts now, but it's getting harder to enjoy this story and the lore.

I wonder if the discord folks love this. Personally, I think Sel is bat shit insane and a major ahole.

Glad Yumi made it, she was great this update. So were Ayane and Makoto. I did like whatever we want to call past Maya but I figure she is lost to us.

Ohh, them not knowing who Noriko is was funny, and sad. Poor girl.

I wonder if anything will come of the pics they found last update. Very frustrating thing about this story is how long until we get more info about a subject. How many updates now since the Rin pic discussion?

Take care all and I am happy if you liked it and understand stuff.
Click to expand...
Gave you a like for the thoughts and the occasional "Another drink".
Would also give you a mad "like" for "Jack Daniels", liquid cough medicine tastes the same and might be cheaper

posts.content_html_raw: To my understanding memory generally follows zipf's law, which is to say that as there are more things to remember about something increasingly one's mind can only remember the most prominent aspects, such that we remember far less about things than we think we do (albeit we have to be careful since the impression that we remember things can sometimes trick us into thinking we remember what we do not). This is something valuable to understand because it can then be exploited for personal pleasure: indeed, in a work as long as Lessons in Love, I imagine many could read it start to finish over and over in an infinite cycle of remembering and forgetting details. I once tested this by watching a 6 hour lecture every single day for a month straight, and while at the start I expected to remember everything about the video, in truth every single watch revealed something new to me. Most damning of all was the realization that "micro-distractions" robbed me of significance comprehension: like if you sneeze while reading a line and then click to next line despite, in reality, having not fully parsed the line you just read, or maybe you get a phone call while reading and in that one moment of distraction you advance the text, etc... Over the course of a long work there will be countless micro-distractions which contribute to not only not "remembering" aspects of a work, but having never KNOWN these parts of the work to begin with. This is all to say that there is less need to wipe one's memory than many often assume, and we can exploit the rotten wires of our brains with glee to begin a so-called Hedonism Loop where we repeated our favorite activities over and over and over without ever engaging in anything new if we so desire. It's only when the value of a work is highly concentrated in the "most prominent aspects" that memory-wiping would be truly necessary, e.g. a mystery not worth a damn outside its answer, or a thriller where shoddy craftsmanship is disguised with the anticipation of who dies next.

posts.content_html_raw:
I have a feeling the Sekai we see in "Kyoto" and the Sekai we see this update aren't the same person. The one in this update seems more like the amalgamation of Sekai's worst(best?) traits and Ami's view of what the perfect mom is, someone who is fine with her little girl wanting to fuck her dad and killing someone without any remorse, being only worried about her daughter going to prison

If I had to guess, Sekai also died in this timeline, but Ami was somehow able to not only bring her ghost back (or something wearing her skin), but also allow her to become a physical manifestation, and then through many resets, this manifestation become part of the world itself, no longer considered a "bug" or "ghost" by the inhabitants (aka students and Sensei)

If I had to guess, the Sekai in our timeline might be in the middle of the process of becoming a tangible entity. At first it was just Akira but as more time passes, other people are starting to be able hear her.

Now this is going into crackpot theory territory, I want to write about it:
I honestly think this might be somewhat Wakana's fault. Not entirely, she wasn't the one who opened Pandora's Box, but it feels like she hasten the process by investigating so much about Sekai, and talking to other people about her, basically making others aware of Sekai's existence. Is like having a virus and infecting others with it but you are unaware of being a host until it is too late. Considering this is how Gods live and die, it would make sense.

I went off the rails but I wanna talk a bit more about this.
The only situation in which I can see Kyoto Sekai and Perfect Life Sekai being the same person... is if the Sekai we see in "Kyoto" is simply at her lowest of lows, to the point that she even seems human.

Either that or we were seeing her from a very biased perspective.
Akira was still a teen during Kyoto, and clearly had already been in a sexual relationship with Sekai for who knows how long. Considering everything I said about Ami's viewpoint, it is somewhat ironic that the whole event happened from Akira's point of view. Maybe the only reason we see Kyoto Sekai as a human being, someone who is broken, who lives in an abusive household, but still has the heart to truly love Akira and her unborn child...is because that's how Akira used to see things. That's how he was taught from a very young age to see the World, through rose-tinted glasses.

Hell we can even see a similar situation but from a third-person pov in this update. Remember New Maya's conversation with Sensei at the school hallway? from our PoV, the way this Sensei was talking and acting seem very offputting and creepy, it sent shivers through my spine since it felt like Ghost Sekai. But I'm sure that from Maya's perspective, he looked more her perfect "person", a prince.

posts.content_html_raw:
Okay, finally done with both updates. They were excellent. Although I didn't particularly enjoy the puzzles, seeing they're generally about inputting stuff you've seen on the screen at some point. Since I don't take notes when playing LiL, I had to cheat. Thanks to that, I could enjoy the weird banter between Sensei and the strange characters commonly present in these puzzles without stressing about answers. Consequently, the experience itself wasn't that terrible. I can't fathom grinding the currency in Sensei Quest, for example.

For some reason, the God of Clowns made me particularly uncomfortable; still, I could not ascertain why.

Having seen Io and Sensei's exchange during the Halloween party, I was tremendously satisfied with my choice of making Sensei leave in Stomachache. Io's smile is precious and beautiful. If Sensei loses control of himself around her and breaks his promise, I'll likely drop the game.

Touka's costume was my favorite, and I loved Yumi's conversation with Makoto. They had plenty of interactions during these two updates: seeing them being friendly is endearing.

More revelations about Kaori and an "h-scene"; Very nice. She's cute, as always.

Nozomu was a bad guy, after all. And it seems that Ami is indeed Akira's daughter. Miu is Ami's granny, and I assume the house by the lake is hers. I initially thought it was Saki's, so this revelation makes me wonder if Ami had much contact with Saki. Probably not.

This, of course, opens another can of worms regarding the Arawaka bloodline and incest. Once again, I'm reminded of Sensei's conversation with Ami at the hot springs and its significance. What was the bad news she refrained from presenting to Sensei? In this scenario, the reasonable answer is that, likely, the news that he already fucked his half-sister, so it was stupid to care about blood.

I once had a theory that Ami knew much more than she let on. I think it involved something I saw in Lamb Legs (possibly we see the "True Ami" who's a kind girl [living outside the Well?] No idea), but I've long since forgotten the details. Regardless, it's confirmed that she knows a lot, possibly more than anyone non-deity (some contenders would be the Maya Ayane meets, the one wearing a hoodie, and Nodoka). It's no coincidence that 今 (Nao) looks like Ami but with large irises.

It was certainly interesting seeing Sekai in the flesh and in action. What Maki and Makoto's dad (I forgot his name) did to young Makoto was disgusting and sad. Expected better of him (Makoto had praised him a lot, from what I remember).

Seeing Yumi finally join the squad was fantastic. Yumi has been particularly great lately, and her addition to the gang will increase the amount of exposition she gets. I was looking forward to it since she started showing signs of noticing something was amiss. Here's to more Yumi in the future. Her clone (spawned by HOPE) certainly looked sexy in Kaori's catgirl costume. A lot of untapped potential there. Something that includes dark eyeliners might be a good fit since it complimented Touka.

One thing this update also puts into question is that, so far, we were under the assumption that all (hard) resets start at the same time, roughly, which is the start of the freshman year at Kumon-mi High.

With the Ami Happy Ending timeline, it appears that either:
  • The resets can begin at an earlier point in time, e.g. before Sekai dies in the car crash
  • The resets always start at the same time but the past can be different
  • Ami has the ability to conjure Sekai in flesh despite her having died and manipulate others into thinking it's really her and that it's perfectly normal for her to reappear in her life
I'm pretty sure Prime Maya would have mentioned if either of the first two options ever occurred in one of her timelines, probably also that Sekai ever appeared as a living being. This gives me more reason to believe that this alternate Maya (I already forgot the nomenclature we agreed for her) > Prime Maya in terms of knowledge and experience.

Also, I'm not entirely sold on the different versions of Maya being just the same exact person at a different stage of time. Otherwise, how would Prime Maya be as shocked at seeing herself getting raped by Ami during that Halloween Scary Room event, if it happened to her in a (admittedly) distant past? Surely it would have left a mark on her and would be a crucial memory.

I just really hope Selebus doesn't trip himself over this web of time travel and timelines and alternative universes shenanigans like many authors do when attempting to incorporate such things in their stories.

For one thing, nobody interrupts the RAS when they start talking about time stuff and the world, and the game makes sure to point this out:
Makoto + Sensei timeline, not interrupted by Ayane:

Ayane + Yumi timeline, not interrupted by Chika or Makoto:

Maya "timeline", not interrupted by Sensei, Ami, or Ayane:

Makoto's supposed return to the main timeline, not interrupted by Noriko or Sana:

Like I said, I don't think it's NTR - and trust that you will find no greater NTR expert than I. However, we have to understand that NTR has grown to be a boogeyman for those who are emotionally fragile and intently possessive. A girl smiling at another guy is NTR; a girl ever having a boyfriend at any time in their life is NTR; a girl having sex before meeting the protagonist is NTR; and, indeed, a girl getting raped is NTR. A popular recent genre of NTR is "BSS" -> Boku ga saki ni suki datta no ni -> "but I liked her first", wherein the NTR is a girl who has never had a relationship with the MC is "stolen" by virtue of falling for another guy. Any world in which a girl does not remain untouched by anyone but the protagonist from birth to death is NTR. Any world in which a girl has any positive or sexual feelings for anyone but the protagonist from birth to death is NTR. Their dream of romance is a nubile virgin saving themselves for the ideal man then giving themselves to him (the purityfriend) as an eternal gift.

This psychology, really, comes from a blend of idealism and a gluttonous streak abetted by a glut of choices. First in the abstract world of fiction we can pursue our ideals unbound by earthly considerations, and for many - dating back to of course the Neolithic era - their "ideal" woman is one completely untouched and wholly devoted. In a sense this I do not decry; I cannot criticize fundamentally one who may yearn for a Maya who has never been fucked senseless by Ami (putting aside the conception that at times these events define us and "a Maya who has never been fucked senseless by Ami is no Maya at all"). The problem is more the gluttony, the gourmand's tongue that develops; a large amount of media caters to this unblemished virgin fetish rather intently, and so while under normal circumstances we may be forced to abandon our idealistic wishes to face the reality that the Virgin Mary of our dreams in fact fucked some random farmer in the back of a sheep pen when Joseph wasn't watching, in the modern world it is fully reasonable for one to absorb themselves completely in harem fantasies where much like in Lessons in Love there exist no men in the world except the protagonist and all girls love him unilaterally. This lack of opposition weakens the mind and spirit until anything outside of that is no longer acceptable - where the mere sight of a rival in love sends one frothing with rage, and THIS is precisely where NTR becomes the eternal boogeyman. Someone leaving their walled garden of gigavirgins will see something like the recent scenes in LiL and start raving about NTR because in their world girls are so pure and devoted that they would rush to immolate themselves in a roaring suicidal fire before there was even a chance of someone other than their beloved touching their skin. Being raped is betrayal; cumming to it is heresy. In their minds Maya and Tsuneyo and so on may now be burning in the ninth circle of hell alongside Judas. Even when faced with the divine fruit of knowledge that is LiL they can turn their back because the harem fantasies of their dreams grow from neighboring trees with abundance. Their walled garden is massive. And so their intolerance for suffering grows. It is a sad state of affairs. Thankfully there is still time for Selebus to delete all these recent scenes and ensure each heroine is wholly devoted/loyal to Sensei and also that every surviving man dies in space. Also it just occurs to me it's ironic that the anti-NTR guy didn't express equal rage at the LITERAL NTR of Haruka - this reflects how it's less the general act NTR itself they dislike and more the personal discomfort they feel at their potential pure waifus being despoiled.

Act 4 - Maya - Adulterer.

posts.content_html_raw:
Despite being directly shown how Ami in some alternative timelines possesses much knowledge about the fuckery, I still find our starting Ami (Amy Prime if you would) also being all-knowing since the beginning quite difficult for me to believe. Many early moments of hers to me really are genuine. Whether it's genuinely goofy, cute, or funny, it's genuine. The idea of our Ami instead being the absolute master of faking personality and hiding cosmic knowledge this entire time is such a tough pill to swallow.

Besides, there are some moments in the early chapters that really don't fit well with her being the ultimate hidden boss vibe. Even if Ami in both Pop Goes the Weasel and God of Light hints that she at the end of the day is still a player and not the game itself which could control everything, the following moments still don't sit well with how "viciously competent" she claims to be.


this is from a happy event so understandably this one lacks some creditability

Nevertheless, this update gives two mechanisms that might help ease off my suspicion: being sent to a certain timeline at a certain timepoint with intact memory, and writing down notes that might be exempt from reset-induced deletion. These two essentially have the same effect, that is to update one's memory and, depending on what kind of memory update it is, effectively displace and usurp your original self in another universe. The Ami that especially gives me this feeling is of course the one in Pop Goes the Weasel; it feels like this murderous Ami has journeyed a lot to finally find and land herself in her own happy ending timeline. She must've tried worlds after worlds just like what Rin described in her delusional dreams when she got rejected by Chika, only to have Nodoka come uninvited and spill way too many beans.

With this in mind, I went back and see whether there existed one glaring moment that could account for this type of displacement, then I found one that looked highly suspicious.

We haven't found out a meaning for this crucifixion scene. We vaguely know The Old Ones might be responsible, but neither the intention or the effect of this murder is known to us, and I feel like finding either is even more impossible if the girl executed here is assumed to be the all-knowing Ami (like, what's the point of that?). So, maybe this was how the all-knowing Ami arrive to this timeline? If this somehow is true then it means the Aim in Ch1-3 was the dumb, occasionally cheerful, and slightly crazy niece; and Ami starting Ch4 is this most threatening niece.
(A similar idea of this in another production is Yuno Gasai in Future Diary)
Granted, I forced a correlation between two things just because they are both suspicious, and neglected technicality so that I could to justify my skepticism. So perhaps all of this would be wrong and at some point I still have to swallow the tough pill that is "Ami has always been faking it since day 1". Sigh, I just want my dumb niece back.

anothersilo said:
With that said, I can totally see how other people would consider it NTR. I don't think people bothered by the scene are "overly-sensitive-to-anything-anywhere-near-NTR people." Some people view girl-on-girl the same as guy-on-girl and I do not think that's inherently wrong. If anything, it's probably less sexist. And I can see how getting NTRed after years of investing into a game and characters could make people very upset. And that scene clearly turned some people off the game.
Click to expand...
The concern isn't the sex/gender of those involved in these matters, the concern is "purity" and "loyalty." As well as auxiliary negative feelings that just come from a bad event. Of course, there are dials and knobs here such that some don't consider purity as violated when there are only girls involved, but that's their business - I never thought of it once. What I observe occurring here are thought processes like: "their purity has been violated -> the purity should have been mine -> I want them less -> this is NTR", or "their loyalty has been called into question -> they should be loyal only to me -> this is NTR." Observe that the review in question misremembers the scene completely and falsely claims that the scene describes Ami as so much better than sensei; this is a self report wherein the reviewer reveals their insecurity for not being 'the best performer', and how they want heroines to never have their loyalty questioned by liking a sexual encounter with someone else more. This insecurity is so great they see it when it is not there. This is what I'm talking about - not "lol Ami is a girl so it's not NTR."

As for me, I would say a key element to true NTR - and what makes it so sickening on a broad scale - is the distortion of Love and values. For example, we understand Maya to have a strong love for Sensei and to greatly value her relationship with him. What would turn the scene into NTR is for her love to be diminished and her values distorted following this encounter; for her to love Sensei less and for her values to be changed such that, e.g., she now puts more value on who fingers her the best rather than who has gone through hell with her or is a perfect personality match or w/e. These kinds of things are horrifying in two ways: one, they trample Love (the most sacred of all human emotions), and two, they essentially murder someone. Value drift is not taken particularly seriously by most people but in practice we can say that we are what we stand for and that our beliefs being corrupted is a corruption of the fundamental self. (Eventually, one comes to realize there is nothing to lean on in the entire world except our beliefs.) So someone "changed" by these kinds of experienced, NTR'd into another being, is essentially dead and gone.

This is to say in summary that an instance of rape (wherein the party enjoys it or not), or an instance of impurity, is not where the threat of true NTR lies. True NTR is a corruption love and values. Which can still happen! If, say, there is an extended arc of Maya following after Ami like a stray cat while denouncing ever having felt anything for Sensei (or something), then that would be NTR. Tsuneyo... well, her NTR may be ridiculous, I envision her shouting that she loves cock more than noodles, so the real threat there is Sensei NTRing her away from Noodles (both meanings) more than her being ntr'd from Sensei. And so on. Therefore we see that people responding to a scene poorly because it plays on their insecurities, denies their... 独占欲 as the Japanese say, threatens the purity of heroines, and so on, is not actually cause for ringing the NTR alarm. That is simply sensitivity resulting in NTR being called as a boogeyman representing any instance of a heroine not being fully pure and fully devoted to the protagonist.

The two main bugs in this version are:

* Maya visitable when she shouldn't be

* If you invite someone from the phone menu at night (or almost any old animated scene - In my specific case, it happened after inviting over Niki) , after the event you end up in the pre-chapter 4 hub. This means you get the old usual Ami telling Sensei to wake up, followed by a jump to evening, with the city background. On weekends you can go to the mall to visit Chika, or go to the Koi Cafe to see Rin and Haruka. If you end up in this situation, it's an easy fix with URM, search for the label `morningch4` or `noonch4`or `nightch4`and jump to the label. You can also not do that and revisit the old generics for nostalgia's sake. You can grind your Rin affection for example.

Apparently this bug is because at the end of the animated scene there's a jump to the label "endofsat" instead of "endofsatch4". Same thing with the non saturday label. This is because Sel hasn't updated the code of the old pre "senseisad" animated scenes, so by default it drops you on chapter 3 menu. A non-URM solution would be to activate a scene with a proper chapter4 jump, maybe the new Molly scene for example.

Or, if you want to, you can edit the animatedscenes.rpy, adding a conditional on every scene to jump to the ch4 label if the chapter4 flag is active, or to the ch3 hub if not. I don't think nobody wants to code that much though.

posts.content_html_raw:
somedoodwhogames said:
HOPE/User2 got infected by the viruses that got installed on the terminal triggered by Sensei's use of Terminal 84, right? What does that mean when we've seen "rabies" used to describe the complete and utter reprogramming of Chica's personality. Are there any hints as to who/what uploaded the viruses...Himawari? Nao? Paredolia? How is HOPE going to be changed by this?
Click to expand...
Those are a lot of complex questions into one. Let's take it step by step. I warn you that the following is a highly lore heavy post, take it slowly.
1. Kumon-mi used to have four seasons, one would assume one god was responsible for each. Then the seasons were taken from them, and it became just winter and summer. Each of them was also doubled in its duration because it encompassed one of the missing ones. That is why, presumably, both winter and summer had one reset in the middle of them and continued on despite of it.

When Pareidolia took over and brought spring back, it was Wires' turn to assume control. Therefore, when Pareidolia is out (by his own will), it should be Wires' turn to assume control because it would be Winter part 2 if Pareidolia didn't bring spring. That's kind of what we see, however, USER2 was unable to kick out the trojans, correct the date, factory reset Akira or deal with the absurd number of gods trying to log in. USER2 became at risk of being infected, but he was unable to leave Akira, and then after being infected, he was attacked by viruses. Thus he was removed by someone.



Another important note is that while performing the scan of situation, USER2 found USER4 as an administrative account.



Moving forward a bit, after the monologue from Narrator Himawari (I'm pretty sure by this point), that makes it seem like she was the one that logged in as USER4 and changed things, we see snow in Kumon-mi.



Snow, mind you, is an event that happens on Winter/Wires' season, this snow however is cut short, and it is unclear if it really was just a passing snow (a sign of the issue of Wires trying to assume control and failing), or something else.



2. Okay, now that we have discussed the Wires' part of the situation, let's move to the other one.

Before Wires shows up, HOPE shows up (and to an extent Wires could have logged in in response to him), well the thing is HOPE should NOT have awakened yet. HOPE sleeps in the underheaven out of summer, that he's awake means that he may be trying to takeover the rest of spring as well. Basically, we have a spring part 2 without a god to look over it, and both Wires and HOPE being awake to take it over (from what we presume).



Think we're done yet? nope. Because I must also point out that HOPE and Wires went to different places in order to take over. We've seen how Wires went directly to Akira and tried to bring him back from his time-travel, but failed, and Akira had to find his way back (it was actually Himawari that brought him, she's right there, and then as a narrator she says she's the one that managed to get his world open again for him).



Well, where did HOPE go then? He went to the world of Alt Maya, Ayane and Yumi. He shows up as HOPE the peerless god of light and is the one that brings them back to Akira's world after declaring that they're important to him now:



a big question for all to ponder is WHY does he go there? My guess is that Alt Maya was the one that called him there. Remember her saying that she had to do something when she learns that the reset is coming? This isn't ironclad at the moment because Kaori is the one that tells Yumi about the reset, which might also mean that she's in league with HOPE, or called him to rescue them.

3. So, we're almost done - we have two different gods that awake following Pareidolia leaving spring, both presumably intent on taking it for themselves. One goes to save Akira and fails. The other goes to save Ayane and Yumi and succeeds. What about Makoto?



Well, she's saved by LongMaya/YouDidIt sort of. She tells the god of clowns to send her back, which he does, while preserving her memory of events. It's just that she, along with Ami and Maya (before the rape) are met with HOPE right after. This is confusing as the rape may have happened after they met HOPE, or in another reality altogether. Not the point here anyway.


My god that was a lot, I'll add a tldr.
tldr: Pareidolia is gone and spring is godless. Both HOPE and Wires wake up to try to takeover it. Wires goes to save Akira and fails, USER4 (probably) has to come in to save both Wires and Akira. HOPE goes to save Ayane and Yumi, he succeeds. Presumably saves Makoto as well (although she was more or less safer than them). Akira has memories of his timeline (since he was saved by Himawari/USER4), the girls that were saved by HOPE don't. It is unclear who has spring at the moment.
This is complicated because the infection is not exactly about a virus, but about Ami becoming infected with something way back during the events of she being "lost" in the old district. This leads to her being killed in a ritual sacrifice, and during paper city you can go to the dorms and find both Kaori (literal god) and Nao-chan (also probably a god) securing her room. They tell you of the infection.



We thought for a long time that the infection might have to do with either the world itself or Sekai. Since the infection tries to attack Wires in the world where Ami has her "happy ending", it is likely that either Ami herself is the infection, or that she's deeply infected. During the events of "somnanbula" some of what she says seems to hint at her intending to bring down the gods and put Akira in their place, so it would follow that she'd try to infect gods.



Aditionally, I haven't talked about this but during Wires' scan, he finds and tries to clear the trojans. USER4 is not a trojan, and USER3 isn't even there anymore. The trojan would likely be either Ami/Sekai or Himawari. I'm betting on Ami/Sekai.
I don't consider the events of the waiting room to be that important, it's likely a lot of nonsense. If I had to point out some things, it's the dude that seems to reference Noriko's symposium, Himawari's presence, and that the angels call the roof where Ayane and Yumi are at also "the waiting room".

Well, most of this is up in the air, so take it for what it is. Anyone reading this will probably leave even more confused than they were at the start. You're welcome Now you have some idea of how my brain looks like when I'm playing a new update (it's a mess).

USER2 became at risk of being infected, but he was unable to leave Akira, and then after being infected, he was attacked by viruses. Thus he was
removed
by someone.
Another important note is that while performing the scan of situation, USER2 found USER4 as an administrative account.
Moving forward a bit, after the monologue from Narrator Himawari (I'm pretty sure by this point), that makes it seem like she was the one that logged in as USER4 and changed things, we see snow in Kumon-mi.
Snow, mind you, is an event that happens on Winter/Wires' season, this snow however is cut short, and it is unclear if it really was just a passing snow (a sign of the issue of Wires trying to assume control and failing), or something else.
2. Okay, now that we have discussed the Wires' part of the situation, let's move to the other one.
Before Wires shows up, HOPE shows up (and to an extent Wires could have logged in in response to him), well the thing is HOPE should NOT have awakened yet. HOPE sleeps in the underheaven out of summer, that he's awake means that he may be trying to takeover the rest of spring as well. Basically, we have a spring part 2 without a god to look over it, and both Wires and HOPE being awake to take it over (from what we presume).

We've seen how Wires went directly to Akira and tried to bring him back from his time-travel, but failed, and Akira had to find his way back (it was actually Himawari that brought him, she's right there, and then as a narrator she says she's the one that managed to get his world open again for him).
Well, where did HOPE go then? He went to the world of Alt Maya, Ayane and Yumi. He shows up as HOPE the peerless god of light and is the one that brings them back to Akira's world after declaring that they're important to him now:
a big question for all to ponder is WHY does he go there? My guess is that Alt Maya was the one that called him there. It's just that she, along with Ami and Maya (before the rape) are met with HOPE right after. This is confusing as the rape may have happened after they met HOPE, or in another reality altogether. Not the point here anyway.
My god that was a lot, I'll add a tldr.

This is complicated because the infection is not exactly about a virus, but about Ami becoming infected with something way back during the events of she being "lost" in the old district. This leads to her being killed in a ritual sacrifice, and during paper city you can go to the dorms and find both Kaori (literal god) and Nao-chan (also probably a god) securing her room. * If you invite someone from the phone menu at night (or almost any old animated scene - In my specific case, it happened after inviting over Niki) , after the event you end up in the pre-chapter 4 hub. Apparently this bug is because at the end of the animated scene there's a jump to the label "endofsat" instead of "endofsatch4". Same thing with the non saturday label. This is because Sel hasn't updated the code of the old pre "senseisad" animated scenes, so by default it drops you on chapter 3 menu. A non-URM solution would be to activate a scene with a proper chapter4 jump, maybe the new Molly scene for example.

(if not interested in more NTR discussion just skip)

It has been brought to my attention that some of the recent reviews about the game have been focused on it needing an NTR tag, and even though we have addressed this discussion on the thread, it seems like we haven't provided enough support for these people. So if you feel betrayed or appalled by the NTR in this game, here's a post for you.

First off, should this game have an NTR tag? Imo, yes, absolutely. Unfortunately, for all that we joke about it, Selebus isn't here. And from his relationship with f95, their relationship with the game is not the best. So who knows how that would even come to be.
If you somehow feel betrayed that recently scenes have been showing sexual interactions between two characters without Akira being involved, you have every right to feel that way. Even though Selebus seems to justify it by claiming that "actually nothing there is real, it's only the two of us here", the effect that those scenes generate on the reader is obviously NTR. Even if the only two people there are ultimately Akira and someone else, or even just Akira - the point remains. If one dreams about NTR, it's still NTR even if it ultimately doesn't exist. It would fall into the case of a game that doesn't have NTR on its main route, but then has a what if or bad end with it. Would that game classify by having NTR? Obviously it would. So does LiL, even if in the end Akira is alone in a coma or something.

That being said, even though not as explicit as the Ami x Maya scene, NTR has always been a part of this game. Maya has been raped by machines and purple hat dude a LONG way back (including her not wanting for him to see her cum from it). Gods have stated multiple times that they rape the girls. Akira himself has engaged in NTR with Haruka (netori) and Chika (bad homie). Akira cucks himself in a happy event (or possibly is seeing Sekai and Nozomu being represented by him and Maya). Otoha assaults Niki. And, very importantly but often ignored, Akira is deeply traumatized by NTR, having to listen to his brother fuck and assault the woman he loves for years on end.

Does this list of NTR stuff that has been in the game for so long negates anyone's right to be outraged by recent scenes? No. But it is also the reason why it may seem a bit weird for someone to go on a rant about it now. This kind of stuff happening has been around for a long time and the only difference is that it's now on the forefront. If it makes anyone feel better, I don't like it either, as I don't like a lot of stuff in the game. I personally don't understand why Selebus seems to have focused on this now, when it's obvious that he will lose money for it, and he could easily have kept it on the background as always. But then again, Selebus seems to believe that no matter what he does it will always be genius and people will swallow it no matter what.
Anyway, if you decide to stop playing the game because of recent NTR scenes, don't leave feeling that you're at odds with us - the community. I, for my part, wish you goodluck and completely understand your decision. The premise of a game where the only dude is you could easily be seen as misleading in terms of an unspoken agreement of Akira being "safe" from any "competition". While we sometimes joke about the NTR-hater crowd, this does not extend to actually reasonable people raising reasonable concerns.

May you find appropriate games, and if you ever change your minds, we'll be here - hopefully with a proper tag. (although if the tag ever happens I can already see the repeated "what kind of NTR does this game has?" being the new "I need a save" lol)

Yeah I enjoy reading your posts, especially the shitposts

re: people disliking it when you are mean/insulting, isn't that natural?

Also while we're on the topic, I'm curious - roughly how old are you, what do you do for a living, and how did you achieve such a high level in that rare skill known as media literacy? Also, why did you change your mind on defending the game's flaws?

To keep it even, I'm <>, work as a <>, and the last question doesn't apply to me cos my media literacy level is -69 uwu (deleted original to preserve anonymity )
Click to expand...
It's just the kind of thing that's saddening to see in practice. I imagine people don't ACTUALLY want to be swayed by their base emotions like this. Like, you don't want to befriend a malicious serial killer just because they're nice to you, and you don't want to dislike... this is a harder example to give purely for rhetorical reasons, but you don't want to fail to recognize the beggar in a street is a Buddha. Imagine a scenario where one is stuck in the middle of nowhere and you have to call for help; pleasant associates may not come while the assholish friend does. That kind of thing. In a LiL context, we don't want to like Ami because she presents herself as a super-niece and writes flowery poetry when in reality she is extremely self-centered and malicious (as also reflected by her "honest" poetry, which is thick and dark); we don't want to dislike Maya because she's vitriolic to us at the start when in reality she is the most devoted partner imaginable. There is a LOT of benefit to seeing the truth of a person / matter regardless of one has a positive or negative experience with them. This isn't to say I specifically am a great person who should be befriended, but it is kind of dispiriting to be reminded of how effective clown masks are - that social relationships can so often be reduced to a meter where "make interactions pleasant = be beloved, make interactions unpleasant = be hated," and that the people around us can be manipulated so easily. (We can also observe this in how Selebus was far more beloved here in the era when he wore that uncannily enthusiastic mask(?) in his initial Patreon posts).

For my own part, although vehemental and some others have said some fairly vicious things I don't take personal offense or hold it against them. Certainly, I would not go so far as to say that their poor reaction to exaggerated condescension means "they are not worth reading" or "their opinion is not at the baseline level of value." I do not evaluate the character of others based on how mad and insulting they are in the moment. Despite all they've said: Vehemental has an acute mind and are most likely good at Elden Ring, Bingoogus's boisterous personality is charming, Moonflare is fairly thoughtful on a variety of subjects and has interesting takes... Riolol so far has just been kind of mean but I maintain optimism as to their greater character. And of, course, there is Selebus, who I am obliging by continuing to post even as he watches, or maybe doesn't. (Also, you endorsed the progress mod! Don't laugh react to vehemental when it is DEVELOPER APPROVED to use progress mod! Maybe ban people the moment you see "hints" on the screenshots, eh? Also, smh, reading F95 on your trip, don't do that to yourself.) Anyway, there's a phrase in Brazil that goes like "fight all day, emerge as friends in the morning." Perhaps one intention here is to see if they hold a grudge for the rest of their lives. It would be VERY neat if e.g. Bingoogus remains pretty insulting after a few years. I have to imagine that like, due to the ignore, over time they would forget the details of my Sensei Quest posting, and then just vaguely remember "that guy sucks," and act based on that. Which could be cool to experience. It's all very novel. (Of course, right now I am deploying "clinical dry autistic" personality, so if that one earns as much ire as "pretentious overlord" personality, then that's fair too. Though I'm not as sympathetic to disliking long posts for being long as I am for disliking insulting and condescending posts.)


"Media literacy" is kind of a joke in the current climate so I don't want to respond seriously at risk of sounding smug or condescending which is 100% guaranteed to result in the ire of a reading audience. But in terms of getting more out of what one reads I think it is beneficial to read a lot, care a lot, and think a lot. Creation is kind of an endless cycle of old content being absorbed and new content being spat out; a familiarity with Little Busters, Higurashi, Cross Channel, and so on make many aspects of LiL more clear (if you are fond of Akira's character development then you will surely delight in Taichi's depiction in Cross Channel). If you read a lot then you will be able to tell when an author is breaking established norms, what is purposeful, what is skillful, and so on. Common patterns for specific themes etc. Selebus's own genius was birthed in part by watching like a thousand anime and a hundred VNs. You can see this in his writing style which constantly injects references to all the stuff he has read, though one needs to be extremely erudite to notice ALL of the references, from Horimiya's egg time (a joint project with Wonder Egg), to FF14 skill names like 'sacred soil' and 'hallowed ground' being deployed, and so on; the overt Subahibi nods are too surface level to be worth considering here.

Secondly is caring a lot. This means not just consuming but paying attention to what you are consuming, and being invested in getting the most out of it. "Paying attention" sounds simple on the surface but is actually much more nuanced than you may imagine. First of all, in the modern era there is always the temptation to have a stream or TV show up on a second monitor. If one gets bored there is also a temptation to skim (note the ENORMOUS number of reviews which mention holding CTRL the moment a scene is uninteresting to them). In the case of books I think barely anyone is reading books anymore (not even Selebus!) so probably not meaningful to talk about them here. But all things considered actually paying attention to what one reads is difficult. Over time one is liable to enter a kind of flow state where they just skim the surface of words without understanding them or ever pausing to think; this is how one can finish a very blatant mystery novel without ever solving the mystery, for example, or miss otherwise major details. It's good to constantly challenge oneself and make sure you are paying attention instead of skimming. Something I like to do is quiz myself on details like "what was the scene I just read about? what was that line saying?" etc, because with some intellectual honesty one may realize that even such simple questions can be surprisingly hard to answer if one was skimming in the moment. Taking the time to re-read in these cases is very valuable.

"Being invested in getting the most out of something" is abstract so allow me to explain that as well. It benefits us, not the author, to try to maximize value from media. We want to enjoy everything as much as possible. An investment in this goes a long way to fully understanding media as one looks at something from every possible angle to maximize enjoyment. Wittgenstein wrote it like this:

Take the question: "How should poetry be read? What is the correct way of reading it?" If you are talking about blank verse the right way of reading it might be stressing it correctly - you discuss how far you should stress the rhythm and how far you should hide it. A man says it ought to be read *this* way and reads it out to you. You say: "Oh yes. Now it makes sense." There are cases of poetry which should almost be scanned - where the metre is as clear as crystal - others where the metre is entirely in the background. I had an experience with the 18th century poet Klopstock. I found that the way to read him was to stress his metre abnormally. Klopstock put (meter symbols) in front of his poems. When I read his poems in this new way, I said: "Ah-ha, now I know why he did this." What had happened? I had read this kind of stuff and had been moderately bored, but when I read it in this particular way, intensely, I smiled, said: "This is grand," etc. But I might not have said anything. The important fact was that I read it again and again. When I read these poems I made gestures and facial expressions which were what would be called gestures of approval. But the important thing was that I read the poems entirely differently, more intensely, and said to others: "Look ! This is how they should be read." Aesthetic adjectives played hardly any role.
Click to expand...
I think most will encounter something which "moderately bores them" or is otherwise unpleasant and stop there. Case closed, right? But It is beneficial FOR OUR OWN SAKE to keep re-reading the poem, looking at it from different angles, rereading it, and so on, until eventually we can smile and declare "This is grand!" There is a goldmine of value to be extracted from media that slips us by if we are not paying attention and invested in finding it. We all know the sorrow of sharing some amazing media with someone who completely writes it off over something comparatively small, like, let's say sharing LiL with someone who drops it near the start because they got bored of affection grinding. This is a totally fair experience to have and a fair reason for dropping it, but think of all the fucking gold they're missing, right? It would be to their own benefit to keep moving the poem about to look for more value. And yes I'm using LiL as an example there for dramatic irony. Essentially, you generally want to look at media from every angle to find the best angle, not stop at the first angle you see. (I think posters like Moonflare are interesting in how they stare VERY intently at a single angle, deriving much meaning from it, but are inflexible when it comes to looking for another angle.)

BTW, a symptom of caring about media is being invested in the process of creation; if you find yourself looking up the storyboard artists of an anime, or the scriptwriters of movies, etc, you are on the write track. Through understanding the process of creation and who is creating our understanding and appreciation for media grows. As for myself, I have written several unpublished, private books just to better understand the mind of an author. It is for this reason I can give sympathetic smiles when people repeatedly ask Selebus "why didn't you make X character do Y?" and he can only say "I can't!". Although this is no grand conclusion, it does not take much experience or awareness of the process of creation to determine that authors end up having characters branch out in their head like independent beings who speak and act on their own as we simply narrate the result. To "just have a character do X" would be a violation of their autonomy most authors would strive to avoid; the questions here likely are unaware that it is precisely stories where authors treat characters like dolls to play which they would end up disliking for their shallowness. P.S. that allegory was deployed purposefully.

Finally, is thinking a lot. This sounds pretentious on the face of it so I will allow a moment to pause and sneer. Ok, moving on. The most important thing of all is to never stop thinking. Philosophy comes from the Greek words philos (love) and sophia (wisdom), meaning "a love for wisdom." It is through a love for wisdom (in some senses: a devotion to finding the truth) that we are encouraged to never stop thinking. We can say in many cases philosophy is merely continuing to think about questions we asked as children before discarding: what is a man, what does it mean to live, why are we here, etc. The key is to never stop thinking. This applies to media as well. There is forever a temptation to write something off as soon as we reach a conclusion, satisfied with the answer we have found - "ah, this boss is really hard and I keep dying, it must be unfair. case closed." or "Ah, this poem was dull on a first read, it must suck. case closed" Etc. Shallow thinking so often lets us reach immediate, but incorrect, conclusions, and we want not to be fooled by them. One's media comprehension will be greatly diminished if one always accepts easy answers.

Anyway, that's a lot of scattered thoughts, but perhaps some might be useful. In the end trying to engage with media on this level is only important for those who devote themselves to media; as for myself, it's my job (partially) but also I don't do anything all day but read books and F95 so there's not much else to do but try to do it as faithfully as I can. Goethe stated that it was the eternal feminine that draws us up high, but I would posit that media itself draws us up high if we allow it.

skwada said:
re: people taking things at face value, yeah I agree with you that it'd be better for it to not be the case but in the end it is the status quo because it is pragmatic. If you take the biological perspective, this is a byproduct of the human species evolving to survive in environments where quick, low-effort decisions based on superficial facts tend to lead to good outcomes more often than not (which is exactly what evolution optimizes for)

re: media literacy, thanks for sharing your thoughts. I remember reading a factoid that humans tend to perform better in pretty much anything when they are being intentional about it rather than just mindlessly going with the flow, which seems to align with what you're saying. Personally, I find it hard to muster up the willpower to do that though. At least when I'm reading classics, I can justify it on the basis that "this is a work which is widely regarded as being worth the effort of properly digesting" but when it comes to random shit on the internet, I just can't do that it mainly comes down to laziness and not being sufficiently invested rather than being a flaw of the works though

I'm curious: have you ever considered making a visual novel of your own? Imo writing is the main obstacle (renders are mainly a matter of putting in the time to get them lookin good) but you seem to have got that covered
Click to expand...
Truly our evolutionary history continues to weigh us down forever.

"Mustering up the willpower" is pretty rough indeed, especially when we're all on a biological time limit and are GOING TO FUCKING DIE ONE DAY!!!!!!!!!! We have to really choose what we do with our time wisely, which is why right now I'm choosing to spend mine with those I cherish above all else. I think, indeed, just out of practicality we will need to pick our battles with media and deploy full literary analysis only on those which earn it or have good reputations as you say. I think the one thing though is that it is often good to acknowledge one's personality responsibility in these cases and hold off being too critical. For example, I chose not to read John Galt's like 200 fucking page radio speech in Atlas Shrugged, but I acknowledge that was a failing of my patience and investment moreso than I decry the very idea of having a 200 page radio speech. It's like playing a game on easy mode then criticizing it for being easy: we make the beds we lie in. That said, this is just a personal philosophy, not an objectively correct way of life which I would lambast others for not following; again, it's ourselves who serve to benefit by uplifting media. Maya's referencing Noriko in that dialogue though. That's how she references Noriko at that point in time.
As it has been pointed out, Akira hadn't met Maya by the time Kyoto happens. Mind you, in Kyoto, Ami hasn't been born, it would be insane for Akira to already be in a relationship with Maya.

Also, Maya's rival is and always will be Noriko, that's because she loses by default against Niki and Sekai. She knows about them, but Akira's allegiance to her was never tested, that's Maya's greatest fear.

She knows that she's a replacement for Sekai, as in, she only has a place because Sekai is dead. And she also knows that Niki would win if Akira had her in his life, that's why she's terrified to the point of making Akira not even mention her name to her (and probably why she had a hand in making sure they stayed apart).

That's of course original Maya, Maya Prime wins against both Sekai and Niki, multiple times at that (including last update version of episcopalis). But that's also maybe due to the fact that our Akira is a product of the current cycle, and thus, to him, Maya Prime is his first love sort of, even if he recovers his memories as time goes on, her impression on him as he "woke up" makes him see his own past in a different way from if he remembered things from the start.

On a minor note, True Sekai doesn't seem to have known Maya, and I think Ghost Sekai's hatred of her is born from the same place as Ami's, Maya took their place on the cycles by accident. From that point of view, it is possible that they have met, if Maya's existence somehow involved her going back into a past where she didn't exist and changing things to what they are now. But yeah, there's not enough at the moment to support this much further. Niki seems to know Maya though, and Ami recalls a playdate with some girl. Imo those are probably references to the timeline change from when Maya inserted herself into the past (supported by the fact Maya can't recall her own parents), but we'll have to wait and see.

Edit: Added images.
Edit2: Mind you, when Noriko shows up, the real foreshadowing is Ami knowing the exact same about it being a corruption of the timeline. (or maybe it wasn't but retcon works I guess)

And she also knows that Niki would win if Akira had her in his life, that's why she's terrified to the point of making Akira not even mention her name to her (and probably why she had a hand in making sure they stayed apart).
That's of course original Maya, Maya Prime wins against both Sekai and Niki, multiple times at that (including last update version of episcopalis). But that's also maybe due to the fact that our Akira is a product of the current cycle, and thus, to him, Maya Prime is his first love sort of, even if he recovers his memories as time goes on, her impression on him as he "woke up" makes him see his own past in a different way from if he remembered things from the start.
On a minor note, True Sekai doesn't seem to have known Maya, and I think Ghost Sekai's hatred of her is born from the same place as Ami's, Maya took their place on the cycles by accident. From that point of view, it is possible that they have met, if Maya's existence somehow involved her going back into a past where she didn't exist and changing things to what they are now. But yeah, there's not enough at the moment to support this much further. Niki seems to know Maya though, and Ami recalls a playdate with some girl. Imo those are probably references to the timeline change from when Maya inserted herself into the past (supported by the fact Maya can't recall her own parents), but we'll have to wait and see.
Edit: Added images.
Edit2: Mind you, when Noriko shows up, the real foreshadowing is Ami knowing the exact same about it being a corruption of the timeline. (or maybe it wasn't but retcon works I guess)
