I planned to take a quick look at an alternate explanation for Ami's assault of Maya in "Right as Rain", but I ended up finding so much stuff to talk about that I've written another very long post. Here's what I think can be concluded directly from the evidence:
  • The scene does not take place in the main timeline.
  • The way Ami acts in the event is basically a carbon copy of Sekai, and Sel intends for the reader to make this connection.
  • Based on the narration, the entity responsible for Maya's time-hopping visions is probably Pareidolia and/or Sekai.
  • In "The Scary Room" Maya is probably shown pictures of being raped, but these pictures include a woman/girl who Maya doesn't instantly recognize (i.e. not Ami). It's also likely that the pictures show a younger Maya.
Individually, none of these points make it impossible that "Right as Rain" shows a real event where Maya was raped by Ami, but each one makes it less and less likely. Instead, I'll tentatively propose a theory that could tie these ideas together:

During the reset Pareidolia and/or Sekai force New Maya to experience nightmares based off of corrupted memories. In the real memory that "Right as Rain" is based on, Maya was still a wizard and was assaulted by Sekai rather than Ami. In "The Scary Room" Pareidolia showed Maya Prime pictures of that real rape by Sekai.

I have to admit, I started from the position of wanting to disprove the reality of this event because I think it would be bad for the story if it turns out that this is a true depiction of Ami Prime. If she's always been an uncaring sadist with full knowledge of the resets and the ability to force a new world, it devalues all of her old events. Suddenly all of her character development, her vulnerabilities, her relationships with her friends at both their highs and lows, even her tender moments with Sensei would be thrown out the window because it was all just an act. I don't want a story where "Della" was just a calculated ploy, not a young girl's insecurities piling up with a traumatic past, causing her to finally break - a break that causes her to hurt herself, not (intentionally) anyone else. Basically, if this is the real Ami Prime, it will feel like a complex character has been replaced with a plot contrivance.

Furthermore, it felt like this event came out of nowhere. Yes, we've seen evidence that Ami knows more about the resets than she lets on, we've seen evidence of her putting on an act and being a master manipulator, we've even seen evidence that she could go psycho and start murdering (for the record, I still think Ami Prime's psycho threats were just an act and will never be realized - in Himawari we trust). What we haven't seen (unless I'm forgetting something) is any hint that she's a sexual sadist, or that her friendship and love for Maya was not just a lie, but covering up a deep-seated hatred. In fact, we've never seen Ami Prime cause intentional physical harm to any other character - her MO is implied threats and psychological manipulation. It's quite a leap for her to suddenly rape her "best friend".
As the narrator points out, in "Right as Rain" Maya has her winter hairstyle, which she hasn't worn since Chapter 2. This is the same hairstyle that she had in her initial time-hopping scenes in this update, as well as in the original "The Scary Room".
If this scene was taking place after Maya "wakes up" and returns to the main timeline, then she should have the haircut from her Chapter 4 Halloween costume.

(bonus sad foreshadowing)
Since the narrator points it out, the hairstyle is not a mistake or meaningless. In order for this to be a real main timeline scene Ami would have had to re-style the passed-out Maya's hair and the narrator would have had to point out the changed hair purely as a red herring. I'm going to rule out this possibility as too far-fetched of a decision for Sel to make.

If the scene isn't happening in the main timeline, maybe it's a real memory from some reset predating Maya Prime. While I can't rule that out entirely, we know of no reason that Ami would have ever had short hair and her Chapter 4 Halloween costume at the same point in time that Maya had her winter hairstyle.

Much more likely is that this is a hallucination or corrupted memory. We saw the possibility of this in Maya's last event, where one of her memories of Sensei is corrupted with a fake Sensei. Maya thinks the nightmares have ended when she's back with Ami, but it's just one more vision in the chain. As "Ami" admits, these visions aren't true memories.

...
There are some very obvious parallels between what Ami does to Maya and what Sekai did to Tsuneyo in the last update. In both events, the victim is stripped naked, restrained, and forced to orgasm against their will. Ami and Sekai degrade their victims in the same way and both refer to raping them as playing with a toy.

...
Ami says that only she's real and everyone else are just tools. According to Akira, Sekai acted similarly while she was alive.
Tsuneyo even seems to be a stand-in for Maya in her event: she's tied to the base of the cross where AmIOkay was crucified in "The Letter T", which was symbolic of how Akira's abuse of Maya continued the cycle of his own abuse by Sekai. A blurred-out Maya also stands to the side as Tsuneyo is molested, representing that Tsuneyo has taken her place.

Ami also visually resembles Sekai, as they both repeatedly smile in the same creepy way.
If you look through past Ami events, she basically never smiles like this, but it's something that Sekai does often. For example:
Sel has even signified Sekai's presence before by having other characters smile in the same way: Akira during Sekai's restoration and Yasu when Sekai speaks through her in "The Art of Drowning".
Although I can't point to anything conclusive, I also think the way Ami talks in "Right as Rain" is very reminiscent of Sekai, with a mixture of condescension, sarcastic teasing, and especially her disdain/vitriol for Maya in particular.

One more hint I might be misinterpreting: Ami accuses Maya of playing with her toy(s) when she's not home. As fun as it is to think of Maya going to town with Ami's vibrator collection, I think this is probably about having sex with Sensei given the earlier "toy" references. If so, it's far more likely that Sekai would refer to Sensei as her toy than that Ami would.
First, I want to remind everyone that while Ami prepared Maya's scary room in Chapter 2, the pictures themselves might be from Pareidolia since he shows up in the event to redact the contents, to talk to us (that's his smiley), and to fake a factory reset while pretending to be Wires.

...

...
A countdown with nonsensical entries is a signature of his, for example when he wakes up SeKaori in "Run, Rabbit, Run".
You might be thinking that Pareidolia is gone so he can't be involved with "Right as Rain", but I'm pretty sure if actually went anywhere, he's already back. This will be a subject for a future post, but clues suggest the New Hope is either just Pareidolia or a combination of the trinity with Pareidolia in control.

At the end of "Right as Rain" a seemingly new entity shows up as the narrator. They identify themselves as "the ghost of better days" while we're shown a picture of Jesus on the cross. The "better days" ties back to "The Scary Room" where Pareidolia and the angels both use that phrase.
I see two possibilities here:
  • Sekai often calls herself a ghost, was alive in better days, and has shown up with the Jesus picture before because of the letter T connection.
  • Pareidolia/god is a ghost because he has returned from non-existence. Outside of "The Scary Room" Pareidolia has also used "better days" to describe Akira's youth. And the Jesus picture is used because of the connection between the trinity and the cross.
This entity tells us that Ami and Maya "died" and in fact never existed. This is probably another hint that the event and this Ami are an illusion, since the girls are still around a bit later in "God of Light". Furthermore, the entity claims that it and Sensei are the only real people, echoing Ami's claim that she's real and everyone else is just a tool. This could mean that the entity is the one pretending to be Ami (and Sensei in the previous event).

One of the things Big P said in "The Scary Room" was that Maya could be seeing memories, the future, or a dream. The same options are twice used to describe what New Maya sees during her time-hopping.
In the middle of one of her hops (before the wizard & Sensei scene) we're shown images that suggest the presence of a god who ostensibly includes the whole trinity.
Its command to obey is later echoed by Ami.

...
Moonflare pointed out that "Right as Rain" is meant to show the origins of (at least some of) the pictures that Maya Prime was shown in "The Scary Room". We finally have an explanation for what was previously a mysterious line: one of the angels pervs out over slides showing Maya "in the chair".
So it definitely seems like Maya is shown pictures of when she was tied to the chair and raped. But there's a couple of reasons to think that it's not Ami raping her. For one, there's someone in the images that Maya thinks she knows but she isn't positive - even with short hair, Ami would be instantly recognized by Maya Prime.
In addition, I think Big P's reference to "better days" places the pictures before the resets, especially given his other uses of that phrase to evoke youthful nostalgia. The angels also comment on Maya's youth in the pictures. I think it's likely that they show a Maya that is physically younger than Maya Prime.

"Mysterious Abundance of Chickens":
One last possible hint: Maya says "there shouldn't be any left" while talking about the mystery woman. She might be saying there should be no photographs of this person at all, and it occurs to me that it's very strange that Sensei and in particular Ami don't have a single picture of Sekai anywhere in their house. This could also fit with my idea that Sekai is the girl in Futaba's ghost story, because the people are mysteriously missing from all of the girl's pictures.
Here's a qyestion: does Maya start acting differently around Ami after "The Scary Room"? Next time someone does a replay of Chapter 2, this would be an interesting thing to look for.
The correspondences between Ami and Sekai can be explained in a few different ways:
  1. Sekai is pretending to be Ami in a nightmare.
  2. The event is physically happening, but Sekai is possessing Ami.
  3. Selebus is just playing with the idea of events repeating themselves, and wants to show that Ami's true personality is remarkably like her mother's.
I tend to discount #3 because while Selebus has done things like this in the past, it's never been to this degree of specificity. The clues about the fake timeline make #2 less likely. When we then consider that New Maya is being shown things by Sekai and/or her bff Pareidolia, it further reinforces the idea that #1 is the most likely option.

Even in a vacuum, I think Sekai makes the most sense for the identity of the mystery woman in the scary room pictures. Maya probably saw pictures of her or even met her, but it was millennia ago as far as Maya Prime was concerned, so there's a good chance she doesn't remember what Sekai looks like - but given the resemblance to Ami and her knowledge of Akira's past, she can certainly make an educated guess.

In theory, if the rape happened before the resets both Maya Prime and New Maya should remember it, but New Maya obviously doesn't recognize the circumstances of the rape, and from her reactions I don't think Maya Prime remembers the circumstances of the scary room pictures. However, we conveniently learned in this update that Alt Maya Prime has forgotten large swathes of her past, no version of Maya has ever remembered her full past, and New Maya isn't certain how her relationship with Sensei began. It's extremely plausible that Maya has repressed this memory or been supernaturally forced to forget it.

...

...
It's hard to establish a motive for "Right as Rain" before we learn how much Maya (or even Ami) remembers of it after the reset, but Ami's claim that she wants to show the pictures to Sensei as part of their seduction really makes no sense. While such a plan might work in the short term, it would also shatter Sensei's illusion of Ami as the innocent little girl whom he must protect due to her post-traumatic fragility, which ultimately would lead to him drifting further away from her.

The other offered motive is the pure pleasure she gets from dominating Maya. Again, we have no evidence that Ami is a sexual sadist, but Sekai certainly is. We have no evidence that Ami hates Maya and wants her to suffer, but both Sekai and Pareidolia loathe her. I can see Sekai delighting in torturing Maya while taking extra pleasure from pretending to be Ami, both to trick Maya into thinking that the event is real and to inflict extra psychological pain by making her think that she was betrayed by her best friend.

"Sekai raped wizard Maya" was the best theory I could come up with to explain the evidence, but it's still just an educated guess. What I am confident about is that "Right as Rain" is fake and Sekai is heavily involved.

spoilers.title: The narrator and the nightmares
spoilers.html:
First, I want to remind everyone that while Ami prepared Maya's scary room in Chapter 2, the pictures themselves might be from Pareidolia since he shows up in the event to redact the contents, to talk to us (that's his smiley), and to fake a factory reset while pretending to be Wires.

...

...
A countdown with nonsensical entries is a signature of his, for example when he wakes up SeKaori in "Run, Rabbit, Run".
You might be thinking that Pareidolia is gone so he can't be involved with "Right as Rain", but I'm pretty sure if actually went anywhere, he's already back. This will be a subject for a future post, but clues suggest the New Hope is either just Pareidolia or a combination of the trinity with Pareidolia in control.

At the end of "Right as Rain" a seemingly new entity shows up as the narrator. They identify themselves as "the ghost of better days" while we're shown a picture of Jesus on the cross. The "better days" ties back to "The Scary Room" where Pareidolia and the angels both use that phrase.
I see two possibilities here:
  • Sekai often calls herself a ghost, was alive in better days, and has shown up with the Jesus picture before because of the letter T connection.
  • Pareidolia/god is a ghost because he has returned from non-existence. Outside of "The Scary Room" Pareidolia has also used "better days" to describe Akira's youth. And the Jesus picture is used because of the connection between the trinity and the cross.
This entity tells us that Ami and Maya "died" and in fact never existed. This is probably another hint that the event and this Ami are an illusion, since the girls are still around a bit later in "God of Light". Furthermore, the entity claims that it and Sensei are the only real people, echoing Ami's claim that she's real and everyone else is just a tool. This could mean that the entity is the one pretending to be Ami (and Sensei in the previous event).

One of the things Big P said in "The Scary Room" was that Maya could be seeing memories, the future, or a dream. The same options are twice used to describe what New Maya sees during her time-hopping.
In the middle of one of her hops (before the wizard & Sensei scene) we're shown images that suggest the presence of a god who ostensibly includes the whole trinity.
Its command to obey is later echoed by Ami.

spoilers.title: The scary room pictures
spoilers.html:
Moonflare pointed out that "Right as Rain" is meant to show the origins of (at least some of) the pictures that Maya Prime was shown in "The Scary Room". We finally have an explanation for what was previously a mysterious line: one of the angels pervs out over slides showing Maya "in the chair".
So it definitely seems like Maya is shown pictures of when she was tied to the chair and raped. But there's a couple of reasons to think that it's not Ami raping her. For one, there's someone in the images that Maya thinks she knows but she isn't positive - even with short hair, Ami would be instantly recognized by Maya Prime.
In addition, I think Big P's reference to "better days" places the pictures before the resets, especially given his other uses of that phrase to evoke youthful nostalgia. The angels also comment on Maya's youth in the pictures. I think it's likely that they show a Maya that is physically younger than Maya Prime.

spoilers.title: Conclusion
spoilers.html:
The correspondences between Ami and Sekai can be explained in a few different ways:
  1. Sekai is pretending to be Ami in a nightmare.
  2. The event is physically happening, but Sekai is possessing Ami.
  3. Selebus is just playing with the idea of events repeating themselves, and wants to show that Ami's true personality is remarkably like her mother's.
I tend to discount #3 because while Selebus has done things like this in the past, it's never been to this degree of specificity. The clues about the fake timeline make #2 less likely. When we then consider that New Maya is being shown things by Sekai and/or her bff Pareidolia, it further reinforces the idea that #1 is the most likely option.

Even in a vacuum, I think Sekai makes the most sense for the identity of the mystery woman in the scary room pictures. Maya probably saw pictures of her or even met her, but it was millennia ago as far as Maya Prime was concerned, so there's a good chance she doesn't remember what Sekai looks like - but given the resemblance to Ami and her knowledge of Akira's past, she can certainly make an educated guess.

In theory, if the rape happened before the resets both Maya Prime and New Maya should remember it, but New Maya obviously doesn't recognize the circumstances of the rape, and from her reactions I don't think Maya Prime remembers the circumstances of the scary room pictures. However, we conveniently learned in this update that Alt Maya Prime has forgotten large swathes of her past, no version of Maya has ever remembered her full past, and New Maya isn't certain how her relationship with Sensei began. It's extremely plausible that Maya has repressed this memory or been supernaturally forced to forget it.

...

...
It's hard to establish a motive for "Right as Rain" before we learn how much Maya (or even Ami) remembers of it after the reset, but Ami's claim that she wants to show the pictures to Sensei as part of their seduction really makes no sense. While such a plan might work in the short term, it would also shatter Sensei's illusion of Ami as the innocent little girl whom he must protect due to her post-traumatic fragility, which ultimately would lead to him drifting further away from her.

The other offered motive is the pure pleasure she gets from dominating Maya. Again, we have no evidence that Ami is a sexual sadist, but Sekai certainly is. We have no evidence that Ami hates Maya and wants her to suffer, but both Sekai and Pareidolia loathe her. I can see Sekai delighting in torturing Maya while taking extra pleasure from pretending to be Ami, both to trick Maya into thinking that the event is real and to inflict extra psychological pain by making her think that she was betrayed by her best friend.

"Sekai raped wizard Maya" was the best theory I could come up with to explain the evidence, but it's still just an educated guess. What I am confident about is that "Right as Rain" is fake and Sekai is heavily involved.

Ok so here is the rest of the somewhat outlandish stuff that has come to mind that I said I would write out. it seems I have timed it after another big post that is perhaps tangentially connected. Unfortunately I'm terrible at structuring writing so I hope it's not too unreadable. And I can't say that much of what's in here is anything more than mostly unfounded speculation based on cherry picked bits of information, that I'll be quite happy to find out is overall completely wrong. I'm just interested if any of it will even be in the same postcode as whatever we learn in the future.
We had to find the 4 orbs in a sensei quest to summon the big orb and sometimes characters, mostly(or only?) just Ami, show up with more realistic eyes. Which you maybe could describe as somewhat “Orb” like. And after the orb fight a set of images flash including “Breed your Nice minigame Ami” who has the “Orb” like realistic eyes and also Meowri/Kaori who appears to have “orb” like eyes albeit in a pixel art style. Now we are missing a green Maya/Nao-chan colour one so perhaps it's not as clear of a connection as it could be. But i'll ignore the other characters “Orb eyes” for now because the more direct connection I can see is that one of the Orbs was simply named the “Red Orb” and That combined with the “Breed your Nice Ami” image flash plus the fact that we have many times now seen “Ami” and “Ami” based strange creatures, with those realistic “Red Orb” eyes leads me to a pretty clear connection between Ami/s and the “Red Orb”. Even if there is nothing in this connection of “Red Orb” and the red realistic eyes I can't ignore the “Breed your Nice Minigame Ami” image flashing after the “Orb” fight. There must be something to that at least.




But again it's another unclear connection that doesn't seem to lead anywhere that would provide any clarity. Only more vague god stuff, 4 orbs to make 1 God Orb, The trinity of four, etc. Additional vague hints that Ami was more than she seemed. (Which I guess was in some ways confirmed in this reset). And possibly some kind of through line between; the strange Ami’s, the “Red Orb” and the “God Orb”. I'm tempted to throw the “Old One” Into that through line as well. But then I think I'm starting to read too much from too little and I'd rather not draw connections before they become apparent lest it stops me from seeing what's there when more clear information becomes available. But I have unfortunately already drawn some connections so I'll give you the rest of this collection of my clumsily constructed curious contrivances.

I feel like rethinking the section in “All For You”(Chapter 3 main) that talks about the thing that “sings in its sleep”. That was disconnected from the orb that's meant to move it - that wanted to find a new resting place and stay hidden - To form a form of force that will form a fourth form forced outforth before the fourth can form its course - etc. I think some of us thought it was Sekai/her ghost, I know I lent more towards that at the time (I don't fully remember the specifics of why). But perhaps instead of that, it was the Old One and our Ami’s place was the new resting place/ host/ hole? It could be that It replaced our Ami when we saw a Ami killed in the last reset, Or perhaps it is just influencing her or became a part of her/ merged with her. We saw Ami talking to something we could not see in one event while she was looking after Akira towards the start of chapter 4 for example.


Now taking a large leap of logic I end up at a strange thought that perhaps in a similar way to Akira creating the God Pareidolia. Perhaps Ami or Ami’s have unintentionally started the creation of a god. Maybe out of a particularly long lived long lost Ami. And that said Ami could just maybe also be the Old One. I guess we will see what happens with User4 in the future. Now there is basically no clear evidence I can provide for these thoughts. Only some extremely loose fighting stuff from "Priestess of Fallen Snow"(chapter 4 main v39) and what pareidolia told us last update about how gods come to exist. As i said it's a pretty small and contrived link but here it is:

Yasu goes off on a Yasu rant and says:
“Spiderwebs, A calendar. The ones you keep inside.
A god. A bucket. Heresy. A man who almost died.
A ghost. A moon. She's lying. There's nowhere we can hide.
We're Done. We're doomed. We're dying. The well has nearly dried.”

Then she says a bunch of hex which I have translated but whatever contextual meaning is in it is lost on me. At Least in regards to anyway it would relate to what I'm rambling on about so I'll just ignore It for now. After the hex the same song from “All For You” when the thing “that sings in its sleep” is introduced starts playing and Yasu says “Have…to warn…him! Have…to save…The lamb!”

To me it seems to be quite clearly talking about Ami looking after Akira post reset. But Ami is never clearly mentioned while everything else that happens seems to be. Some of those things are:
  • “A moon” (Goodnight moon?)
  • “A ghost” (Sekais ghost)
  • “A bucket”
  • “A man who almost died” (Akira)
  • “The ones you keep inside” (could be the gods in Akiras head, could be something else)
  • “A god” (Singular…Perhaps it's Pareidolia, But Perhaps it's Ami or something that is influencing Ami… whatever Ami was talking to that we could not see maybe… Could it be the Old One?),
  • “She’s lying” (Ami is lying… but She was not directly mentioned…So… Is She now a God that is lying?)
  • “There's nowhere we can hide. We're Done. We're doomed. We're dying.” (Perhaps it's Old One/Ancient Ami that has come to reshape this Terminal to suit her needs. Perhaps summoned to Terminal 23 by our Ami, Unintentionally or otherwise.)
  • “The well has nearly dried.” ( I'm not sure about this, or the other things mentioned.).




When he shall die, take him and cut him out in little stars and he will make the face of heaven so fine that all the world will be in love with night and pay no worship to the garish sun.
LINE BREAK
go unto them and make them believe, but make them trust you first
cursed be those gentiles lest they destroy the world we have built
from atop this roof i speak to you, o messenger . o child.
you are permanent and perfect. I am rabid and reviled.
Now obviously that's all extremely selective, I'm basically just doing your average conspiracy theorist rearrange everything until it fits your predetermined outcome bit here. I'm probably doing that with all of this post to be honest. But maybe it will point someone towards something else that makes more sense. It could all just be about Sekai’s “ghost”. But when I think about it now I'm not sure why Yasus God would suddenly be so worried about Sekai when I'm pretty sure she had already been showing up for a while at this point.

Which leads me to another excessive rearrangement to fit my conspiracy. “The Girl with broken wings”... It's pretty clear this is a pen name Ami is using for her poems. I don't actually remember if it's ever mentioned on her in-universe poems, (the ones she handed in to the poetry contest for example). Or if it's only shown with some of the poems presented directly to the player. I think it might be the latter. And what's interesting is there are other poems, clearly written by an Ami, that are presented directly to the player but do not include the pen name “The Girl with broken wings”. Making me think a specific and different Ami wrote these ones.
I don't remember where this was from it was in my pile of screenshots. It might have been last Halloween reset if the date on the file was anything to go by.


I was going to look for the rest of them but I didn't have the patience for it. There are also 2 in the latest update. One of them I will talk about next.
“The Girl with broken wings” is also a bit of a strange name is it not. Broken wings implies that there was something significant she could once do that she no longer can. The “Old One” was said to be trapped in a different world (in an image from the Noriko event “I really want to stay at your house”). Perhaps it used to be able to travel between them. Perhaps you could say that it has broken wings…

The blue text in this also speaks like the "girl with broken wings" & "Narrator Ami" sometimes do; "The girl with the me who is me who is Ami I am Ami" this is from the next poem I will mention and its strangle similar.
There is this poem in the latest update seemingly from “The Girl with broken wings”. It all but confirms the idea that these poems are written by an Ami. But crucially it doesn't really seem like it is our Ami (or at least the Ami we think we know) that wrote it. Based on that last paragraph.

somewhere its close/ somewhere it's far

it matches my eyes/ that same shade of red

if the memories fade/ why not keep them inside?

our feet touch the sand/ our hearts touch the sun

But only if you can/ forget everything
if you promise me that/ i'll repair these old wings

And we'll fly off together to a place no one can reach us
THIS IS SUPPOSED TO BE MY STORY

The 2nd one though is where I am reminded of the biggest problem with this whole line of thought. Simply because it makes me think of Sekai. And that is simply that this line of thought would nullify Sekais obvious importance in the direction Ami was going. Saying The “Old One” is an Ancient Ami that replaced Ami seemingly completely ignores Sekai which would be a clear mistake to make. But at the same time If Our Ami is the one that has survived billions of years. Why would Sekai and Sekai’s poetry now suddenly affect her so much? Surely she would have already encountered it. Already encountered Sekai even. There is something we are missing there. Something not quite right with this Ancient Ami Old One Idea. Something not quite right with Our Ami having survived billions of years. And something not quite right with how Sekai fits into this. I wonder if the answer lies somewhere with the Narrator Ami and User4.

Let's say Narrator ami, “The Girl with broken wings”, The Billion year old Ami, and “The Old One” are the same thing or closely connected. Could Sekai, Her poetry and her “ghost”, have awoken our Ami to the world in some way further than she may already have been. Some way that eventually summoned “Narrator Ami”/“The Girl with broken wings”/”The Old One” out of whatever world it was trapped in and into Terminal 23. And then in some way akin to Akira creating Pareidolia Ami has now turned them into a new God That will become User4. Perhaps it can and has been possessing Ami in the same way Pareidolia appeared to possess Akira. Could that explain Ami sometimes knowing way too much lately. And her flip flopping schizophrenic acting skills. Sometimes it's our Ami And Sometimes it's this new God… This is also not to say that our Ami never knew anything about the nature of the world before this stuff influenced her. She seemed like she might have to be honest. But after this influence she started to become the Ami we see now. The Ami in the events before the reset, “Prince” Ami, "Right as Rain" Ami, etc.

The other Questions I have but can't think about now after writing all this bullshit is; in what way is the Ima/Nao thing that looks like Ami fitting into this, what about Nao-chan, Kaori, Himawari, the 4 Ami’s from last Halloween and a whole bunch of other stuff.

In the end I'm sure I could conjure more connections; more through lines, do some more painting by numbers with numbers that I wrote in. But at that point I would just be looking for “pepe silvia”, if I wasn't doing that already with the entirety of this post. And I don't particularly like doing that because you end up way too invested in your own head canon and become resistant to reading anything in the text in front of you that might contradict it, regardless of how obvious that contradiction might be. So I will just stop here. Along with that, this is now far too long. And I don't have the patience now to go back over this and improve the structure. So imagine how bad it will become if I keep adding to it with everything that comes to mind while writing it.

Actually I lied. I just played some of the new generic events and the Ami ones specifically are quite strange. So they might be somewhat relevant to this whole mess of a post. You have the meat mall when you call her mid day. The call her at night event is extremely strange (the strangest of all of them maybe) and you get 17 affection points at the end of it. The invite over hang out event seems to be in some strange void space despite it saying it's ami’s room. And in the maid cafe one he can't stop saying how cute ami is to an excessive degree (idk maybe that one is normal…).
spoilers.text:

Which you maybe could describe as somewhat “Orb” like. And after the orb fight a set of images flash including “Breed your Nice minigame Ami” who has the “Orb” like realistic eyes and also Meowri/Kaori who appears to have “orb” like eyes albeit in a pixel art style. Now we are missing a green Maya/Nao-chan colour one so perhaps it's not as clear of a connection as it could be. But i'll ignore the other characters “Orb eyes” for now because the more direct connection I can see is that one of the Orbs was simply named the “Red Orb” and That combined with the “Breed your Nice Ami” image flash plus the fact that we have many times now seen “Ami” and “Ami” based strange creatures, with those realistic “Red Orb” eyes leads me to a pretty clear connection between Ami/s and the “Red Orb”. Even if there is nothing in this connection of “Red Orb” and the red realistic eyes I can't ignore the “Breed your Nice Minigame Ami” image flashing after the “Orb” fight. There must be something to that at least.

Orb images
But again it's another unclear connection that doesn't seem to lead anywhere that would provide any clarity. Only more vague god stuff, 4 orbs to make 1 God Orb, The trinity of four, etc. Additional vague hints that Ami was more than she seemed. (Which I guess was in some ways confirmed in this reset). And possibly some kind of through line between; the strange Ami’s, the “Red Orb” and the “God Orb”. I'm tempted to throw the “Old One” Into that through line as well. But perhaps instead of that, it was the Old One and our Ami’s place was the new resting place/ host/ hole? It could be that It replaced our Ami when we saw a Ami killed in the last reset, Or perhaps it is just influencing her or became a part of her/ merged with her. We saw Ami talking to something we could not see in one event while she was looking after Akira towards the start of chapter 4 for example.

it sings in its sleep.

Perhaps Ami or Ami’s have unintentionally started the creation of a god. Maybe out of a particularly long lived long lost Ami. And that said Ami could just maybe also be the Old One. I guess we will see what happens with User4 in the future. Now there is basically no clear evidence I can provide for these thoughts. Yasu goes off on a Yasu rant and says:
“Spiderwebs, A calendar. The ones you keep inside.
A god. A bucket. Heresy. A man who almost died.
A ghost. A moon. She's lying. There's nowhere we can hide.
We're Done. We're doomed. We're dying. The well has nearly dried.”
Then she says a bunch of hex which I have translated but whatever contextual meaning is in it is lost on me. At Least in regards to anyway it would relate to what I'm rambling on about so I'll just ignore It for now. After the hex the same song from “All For You” when the thing “that sings in its sleep” is introduced starts playing and Yasu says “Have…to warn…him! Have…to save…The lamb!”
To me it seems to be quite clearly talking about Ami looking after Akira post reset. But Ami is never clearly mentioned while everything else that happens seems to be. Some of those things are:
“A moon” (Goodnight moon?)
“A ghost” (Sekais ghost)
“A bucket”
“A man who almost died” (Akira)
“The ones you keep inside” (could be the gods in Akiras head, could be something else)
“A god” (Singular…Perhaps it's Pareidolia, But Perhaps it's Ami or something that is influencing Ami… whatever Ami was talking to that we could not see maybe… Could it be the Old One?),
“She’s lying” (Ami is lying… but She was not directly mentioned…So… Is She now a God that is lying?)
“There's nowhere we can hide. We're Done. We're doomed. We're dying.” (Perhaps it's Old One/Ancient Ami that has come to reshape this Terminal to suit her needs. Perhaps summoned to Terminal 23 by our Ami, Unintentionally or otherwise.)

aramaug said:
I planned to take a quick look at an alternate explanation for Ami's assault of Maya in "Right as Rain", but I ended up finding so much stuff to talk about that I've written another very long post. Here's what I think can be concluded directly from the evidence:
  • The scene does not take place in the main timeline.
  • The way Ami acts in the event is basically a carbon copy of Sekai, and Sel intends for the reader to make this connection.
  • Based on the narration, the entity responsible for Maya's time-hopping visions is probably Pareidolia and/or Sekai.
  • In "The Scary Room" Maya is probably shown pictures of being raped, but these pictures include a woman/girl who Maya doesn't instantly recognize (i.e. not Ami). It's also likely that the pictures show a younger Maya.
Individually, none of these points make it impossible that "Right as Rain" shows a real event where Maya was raped by Ami, but each one makes it less and less likely. Instead, I'll tentatively propose a theory that could tie these ideas together:

During the reset Pareidolia and/or Sekai force New Maya to experience nightmares based off of corrupted memories. In the real memory that "Right as Rain" is based on, Maya was still a wizard and was assaulted by Sekai rather than Ami. In "The Scary Room" Pareidolia showed Maya Prime pictures of that real rape by Sekai.

I have to admit, I started from the position of wanting to disprove the reality of this event because I think it would be bad for the story if it turns out that this is a true depiction of Ami Prime. If she's always been an uncaring sadist with full knowledge of the resets and the ability to force a new world, it devalues all of her old events. Suddenly all of her character development, her vulnerabilities, her relationships with her friends at both their highs and lows, even her tender moments with Sensei would be thrown out the window because it was all just an act. I don't want a story where "Della" was just a calculated ploy, not a young girl's insecurities piling up with a traumatic past, causing her to finally break - a break that causes her to hurt herself, not (intentionally) anyone else. Basically, if this is the real Ami Prime, it will feel like a complex character has been replaced with a plot contrivance.

Furthermore, it felt like this event came out of nowhere. Yes, we've seen evidence that Ami knows more about the resets than she lets on, we've seen evidence of her putting on an act and being a master manipulator, we've even seen evidence that she could go psycho and start murdering (for the record, I still think Ami Prime's psycho threats were just an act and will never be realized - in Himawari we trust). What we haven't seen (unless I'm forgetting something) is any hint that she's a sexual sadist, or that her friendship and love for Maya was not just a lie, but covering up a deep-seated hatred. In fact, we've never seen Ami Prime cause intentional physical harm to any other character - her MO is implied threats and psychological manipulation. It's quite a leap for her to suddenly rape her "best friend".
As the narrator points out, in "Right as Rain" Maya has her winter hairstyle, which she hasn't worn since Chapter 2. This is the same hairstyle that she had in her initial time-hopping scenes in this update, as well as in the original "The Scary Room".

I'm going to rule out this possibility as too far-fetched of a decision for Sel to make.

If the scene isn't happening in the main timeline, maybe it's a real memory from some reset predating Maya Prime. While I can't rule that out entirely, we know of no reason that Ami would have ever had short hair and her Chapter 4 Halloween costume at the same point in time that Maya had her winter hairstyle.

Much more likely is that this is a hallucination or corrupted memory. We saw the possibility of this in Maya's last event, where one of her memories of Sensei is corrupted with a fake Sensei. Maya thinks the nightmares have ended when she's back with Ami, but it's just one more vision in the chain. As "Ami" admits, these visions aren't true memories.

In addition, I think Big P's reference to "better days" places the pictures before the resets, especially given his other uses of that phrase to evoke youthful nostalgia. This could also fit with my idea that Sekai is the girl in Futaba's ghost story, because the people are mysteriously missing from all of the girl's pictures.
View attachment 4211110
Here's a qyestion: does Maya start acting differently around Ami after "The Scary Room"? Next time someone does a replay of Chapter 2, this would be an interesting thing to look for.
The correspondences between Ami and Sekai can be explained in a few different ways:
  1. Sekai is pretending to be Ami in a nightmare.
  2. The event is physically happening, but Sekai is possessing Ami.
  3. Selebus is just playing with the idea of events repeating themselves, and wants to show that Ami's true personality is remarkably like her mother's.
I tend to discount #3 because while Selebus has done things like this in the past, it's never been to this degree of specificity. The clues about the fake timeline make #2 less likely. When we then consider that New Maya is being shown things by Sekai and/or her bff Pareidolia, it further reinforces the idea that #1 is the most likely option.

Even in a vacuum, I think Sekai makes the most sense for the identity of the mystery woman in the scary room pictures. Maya probably saw pictures of her or even met her, but it was millennia ago as far as Maya Prime was concerned, so there's a good chance she doesn't remember what Sekai looks like - but given the resemblance to Ami and her knowledge of Akira's past, she can certainly make an educated guess.

In theory, if the rape happened before the resets both Maya Prime and New Maya should remember it, but New Maya obviously doesn't recognize the circumstances of the rape, and from her reactions I don't think Maya Prime remembers the circumstances of the scary room pictures. However, we conveniently learned in this update that Alt Maya Prime has forgotten large swathes of her past, no version of Maya has ever remembered her full past, and New Maya isn't certain how her relationship with Sensei began. It's extremely plausible that Maya has repressed this memory or been supernaturally forced to forget it.

While such a plan might work in the short term, it would also shatter Sensei's illusion of Ami as the innocent little girl whom he must protect due to her post-traumatic fragility, which ultimately would lead to him drifting further away from her.

The other offered motive is the pure pleasure she gets from dominating Maya. Again, we have no evidence that Ami is a sexual sadist, but Sekai certainly is. We have no evidence that Ami hates Maya and wants her to suffer, but both Sekai and Pareidolia loathe her. I can see Sekai delighting in torturing Maya while taking extra pleasure from pretending to be Ami, both to trick Maya into thinking that the event is real and to inflict extra psychological pain by making her think that she was betrayed by her best friend.

"Sekai raped wizard Maya" was the best theory I could come up with to explain the evidence, but it's still just an educated guess. What I am confident about is that "Right as Rain" is fake and Sekai is heavily involved.

Sekai is pretending to be Ami in a nightmare.

However, we conveniently learned in this update that Alt Maya Prime has forgotten large swathes of her past, no version of Maya has ever remembered her full past, and New Maya isn't certain how her relationship with Sensei began. The other offered motive is the pure pleasure she gets from dominating Maya. Again, we have no evidence that Ami is a sexual sadist, but Sekai certainly is. I can see Sekai delighting in torturing Maya while taking extra pleasure from pretending to be Ami, both to trick Maya into thinking that the event is real and to inflict extra psychological pain by making her think that she was betrayed by her best friend.

spoilers.title: General thoughts
spoilers.html:
I have to admit, I started from the position of wanting to disprove the reality of this event because I think it would be bad for the story if it turns out that this is a true depiction of Ami Prime. If she's always been an uncaring sadist with full knowledge of the resets and the ability to force a new world, it devalues all of her old events. Suddenly all of her character development, her vulnerabilities, her relationships with her friends at both their highs and lows, even her tender moments with Sensei would be thrown out the window because it was all just an act. I don't want a story where "Della" was just a calculated ploy, not a young girl's insecurities piling up with a traumatic past, causing her to finally break - a break that causes her to hurt herself, not (intentionally) anyone else. Basically, if this is the real Ami Prime, it will feel like a complex character has been replaced with a plot contrivance.

Furthermore, it felt like this event came out of nowhere. Yes, we've seen evidence that Ami knows more about the resets than she lets on, we've seen evidence of her putting on an act and being a master manipulator, we've even seen evidence that she could go psycho and start murdering (for the record, I still think Ami Prime's psycho threats were just an act and will never be realized - in Himawari we trust). What we haven't seen (unless I'm forgetting something) is any hint that she's a sexual sadist, or that her friendship and love for Maya was not just a lie, but covering up a deep-seated hatred. In fact, we've never seen Ami Prime cause intentional physical harm to any other character - her MO is implied threats and psychological manipulation. It's quite a leap for her to suddenly rape her "best friend".

spoilers.title: Fake timeline
spoilers.html:
As the narrator points out, in "Right as Rain" Maya has her winter hairstyle, which she hasn't worn since Chapter 2. This is the same hairstyle that she had in her initial time-hopping scenes in this update, as well as in the original "The Scary Room".
View attachment 4210706
If this scene was taking place after Maya "wakes up" and returns to the main timeline, then she should have the haircut from her Chapter 4 Halloween costume.
View attachment 4210707
(bonus sad foreshadowing)
Since the narrator points it out, the hairstyle is not a mistake or meaningless. In order for this to be a real main timeline scene Ami would have had to re-style the passed-out Maya's hair and the narrator would have had to point out the changed hair purely as a red herring. I'm going to rule out this possibility as too far-fetched of a decision for Sel to make.

If the scene isn't happening in the main timeline, maybe it's a real memory from some reset predating Maya Prime. While I can't rule that out entirely, we know of no reason that Ami would have ever had short hair and her Chapter 4 Halloween costume at the same point in time that Maya had her winter hairstyle.

Much more likely is that this is a hallucination or corrupted memory. We saw the possibility of this in Maya's last event, where one of her memories of Sensei is corrupted with a fake Sensei. Maya thinks the nightmares have ended when she's back with Ami, but it's just one more vision in the chain. As "Ami" admits, these visions aren't true memories.

spoilers.title: Conclusion
spoilers.html:
The correspondences between Ami and Sekai can be explained in a few different ways:
  1. Sekai is pretending to be Ami in a nightmare.
  2. The event is physically happening, but Sekai is possessing Ami.
  3. Selebus is just playing with the idea of events repeating themselves, and wants to show that Ami's true personality is remarkably like her mother's.
I tend to discount #3 because while Selebus has done things like this in the past, it's never been to this degree of specificity. The clues about the fake timeline make #2 less likely. When we then consider that New Maya is being shown things by Sekai and/or her bff Pareidolia, it further reinforces the idea that #1 is the most likely option.

Even in a vacuum, I think Sekai makes the most sense for the identity of the mystery woman in the scary room pictures. Maya probably saw pictures of her or even met her, but it was millennia ago as far as Maya Prime was concerned, so there's a good chance she doesn't remember what Sekai looks like - but given the resemblance to Ami and her knowledge of Akira's past, she can certainly make an educated guess.

In theory, if the rape happened before the resets both Maya Prime and New Maya should remember it, but New Maya obviously doesn't recognize the circumstances of the rape, and from her reactions I don't think Maya Prime remembers the circumstances of the scary room pictures. However, we conveniently learned in this update that Alt Maya Prime has forgotten large swathes of her past, no version of Maya has ever remembered her full past, and New Maya isn't certain how her relationship with Sensei began. It's extremely plausible that Maya has repressed this memory or been supernaturally forced to forget it.
View attachment 4211112
...
View attachment 4211114 View attachment 4211115
...
View attachment 4211116
It's hard to establish a motive for "Right as Rain" before we learn how much Maya (or even Ami) remembers of it after the reset, but Ami's claim that she wants to show the pictures to Sensei as part of their seduction really makes no sense. While such a plan might work in the short term, it would also shatter Sensei's illusion of Ami as the innocent little girl whom he must protect due to her post-traumatic fragility, which ultimately would lead to him drifting further away from her.

The other offered motive is the pure pleasure she gets from dominating Maya. Again, we have no evidence that Ami is a sexual sadist, but Sekai certainly is. We have no evidence that Ami hates Maya and wants her to suffer, but both Sekai and Pareidolia loathe her. I can see Sekai delighting in torturing Maya while taking extra pleasure from pretending to be Ami, both to trick Maya into thinking that the event is real and to inflict extra psychological pain by making her think that she was betrayed by her best friend.

"Sekai raped wizard Maya" was the best theory I could come up with to explain the evidence, but it's still just an educated guess. What I am confident about is that "Right as Rain" is fake and Sekai is heavily involved.

So, i've been brooding over commenting on the latest update. And i finished this one rather quick, on nov 2nd.
First, because i think it's a mess.
Then Moonflare, DeanNoriko and Apollo somenumbers, pretty much came up with about 50% of what i would have had to say already.
Now Aramaug kind of added another 40ish%.

I think the update is a mess because, like Apollo said something like "Timetravel in stories is bad" <- Signed.
It adds a whole new big can of worms, if the car crash is part of the cycles. Unless it's countered by a possibility of Ami being capable to create her own Sekai.

I guess i could go a bit deeper here, like how i see things more as seperate realities with their own respective timelines with a probably shared point of origin. But no.
There would be one funny point though, from a discussion we had here in the thread.
If Maya and Akira met before or after the car crash. Maybe now both is true.

Anyway.

Some thoughts i want to add.

I don't even want to dive into the whole timetravel, three Mayas stuff. Doesn't make sense to do so to me.

What i find interesting though is, that Maya always knew so much more.
Maybe she didn't tell Akira because she really didn't want to make Akiras head go boom, but why not Ayane?
She already told her about psycho Ami, so why not about the "Scary Room"?
Or how she very likely knew about what happened during "resets"?

Resets/Reset Puzzles/Happy Events -> RRPHE

There are at least three points in where, very likely Maya, seemed to be aware, at least something, going on during a RRPHE with Akira or parts of the RAS.
I say likely, because it could also have been Ami, but i lean towards Maya because my inner Sherlock tells me thats Maya's waist and tits.

The three situations are:

1:
During an earlier RRPHE there's a girl sitting (in seiza, guess thats a Maya thing) in a dark corner under, i think a desk, in i think Akira's room. You don't see the head or hair, nothing that would ultimately discern Maya from Ami, given their bodies being similar. Just, and i guess you could go back to Sel's waist tier list, that i think Ami's would be thinner and so i settled for Maya.

2:
During the first Ras slumber party, the one where Yumi might have been killed, you see what i think is Maya, very pixaleted though, sitting (in i guess seiza again) in a corner.
And while it's very pixelated, my gut feeling was like: She looks very sad.

3:
During the events (Halloween) where Maya goes pop, where Akira wakes up on the rooftop after, i think "New Times Roman", theres someone sitting on the left, behind a bush?. Ah, don't remember that exactly anymore, but someone was there.
I think that was Maya again, though, this time i'm not sure if it is conscious Maya or just her body, stripped of her conscious.

I think there is a lot to speculate about why she was there and conscious this three times, while everyone else is normally supposed to be in TPose, if there at all.
This all makes me believe that Maya is just one big fat liar, and i'd really like to know why already.

There's another interesting thing to add i guess.
Three times in this update i was like: Ok, Sel is still reading here and incorperates things from here into the story.
I mean he does at least and often to mock people.
Besides, we here and the discord, provide him with genuine ideas through theorycrafting, all for FREEEEEEE

Now, i don't remember what the other two were, but what a coincidence that some time ago this thread was about people (me included) who have shittons of saves.
Though, someone mentioned that Amy, the first time in the mall, mentiones to save there because "This might be important in the future".
Hm, i wonder. I didn't look that up yet if it's really there, and if it is, since when is it?
If it has been there since the coresponding event, that would be one well planned and played i'd say.
Maybe it even feels like cherishing those with lot's of saves, opposite to those that have like only one page and always overwrite them.
I mean, the only way to get the last Happy Event legitly, is to play up to this update and still have a save from back in the mall and load that one and play the new part.

I somehow want to make this quick.
I said i think Maya is a big fat liar.
Ayane is too.
My guess here is, that Sel just gave them to much knowledge and now we have a "knowing characters" vs Sel doesn't want to spill the beans, kind of problem. Like, he wrote himself into a corner.
Ayane pretty much came unaltered, supernatural wise, out of the forest after meeting Himawari. Yet she never told anyone the details. Argh, c'mon.
Then there's also the last "Beach Trip", where Himawari took Ayane somewhere.

What comes to mind is, that there are pivotal characters in the story, that know more then they ever tell anyone.
It feels like they are their own factions, with their own agenda and because of that, they keep important things to themselfes.

I pretty much forgot a couple of nice things, but that just happens. Might come up with'em later.

While this was very interesting, as always, I feel like some of what's been theorized could mainly be explained by the difference in interpretation as to the events presented in 0.45 being real or not. I take them as mostly, if not all, real. So this post will attempt to take that approach to some of the "problems" aramaug has pointed out. For the minor stuff, it could simply be extrapolated from what I'll present.
I definitely agree that it would make more sense for the scary room pictures to involve Sekai, it was something that we both agreed on in the past iirc. But, it was revealed that Ami has kept pictures of other timelines, as the ones found during 0.44. So it wouldn't be Akira keeping the pictures, but Ami. During 0.45, we see confirmation that stuff can be kept safe from resets, and that Maya Prime did it constantly in the form of notes (which is probably what's in the boxes). It also fits with Ayane seeing them and thinking they could help, as they'd be Maya's diaries.

Furthermore, if Maya Prime had issues remembering stuff, that would be a thousand times more the case for Ami, that has been around much longer than Maya Prime, seeing her being factory reset plenty of times, and potentially being around even before Maya existed in the first place. Therefore, these "distortions" to Ami's mind can be safely explained by which memories she has kept (even maybe creating a second personality that lies dormant most of the time that holds said memories in order to protect the active Ami).
Maya hasn't always been real. You focus on the event in the scary room, but a lot of things are shown in the "happy end" timeline that are relevant to it. For one, that's a real thing because our Nodoka is there. Pareidolia sent our Nodoka to the timeline where Akira and Makoto end up, Ami's happy end. Why does he do that? It's in order to further gift Akira with information.

That information is that they should avoid the roof, that Nodoka has to stop researching, and that Ami is a psychopath. Beyond that there is also information in that in Ami's happy end the color is back and more beautiful than ever before (It is said that Maya is the result of Akira stealing a color), and Nodoka says that "she" isn't crazy, but scared. Well, the one she that is acting crazy is either Nodoka or Ami, but I'd think she's talking about Ami. And the one last piece of information is that Nodoka says she has to finish naming her child. Given that the one child to be named is Himawari, and that in the same update there is a reference to it in the form of Alexis, she's probably talking about her.
There's a lot to talk about regarding Nodoka's information, but focusing on what's revelant here: Sekai doesn't act like this is her ending, it's Ami's. This is yet another case of Ami seeing the world as being made for her and Akira, much like that one special Ami event.

Why this is relevant to the case of our Ami "not ever acting in such a way", well, she has. It's just that our Ami differs from this one Ami for the very important reason that Maya didn't yet exist. What she says to Maya in the scary room is that she's very pissed at the fact that Maya, an accident, came in, changed everything, started to behave like she's main girl of her own anime, and Ami can't do shit about it. In the cycles before Maya was a thing, Ami could simply kill whoever got in the way, the world would reset, and she would try yet another version of her happy ending, but all of them were hers without a doubt.

At some point, everything changed, and Maya was conjured by Akira (likely), which put her by default as his chosen one, and Ami would have to play with this random fake best friend that's stealing her place and lying to her. Ami can't behave the way she did before because this isn't her world anymore, she has likely killed Maya many times over and it did nothing, leading to her choosing a different tactic. Even then, by Maya Prime's account and what we see on Akira's sports' fan world, Ami is okay with things as long as Akira is fucking her more or less. "Our" Ami has referenced those better days, however, a couple of times already, including when she talks about the worlds when she and Akira would drive alone through the empty city. This simply wouldn't have been possible if it was a Maya cycle. She's likely referencing her better days, before Maya happened.

In fact, our Ami completely loses it when Maya is finally gone and yet Akira continues not making Ami his chosen one (Maya remains his chosen even if gone) - this also explains why she goes into caretaker mode, being because she recognizes that Maya has been factory reset, and jumps at the opportunity. What we see in the scary room with Ami being sadistic doesn't have to be her being Sekai, but that she's deriving pleasure in proving that Maya is not a main girl. Those are very different intents. Whereas Sekai wouldn't care about something like that, because she knows she wins by default, Ami is ever scared about it. So, in fact, what Ami is trying to do there is "see how you don't really love Akira, anyone can make you cum, you're just a whore", or, in other words, "how dare you try to take my place? you're just a doll" - which is, exactly, the sentiment "our" Ami verbalizes a couple of times, when she asks if they would ever die for Akira, or when she repeatedly states she's the only one for him.

This actually explains a whole lot about our Ami, that being why she behaves the way she does and where her obsession comes from.

Consider for a moment that Ami isn't behaving strangely at all during the entire game, she has lived countless times through realities where only her and Akira were real people. They made their happy ending in each of those until something got in the way or it reset, and they'd do it again. Countless times. Why wouldn't she behave like she's the only one for him? Why wouldn't she consider everyone else a nuisance? Why wouldn't she be okay with it as long as all the others are playing their roles to their happy ending, and start behaving aggresively when they don't?

Our Ami makes perfect sense if you start viewing her through the lens of the "original Maya". In fact, the only reason as to why Maya doesn't behave like this is that she's an accident. Everytime she gets close to Akira, she breaks him. That's what makes it hell for her. But Ami had no such issue. It was pretty much a paradise in search of the perfect world, "found an issue? reload and try again" type of situation. But then came the fucking watermelon girl.
I take Maya not remembering her parents a confirmation that they didn't exist. As I see it, Maya started existing at some point, and that likely changed the timeline causing Sekai to die. I don't mean that in a way in which Maya herself caused Sekai to die, or that they're involved in any way, but that we have some examples of worlds where Sekai exists and there's no Maya.

To me, that's the source of Sekai's hatred for Maya, that Maya's existence overrides her possibility to exist as a living being in the cycles. That also presents an issue in the form of "if Sekai didn't die, but married Akira instead, then what started the cycles?" - because Ami's happy ending is clearly a cycle, Sekai doesn't seem to be aware of it by taking the police into account (even though she accepts it without a problem), so it started at some point. That being said, if Maya didn't exist, how were things before and why did they change?

Akira would have married Sekai, which would have led to him never actually dating Niki (they weren't boyfriend/girlfriend in Kyoto, just almost there), which would have led to Noriko not being in love with him (because she was in love when she was 6, and she'd be a baby by then), which would have also led to Ami never meeting Noriko. Which would have led to our Ami never having memories of Noriko before she showed up in class. Which would make Noriko a second Maya in Ami's view, in the sense of being someone else with a fake history with Akira that didn't ever come to be in the original Ami's timeline. This would also make Ami's knowledge of Niki make more sense, as in her own timeline Akira never dated Niki to begin with, and was instead married to her mom and at most fooled around with the girls in class.

So, in that sense, we have timeline A where Akira marries Sekai, Maya doesn't exist, he never dated Niki, Noriko never fell in love, and where Ami lived for thousands of years making her happy ending. Then we have timeline B, our timeline, where Maya exists, Akira refuses to marry Sekai, he starts dating Niki, Noriko falls in love, Maya takes Akira away, and Ami is ever just the niece instead of the daughter (even though she knows this is all fake).
At the moment it's simply impossible to say whether this interpretation or aramaug's is the correct one. I thought however that it was important to point out that a lot of the issues raised by his interpretation depend on not taking these into account. Especially the notion that these are corrupted memories, instead of actual moments from other timelines. I favor the second interpretation.

To me, the fact that our Nodoka is there, that what we are presented explains so much of our Ami behavior throughout the whole game, that Selebus has rarely presented lore that was untrue (Kyoto might have been the first, if it even is at that), and the sheer amount of time we spent on these revelations to just be misdirection are enough for me to assume these are at most true.

Edit: on a minor note, I also thought that when HOPE (with the number three on his body) says "guess who's back" it was Pareidolia. Also, the fact that he shows up as "HOPE the peerless god of light" aka has a namechange is not lost on me. The one thing against them being a trinity is that Wires is attacked by the corruption after HOPE appears. So at that point they're likely not the same entity.

Individually, none of these points make it impossible that "Right as Rain" shows a real event where Maya was raped by Ami, but each one makes it less and less likely. Instead, I'll tentatively propose a theory that could tie these ideas together:
During the reset Pareidolia and/or Sekai force New Maya to experience nightmares based off of corrupted memories. In the real memory that "Right as Rain" is based on, Maya was still a wizard and was assaulted by Sekai rather than Ami.
In "The Scary Room" Pareidolia showed Maya Prime pictures of that real rape by Sekai.

If she's always been an uncaring sadist with full knowledge of the resets and the ability to force a new world, it devalues all of her old events. Suddenly all of her character development, her vulnerabilities, her relationships with her friends at both their highs and lows, even her tender moments with Sensei would be thrown out the window because it was all just an act. I don't want a story where "Della" was just a calculated ploy, not a young girl's insecurities piling up with a traumatic past, causing her to finally break - a break that causes her to hurt herself, not (intentionally) anyone else. Basically, if this is the real Ami Prime, it will feel like a complex character has been replaced with a plot contrivance.
Furthermore, it felt like this event came out of nowhere. Yes, we've seen evidence that Ami knows more about the resets than she lets on, we've seen evidence of her putting on an act and being a master manipulator, we've even seen evidence that she could go psycho and start murdering (for the record, I still think Ami Prime's psycho threats were just an act and will never be realized - in Himawari we trust). In fact, we've never seen Ami Prime cause intentional physical harm to any other character - her MO is implied threats and psychological manipulation. While this was very interesting, as always, I feel like some of what's been theorized could mainly be explained by the difference in interpretation as to the events presented in 0.45 being real or not. I take them as mostly, if not all, real. So this post will attempt to take that approach to some of the "problems" aramaug has pointed out. For the minor stuff, it could simply be extrapolated from what I'll present.
Spoiler:
Pictures and Diaries
I definitely agree that it would make more sense for the scary room pictures to involve Sekai, it was something that we both agreed on in the past iirc. But, it was revealed that Ami has kept pictures of other timelines, as the ones found during 0.44. So it wouldn't be Akira keeping the pictures, but Ami. During 0.45, we see confirmation that stuff can be kept safe from resets, and that Maya Prime did it constantly in the form of notes (which is probably what's in the boxes). It also fits with Ayane seeing them and thinking they could help, as they'd be Maya's diaries.
Furthermore, if Maya Prime had issues remembering stuff, that would be a thousand times more the case for Ami, that has been around much longer than Maya Prime, seeing her being factory reset plenty of times, and potentially being around even before Maya existed in the first place. Therefore, these "distortions" to Ami's mind can be safely explained by which memories she has kept (even maybe creating a second personality that lies dormant most of the time that holds said memories in order to protect the active Ami).
Spoiler:
Nodoka's sacrifice and Ami's backstory
Maya hasn't always been real. You focus on the event in the scary room, but a lot of things are shown in the "happy end" timeline that are relevant to it. For one, that's a real thing because our Nodoka is there. Pareidolia sent our Nodoka to the timeline where Akira and Makoto end up, Ami's happy end. Why does he do that? It's in order to further gift Akira with information.
That information is that they should avoid the roof, that Nodoka has to stop researching, and that Ami is a psychopath. Beyond that there is also information in that in Ami's happy end the color is back and more beautiful than ever before (It is said that Maya is the result of Akira stealing a color), and Nodoka says that "she" isn't crazy, but scared. Well, the one she that is acting crazy is either Nodoka or Ami, but I'd think she's talking about Ami. And the one last piece of information is that Nodoka says she has to finish naming her child. Given that the one child to be named is Himawari, and that in the same update there is a reference to it in the form of Alexis, she's probably talking about her.
Spoiler:
Nodoka stuff
There's a lot to talk about regarding Nodoka's information, but focusing on what's revelant here: Sekai doesn't act like this is her ending, it's Ami's. This is yet another case of Ami seeing the world as being made for her and Akira, much like that one special Ami event.
Why this is relevant to the case of our Ami "not ever acting in such a way", well, she has. It's just that our Ami differs from this one Ami for the very important reason that Maya didn't yet exist. What she says to Maya in the scary room is that she's very pissed at the fact that Maya, an accident, came in, changed everything, started to behave like she's main girl of her own anime, and Ami can't do shit about it. In the cycles before Maya was a thing, Ami could simply kill whoever got in the way, the world would reset, and she would try yet another version of her happy ending, but all of them were hers without a doubt.
At some point, everything changed, and Maya was conjured by Akira (likely), which put her by default as his chosen one, and Ami would have to play with this random fake best friend that's stealing her place and lying to her. Ami can't behave the way she did before because this isn't her world anymore, she has likely killed Maya many times over and it did nothing, leading to her choosing a different tactic. Even then, by Maya Prime's account and what we see on Akira's sports' fan world, Ami is okay with things as long as Akira is fucking her more or less. "Our" Ami has referenced those better days, however, a couple of times already, including when she talks about the worlds when she and Akira would drive alone through the empty city. This simply wouldn't have been possible if it was a Maya cycle. She's likely referencing her better days, before Maya happened.
In fact, our Ami completely loses it when Maya is finally gone and yet Akira continues not making Ami his chosen one (Maya remains his chosen even if gone) - this also explains why she goes into caretaker mode, being because she recognizes that Maya has been factory reset, and jumps at the opportunity. What we see in the scary room with Ami being sadistic doesn't have to be her being Sekai, but that she's deriving pleasure in proving that Maya is not a main girl. Those are very different intents. Whereas Sekai wouldn't care about something like that, because she knows she wins by default, Ami is ever scared about it. So, in fact, what Ami is trying to do there is "see how you don't really love Akira, anyone can make you cum, you're just a whore", or, in other words, "how dare you try to take my place? you're just a doll" - which is,
exactly
, the sentiment "our" Ami verbalizes a couple of times, when she asks if they would ever die for Akira, or when she repeatedly states she's the only one for him.
This actually explains a whole lot about our Ami, that being why she behaves the way she does and where her obsession comes from.
Consider for a moment that Ami isn't behaving strangely at all during the entire game, she has lived countless times through realities where only her and Akira were real people. They made their happy ending in each of those until something got in the way or it reset, and they'd do it again. Countless times. Why wouldn't she behave like she's the only one for him? Why wouldn't she consider everyone else a nuisance? Why wouldn't she be okay with it as long as all the others are playing their roles to their happy ending, and start behaving aggresively when they don't?
Our Ami makes perfect sense if you start viewing her through the lens of the "original Maya". In fact, the only reason as to why Maya doesn't behave like this is that she's an accident. Everytime she gets close to Akira, she breaks him. That's what makes it hell for her. But Ami had no such issue. It was pretty much a paradise in search of the perfect world, "found an issue? reload and try again" type of situation. But then came the fucking watermelon girl.
Spoiler:
Maya didn't exist
I take Maya not remembering her parents a confirmation that they didn't exist. As I see it, Maya started existing at some point, and that likely changed the timeline causing Sekai to die. I don't mean that in a way in which Maya herself caused Sekai to die, or that they're involved in any way, but that we have some examples of worlds where Sekai exists and there's no Maya.
To me, that's the source of Sekai's hatred for Maya, that Maya's existence overrides her possibility to exist as a living being in the cycles. That also presents an issue in the form of "if Sekai didn't die, but married Akira instead, then what started the cycles?" - because Ami's happy ending is clearly a cycle, Sekai doesn't seem to be aware of it by taking the police into account (even though she accepts it without a problem), so it started at some point. That being said, if Maya didn't exist, how were things before and why did they change?
Akira would have married Sekai, which would have led to him never actually dating Niki (they weren't boyfriend/girlfriend in Kyoto, just almost there), which would have led to Noriko not being in love with him (because she was in love when she was 6, and she'd be a baby by then), which would have also led to Ami never meeting Noriko. Which would have led to our Ami never having memories of Noriko before she showed up in class. Which would make Noriko a second Maya in Ami's view, in the sense of being someone else with a fake history with Akira that didn't ever come to be in the original Ami's timeline. This would also make Ami's knowledge of Niki make more sense, as in her own timeline Akira never dated Niki to begin with, and was instead married to her mom and at most fooled around with the girls in class.
So, in that sense, we have timeline A where Akira marries Sekai, Maya doesn't exist, he never dated Niki, Noriko never fell in love, and where Ami lived for thousands of years making her happy ending. Then we have timeline B, our timeline, where Maya exists, Akira refuses to marry Sekai, he starts dating Niki, Noriko falls in love, Maya takes Akira away, and Ami is ever just the niece instead of the daughter (even though she knows this is all fake).
At the moment it's simply impossible to say whether this interpretation or aramaug's is the correct one. I thought however that it was important to point out that a lot of the issues raised by his interpretation depend on not taking these into account. Especially the notion that these are corrupted memories, instead of actual moments from other timelines. I favor the second interpretation.
To me, the fact that our Nodoka is there, that what we are presented explains so much of our Ami behavior throughout the whole game, that Selebus has rarely presented lore that was untrue (Kyoto might have been the first, if it even is at that), and the sheer amount of time we spent on these revelations to just be misdirection are enough for me to assume these are at most true.
Edit: on a minor note, I also thought that when HOPE (with the number three on his body) says "guess who's back" it was Pareidolia. Also, the fact that he shows up as "HOPE the peerless god of light" aka has a namechange is not lost on me. The one thing against them being a trinity is that Wires is attacked by the corruption
after
HOPE appears. So at that point they're likely not the same entity.

At the end of "Right as Rain" a seemingly new entity shows up as the narrator. They identify themselves as "the ghost of better days" while we're shown a picture of Jesus on the cross. The "better days" ties back to "The Scary Room" where Pareidolia and the angels both use that phrase.
